lessons.title: Numbers in Words and Figures: Reading and Writing Numbers
lessons.notes_html:
Numbers in words and figures

We can write a number in figures using digits, or in words using number names. To change words into figures, break the words into parts such as thousands, hundreds, tens and ones, write each part, and then add the parts together. To change figures into words, read the thousands part first, then the hundreds, tens and ones.

Worked example

Write in figures: Four hundred fifty six thousand and nine hundred twenty six.

Step 1: Four hundred fifty six thousand = 456,000.

Step 2: Nine hundred twenty six = 926.

Step 3: Add the parts: 456,000 + 926 = 456,926.

Answer: 456,926.

Key points

  • Break number words into thousands, hundreds, tens and ones parts.
  • Fill empty places with zero, for example 729,006 has zeros in the hundreds and tens places.
  • Read figures in groups: thousands first, then the last three digits.

mcqs.q: What is four thousand six hundred and ninety two in figures?
mcqs.why: Break the words into parts: four thousand = 4,000, six hundred = 600 and ninety two = 92. Add them: 4,000 + 600 + 92 = 4,692.

mcqs.q: What is sixty nine thousand four hundred and seven in figures?
mcqs.why: Sixty nine thousand = 69,000, four hundred = 400 and seven = 7. Add the parts: 69,000 + 400 + 7 = 69,407.

mcqs.q: What is 2,561 in words?
options: Two thousand five hundred and sixty
Two thousand five hundred and sixteen
Two thousand five hundred and sixty one
mcqs.why: Split 2,561 into 2 thousand and 561. Read 2,000 as two thousand and 561 as five hundred and sixty one, so the full name is two thousand five hundred and sixty one.

mcqs.q: What is 92,000 in words?
mcqs.why: In 92,000 the digits 92 stand in the thousands part and the last three places are zero, so we read only ninety two thousand and nothing after it.

mcqs.q: What is seven hundred twenty nine thousand and six in figures?
mcqs.why: Seven hundred twenty nine thousand = 729,000 and six = 6. Add: 729,000 + 6 = 729,006. The empty hundreds and tens places are filled with zeros.

mcqs.q: What is 34,561 in words?
options: Thirty four thousand five hundred and sixty
Thirty four thousand five hundred and sixty one
Three hundred forty five thousand sixty one
mcqs.why: Split 34,561 into 34 thousand and 561. Read 34,000 as thirty four thousand and 561 as five hundred and sixty one, giving thirty four thousand five hundred and sixty one.

mcqs.q: What is nine hundred two thousand and forty two in figures?
mcqs.why: Nine hundred two thousand = 902,000 and forty two = 42. Add the parts: 902,000 + 42 = 902,042. A zero fills the empty hundreds place.

mcqs.q: What is 245,612 in words?
options: Two hundred forty five thousand six hundred twenty
Two hundred and forty five thousand six hundred and two
Two hundred and forty five thousand six hundred and twelve
Twenty four thousand five hundred and sixty two
mcqs.why: Split 245,612 into 245 thousand and 612. Read 245,000 as two hundred and forty five thousand and 612 as six hundred and twelve, so the name is two hundred and forty five thousand six hundred and twelve.

mcqs.q: What is seven hundred thousand in figures?
mcqs.why: Seven hundred thousand means 700 thousands. Write 700 followed by three zeros for the last three places: 700 x 1,000 = 700,000.

mcqs.q: What is 56,081 in words?
options: Fifty six thousand eight hundred and one
Fifty six thousand eight hundred eighty one
Five hundred sixty thousand eighty one
mcqs.why: Split 56,081 into 56 thousand and 081. The hundreds place is zero so we skip it: fifty six thousand, then eighty one from the tens and ones places.

lessons.title: Place Value and Value: What Each Digit Stands For
lessons.notes_html:
Place value and value

The place value of a digit is the place where it stands, such as ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands, millions, ten millions and hundred millions. The value of a digit is the digit multiplied by its place, for example a 5 in the millions place has value 5 x 1,000,000 = 5,000,000.

Worked example

Find the place value and value of the digit 2 in 12,345,678.

Step 1: Count the places from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands, millions.

Step 2: The digit 2 stands in the millions place.

Step 3: Value = 2 x 1,000,000 = 2,000,000.

Answer: The digit 2 is in the millions place and its value is 2,000,000.

Key points

  • Always count places from the right, starting at the ones place.
  • Value = digit x place, so the same digit has different values in different places.
  • A zero in any place has value zero, but it holds the other digits in their correct places.

mcqs.q: What is the value of the digit 2 in 12,345,678?
mcqs.why: Count from the right: the digit 2 stands in the millions place. Value = 2 x 1,000,000 = 2,000,000.

mcqs.q: What is the value of the digit 8 in 58,923,107?
mcqs.why: Count from the right: ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, hundred thousands, millions. The 8 is in the millions place, so its value is 8 x 1,000,000 = 8,000,000.

mcqs.q: What is the value of the digit 1 in 100,000,000?
mcqs.why: The digit 1 stands in the hundred millions place, the ninth place from the right. Value = 1 x 100,000,000 = 100,000,000.

mcqs.q: What is the value of the digit 9 in 23,964,579?
mcqs.why: Count from the right: the digit 9 stands in the hundred thousands place. Value = 9 x 100,000 = 900,000.

mcqs.q: In 9,234,513, what is the value of the digit 3 in the ten thousands place?
mcqs.why: The number 9,234,513 has 3 in the ten thousands place and another 3 in the ones place. For the ten thousands place: 3 x 10,000 = 30,000.

mcqs.q: What is the value of the digit 5 in 50,120,306?
mcqs.why: Count from the right: the digit 5 is the eighth digit, standing in the ten millions place. Value = 5 x 10,000,000 = 50,000,000.

mcqs.q: What is the value of the digit 8 in 3,567,899?
mcqs.why: In 3,567,899 the places from the right are ones 9, tens 9, hundreds 8. So 8 is in the hundreds place and its value is 8 x 100 = 800.

mcqs.q: What is the value of the digit 7 in 76,905,851?
mcqs.why: The digit 7 is the first digit of the eight digit number 76,905,851, so it stands in the ten millions place. Value = 7 x 10,000,000 = 70,000,000.

mcqs.q: In 25,960,238, what is the value of the digit 2 in the hundreds place?
mcqs.why: The last three digits of 25,960,238 are 238, so 2 stands in the hundreds place. Value = 2 x 100 = 200. The 5 in the same number is worth 5,000,000, which is a different digit.

mcqs.q: What is the value of the digit 6 in the millions place in 36,564,396?
mcqs.why: In 36,564,396 the digits are 3 in ten millions and 6 in millions. Value of the millions digit = 6 x 1,000,000 = 6,000,000.

lessons.title: Numbers up to Millions: Reading Big Numbers
lessons.notes_html:
Numbers up to millions

Big numbers are read in groups: the millions group, the thousands group and the last three digits. Read each group like a small number and then say its group name, for example 4,312,687 is four million three hundred and twelve thousand six hundred and eighty seven. One million is 1,000,000, ten million is 10,000,000 and one hundred million is 100,000,000.

Worked example

Write 4,312,687 in words.

Step 1: Group the digits: 4 in the millions group, 312 in the thousands group and 687 as the last three digits.

Step 2: Read each group in order: four million, three hundred and twelve thousand, six hundred and eighty seven.

Answer: Four million three hundred and twelve thousand six hundred and eighty seven.

Key points

  • Commas separate the groups of three digits from the right.
  • When a group is zero, skip its name, for example 50,001,000 is fifty million one thousand.
  • In a counting pattern, find the gap between neighbours and add it each time.

mcqs.q: What is 5,000,000 in words?
mcqs.why: Group 5,000,000 as 5 in the millions group with both other groups zero. Zero groups are skipped, so we read only five million.

mcqs.q: What is two million, ninety thousand and sixty eight in figures?
mcqs.why: Two million = 2,000,000, ninety thousand = 90,000 and sixty eight = 68. Add: 2,000,000 + 90,000 + 68 = 2,090,068, with zeros filling the empty places.

mcqs.q: What is twenty million and twenty in figures?
mcqs.why: Twenty million = 20,000,000 and twenty = 20. Add: 20,000,000 + 20 = 20,000,020. All the thousands and hundreds places stay zero.

mcqs.q: What number comes just after 2,000,019 when counting up to two million twenty?
mcqs.why: Counting adds 1 each time: 2,000,019 + 1 = 2,000,020, which is the last number in the count from two million to two million twenty.

mcqs.q: In the pattern 2,450,761, 2,451,761, 2,452,761, what is the next number?
In the pattern 7,000,300, 7,000,400, 7,000,500, what is the next number?
What is 50,001,000 in words?
mcqs.why: Group 50,001,000 as 50 million, 001 thousand and 000. Read the groups in order and skip the zero group: fifty million one thousand.

mcqs.q: What is ninety million and sixty seven thousand in figures?
mcqs.why: Ninety million = 90,000,000 and sixty seven thousand = 67,000. Add: 90,000,000 + 67,000 = 90,067,000. The last three places stay zero.

mcqs.q: How is 22,233,341 split into ten millions and millions?
mcqs.why: Read the first two digits of 22,233,341: the 2 on the left is in the ten millions place and the next 2 is in the millions place, so the split is 2 ten millions and 2 millions, with 233,341 left over.

mcqs.q: What is 241,935 in words?
options: Two hundred and forty one thousand nine hundred and thirty five
Twenty four thousand nine hundred and thirty five
Two hundred and fourteen thousand nine hundred and thirty five
Two million four hundred thousand nine hundred and thirty five
mcqs.why: Group 241,935 as 241 thousand and 935. Read 241 as two hundred and forty one, say thousand, then read 935 as nine hundred and thirty five.

lessons.title: Comparing and Ordering Numbers: Bigger, Smaller and In Order
lessons.notes_html:
Comparing and ordering numbers

To compare two numbers, first count the digits: the number with more digits is bigger. If both numbers have the same number of digits, compare place by place from the left until the digits differ; the number with the bigger digit in that place is bigger. Ascending order means smallest to biggest and descending order means biggest to smallest.

Worked example

Compare 92,333,444 and 92,315,617: which is bigger?

Step 1: Both numbers have 8 digits, so compare from the leftmost place.

Step 2: The digits agree until the ten thousands place, where 92,333,444 has 3 and 92,315,617 has 1.

Step 3: 3 is bigger than 1, so the number with 3 in this place is bigger.

Answer: 92,333,444 is bigger than 92,315,617.

Key points

  • More digits always means a bigger number.
  • With equal digits, compare from the left and stop at the first place where the digits differ.
  • Ascending order starts with the smallest number; descending order starts with the biggest.

mcqs.q: Which number is bigger: 52,001,000 or 345,912?
mcqs.why: Count the digits: 52,001,000 has 8 digits and 345,912 has only 6 digits. The number with more digits is bigger, so 52,001,000 is bigger.

mcqs.q: Which number is smaller: 2,456,123 or 24,345,611?
mcqs.why: Count the digits: 2,456,123 has 7 digits and 24,345,611 has 8 digits. Fewer digits means a smaller number, so 2,456,123 is smaller.

mcqs.q: Which number is bigger: 7,123,400 or 8,567,001?
mcqs.why: Both numbers have 7 digits. Compare from the left: in the millions place 7,123,400 has 7 and 8,567,001 has 8. Since 8 is bigger than 7, 8,567,001 is bigger.

mcqs.q: Which number is bigger: 92,333,444 or 92,315,617?
mcqs.why: Both have 8 digits and agree until the ten thousands place, where 92,333,444 has 3 and 92,315,617 has 1. Since 3 is bigger than 1, 92,333,444 is bigger.

mcqs.q: Which number is smaller: 24,000,008 or 24,000,005?
mcqs.why: Both have 8 digits and agree until the ones place, where 24,000,008 has 8 and 24,000,005 has 5. Since 5 is less than 8, 24,000,005 is smaller.

mcqs.q: Which number comes first in ascending order: 3,174,215, 3,741,512 or 3,076,005?
mcqs.why: Ascending order starts with the smallest. All have 7 digits; comparing from the left, 3,076,005 has 0 in the hundred thousands place while the others have 1 and 7, so 3,076,005 is smallest and comes first.

mcqs.q: Which number comes first in descending order: 95,123,415, 95,312,415 or 95,113,417?
mcqs.why: Descending order starts with the biggest. Comparing from the left, the numbers agree until the hundred thousands place: 95,312,415 has 3 there, more than 2 and 1 in the others, so 95,312,415 is biggest and comes first.
All have 8 digits and start with 5 in the ten millions place. In the millions place they have 9, 9, 2 and 8. The smallest digit there is 2, so 52,111,222 is the smallest number.

All have 8 digits. Two start with 14 million and two with 13 million, so the biggest is one of the 14 million numbers. Between 14,111,920 and 14,160,000, the hundred thousands digits are 1 and 6, so 14,160,000 is biggest.

Compare place by place from the left: the 13 million numbers come before the 14 million numbers, and within each pair the smaller hundred thousands digit comes first. Smallest to biggest: 13,100,219, 13,200,415, 14,111,920, 14,160,000.

lessons.title: Addition: Adding Big Numbers in Columns
lessons.notes_html:
Addition in columns

To add big numbers, write them in vertical form with ones under ones and tens under tens. Add one column at a time from the right. When a column total is 10 or more, write the ones digit and carry the tens digit to the next column.

Worked example

Add 92,345 + 50,178.

Step 1: Ones: 5 + 8 = 13; write 3 and carry 1.

Step 2: Tens: 4 + 7 + 1 carried = 12; write 2 and carry 1.

Step 3: Hundreds: 3 + 1 + 1 carried = 5; write 5.

Step 4: Thousands: 2 + 0 = 2; write 2. Ten thousands: 9 + 5 = 14; write 4 and carry 1, then write the carried 1.

Answer: 92,345 + 50,178 = 142,523.

Key points

  • Keep digits in straight columns by place value.
  • Never forget to add the carried digit in the next column.
  • Adding two numbers less than a million can give an answer over a million.

mcqs.why: Add column by column: ones 1 + 5 = 6, tens 3 + 4 = 7, hundreds 4 + 2 = 6, thousands 5 + 1 = 6, ten thousands 2 + 4 = 6. The sum is 66,676.

Ones 6 + 7 = 13, write 3 carry 1. Tens 3 + 1 + 1 = 5. Hundreds 2 + 0 = 2. Thousands 7 + 8 = 15, write 5 carry 1. Ten thousands 0 + 9 + 1 = 10, write 0 carry 1. Hundred thousands 1 + 2 + 1 = 4. Sum = 405,253.
Ones 5 + 8 = 13, write 3 carry 1. Tens 4 + 7 + 1 = 12, write 2 carry 1. Hundreds 3 + 1 + 1 = 5. Thousands 2 + 0 = 2. Ten thousands 9 + 5 = 14, write 4 and carry 1 into a new column. Sum = 142,523.

Ones 9 + 8 = 17, write 7 carry 1. Tens 2 + 4 + 1 = 7. Hundreds 6 + 5 = 11, write 1 carry 1. Thousands 9 + 1 + 1 = 11, write 1 carry 1. Ten thousands 4 + 0 + 1 = 5. Hundred thousands 3 + 2 = 5. Sum = 551,177.
Ones 7 + 5 = 12, write 2 carry 1. Tens 1 + 3 + 1 = 5. Hundreds 3 + 2 = 5. Thousands 4 + 0 = 4. Ten thousands 2 + 9 = 11, write 1 and carry 1 into a new column. Sum = 114,552.

Ones 9 + 2 = 11, write 1 carry 1. Tens 9 + 8 + 1 = 18, write 8 carry 1. Hundreds 9 + 9 + 1 = 19, write 9 carry 1. Thousands 7 + 9 + 1 = 17, write 7 carry 1. Ten thousands 6 + 4 + 1 = 11, write 1 carry 1. Hundred thousands 0 + 2 + 1 = 3. Sum = 317,981.

Ones 2 + 4 = 6, tens 1 + 3 = 4, hundreds 6 + 3 = 9, thousands 2 + 2 = 4. Ten thousands 9 + 2 = 11, write 1 carry 1. Hundred thousands 3 + 7 + 1 = 11, write 1 and carry 1 into a new column. Sum = 1,114,946.

Ones 6 + 6 = 12, write 2 carry 1. Tens 6 + 9 + 1 = 16, write 6 carry 1. Hundreds 5 + 8 + 1 = 14, write 4 carry 1. Thousands 5 + 8 + 1 = 14, write 4 carry 1. Ten thousands 5 + 7 + 1 = 13, write 3 carry 1. Hundred thousands 5 + 7 + 1 = 13, write 3 carry 1. Sum = 1,334,462.
Ones 2 + 3 = 5, tens 5 + 2 = 7, hundreds 0 + 2 = 2, thousands 0 + 1 = 1, ten thousands 1 + 8 = 9. Hundred thousands 9 + 8 = 17, write 7 and carry 1 into a new column. Sum = 1,791,275.

Ones 5 + 6 = 11, write 1 carry 1. Tens 5 + 1 + 1 = 7. Hundreds 5 + 0 = 5. Thousands 9 + 2 = 11, write 1 carry 1. Ten thousands 9 + 1 + 1 = 11, write 1 carry 1. Hundred thousands 9 + 3 + 1 = 13, write 3 carry 1. Sum = 1,311,571.

lessons.title: Addition Word Problems: Finding Totals in Real Life
lessons.notes_html:
Addition word problems

When a word problem asks for a total, a combined amount or how much altogether, we add the given numbers. Read the problem, pick out the two amounts, write them in columns and add carefully with carrying.

Worked example

The Government of Sindh spent Rs 581,034 on one road and Rs 347,083 on another road. How much is it in total?

Step 1: Total means add: 581,034 + 347,083.

Step 2: Ones 4 + 3 = 7. Tens 3 + 8 = 11, write 1 and carry 1. Hundreds 0 + 0 + 1 = 1. Thousands 1 + 7 = 8.

Step 3: Ten thousands 8 + 4 = 12, write 2 and carry 1. Hundred thousands 5 + 3 + 1 = 9.

Answer: The total amount spent is Rs 928,117.

Key points

  • Words like total, altogether and in all point to addition.
  • Keep the unit in the answer, such as Rs, kg or people.
  • Add in columns and do not forget the carried digits.

mcqs.q: In an examination, 27,514 girls and 20,328 boys appeared. How many students appeared in total?
mcqs.why: Total means add: 27,514 + 20,328. Ones 4 + 8 = 12, write 2 carry 1. Tens 1 + 2 + 1 = 4. Hundreds 5 + 3 = 8. Thousands 7 + 0 = 7. Ten thousands 2 + 2 = 4. Total = 47,842 students.

mcqs.q: The Government of Sindh spent Rs 581,034 on one road and Rs 347,083 on another road. How much was spent in total?
mcqs.why: Add the two amounts: 581,034 + 347,083. Ones 4 + 3 = 7. Tens 3 + 8 = 11, write 1 carry 1. Hundreds 0 + 0 + 1 = 1. Thousands 1 + 7 = 8. Ten thousands 8 + 4 = 12, write 2 carry 1. Hundred thousands 5 + 3 + 1 = 9. Total = Rs 928,117.

mcqs.q: One company makes 865,271 bicycles in a year and another company makes 725,059 bicycles. How many bicycles do they make in total?
mcqs.why: Add: 865,271 + 725,059. Ones 1 + 9 = 10, write 0 carry 1. Tens 7 + 5 + 1 = 13, write 3 carry 1. Hundreds 2 + 0 + 1 = 3. Thousands 5 + 5 = 10, write 0 carry 1. Ten thousands 6 + 2 + 1 = 9. Hundred thousands 8 + 7 = 15. Total = 1,590,330 bicycles.

mcqs.q: Bismah spent Rs 857,600 on computers and Aleesha spent Rs 641,200. How much did they spend in total?
mcqs.why: Add: 857,600 + 641,200. Ones, tens are 0. Hundreds 6 + 2 = 8. Thousands 7 + 1 = 8. Ten thousands 5 + 4 = 9. Hundred thousands 8 + 6 = 14, write 4 and carry 1 into a new column. Total = Rs 1,498,800.

mcqs.q: A match at Karachi was watched by 55,384 people and a match at Lahore by 43,298 people. How many people watched in total?
mcqs.why: Add: 55,384 + 43,298. Ones 4 + 8 = 12, write 2 carry 1. Tens 8 + 9 + 1 = 18, write 8 carry 1. Hundreds 3 + 2 + 1 = 6. Thousands 5 + 3 = 8. Ten thousands 5 + 4 = 9. Total = 98,682 people.

mcqs.q: Pakistan Railways carried 347,180 kg of mangoes in the first week and 449,130 kg in the next week. How many kg were carried in total?
mcqs.why: Add: 347,180 + 449,130. Ones 0. Tens 8 + 3 = 11, write 1 carry 1. Hundreds 1 + 1 + 1 = 3. Thousands 7 + 9 = 16, write 6 carry 1. Ten thousands 4 + 4 + 1 = 9. Hundred thousands 3 + 4 = 7. Total = 796,310 kg.

mcqs.q: A road cost Rs 581,034 and a computer project cost Rs 449,130. What is the total cost?
mcqs.why: Add the two costs from this unit: 581,034 + 449,130. Ones 4 + 0 = 4. Tens 3 + 3 = 6. Hundreds 0 + 1 = 1. Thousands 1 + 9 = 10, write 0 carry 1. Ten thousands 8 + 4 + 1 = 13, write 3 carry 1. Hundred thousands 5 + 4 + 1 = 10. Total = Rs 1,030,164.

mcqs.q: One group has 55,384 people and another group has 27,514 people. How many people are there in total?
mcqs.why: Add: 55,384 + 27,514. Ones 4 + 4 = 8. Tens 8 + 1 = 9. Hundreds 3 + 5 = 8. Thousands 5 + 7 = 12, write 2 carry 1. Ten thousands 5 + 2 + 1 = 8. Total = 82,898 people.

mcqs.q: A hall holds 20,328 boys and then 43,298 more people come in. How many people are there now?
mcqs.why: Add: 20,328 + 43,298. Ones 8 + 8 = 16, write 6 carry 1. Tens 2 + 9 + 1 = 12, write 2 carry 1. Hundreds 3 + 2 + 1 = 6. Thousands 0 + 3 = 3. Ten thousands 2 + 4 = 6. Total = 63,626 people.

mcqs.q: Aleesha spent Rs 641,200 and the first road cost Rs 581,034. What is the total of these two amounts?
mcqs.why: Add: 641,200 + 581,034. Ones 0 + 4 = 4. Tens 0 + 3 = 3. Hundreds 2 + 0 = 2. Thousands 1 + 1 = 2. Ten thousands 4 + 8 = 12, write 2 carry 1. Hundred thousands 6 + 5 + 1 = 12. Total = Rs 1,222,234.

lessons.title: Subtraction: Taking Away with Borrowing
lessons.notes_html:
Subtraction in columns

To subtract, write the bigger number on top and the smaller number below it in columns, then subtract from the right. When the top digit is smaller than the bottom digit, borrow 1 from the next column: the top digit grows by 10 and the next top digit falls by 1.

Worked example

Subtract: 583,729 - 21,678.

Step 1: Ones: 9 - 8 = 1.

Step 2: Tens: borrow so the top digit becomes 12; 12 - 7 = 5. Hundreds: after borrowing the top digit becomes 6; 6 - 6 = 0.

Step 3: Thousands: 3 - 1 = 2. Ten thousands: 8 - 2 = 6. Hundred thousands: 5 - 0 = 5.

Answer: 583,729 - 21,678 = 562,051.

Key points

  • The bigger number always goes on top.
  • After borrowing, the lending digit becomes 1 less.
  • Subtracting a number from an equal round number like 100,000 needs borrowing across all the zeros.

mcqs.why: Subtract column by column: ones 4 - 3 = 1, tens 6 - 5 = 1, hundreds 1 - 0 = 1, thousands 2 - 0 = 2, ten thousands 3 - 2 = 1. Answer = 12,111. No borrowing is needed.
Ones 8 - 8 = 0, tens 4 - 2 = 2, hundreds 9 - 3 = 6, thousands 7 - 6 = 1, ten thousands 2 - 1 = 1, hundred thousands 6 - 0 = 6. Answer = 611,620.
Ones 9 - 8 = 1. Tens: borrow, 12 - 7 = 5. Hundreds: after borrowing, 6 - 6 = 0. Thousands 3 - 1 = 2. Ten thousands 8 - 2 = 6. Hundred thousands 5 - 0 = 5. Answer = 562,051.

Ones: borrow, 14 - 5 = 9. Tens: after borrowing, 4 - 3 = 1. Hundreds 8 - 0 = 8. Thousands: borrow, 13 - 5 = 8. Ten thousands: after borrowing, 8 - 8 = 0. Hundred thousands 7 - 1 = 6. Answer = 608,819.
Ones 5 - 0 = 5, tens 6 - 1 = 5, hundreds 7 - 2 = 5, thousands 8 - 3 = 5, ten thousands 9 - 4 = 5. Every column gives 5, so the answer is 55,555.
Borrow across the zeros: ones become 10 - 9 = 1, and every other column becomes 9 - 9 = 0, with the hundred thousands digit becoming 0. Answer = 1.
Borrow across the zeros: ones 10 - 4 = 6, tens 9 - 6 = 3, hundreds 9 - 8 = 1, thousands 9 - 7 = 2, ten thousands 9 - 3 = 6, hundred thousands 6 - 5 = 1. Answer = 162,136.

Ones: borrow, 10 - 1 = 9. Tens: after borrowing, 9 - 0 = 9. Hundreds: after borrowing, 9 - 0 = 9. Thousands: after borrowing, 0 - 0 = 0. Ten thousands 9 - 9 = 0 and hundred thousands 9 - 9 = 0. Answer = 999.
Ones, tens, hundreds, thousands and ten thousands columns are all equal digits, so each gives 0. Only the hundred thousands column differs: 9 - 8 = 1. Answer = 100,000.

Ones: borrow, 12 - 4 = 8. Tens: after borrowing, 9 - 9 = 0. Hundreds: after borrowing, 9 - 9 = 0. Thousands: borrow, 12 - 3 = 9. Ten thousands: after borrowing, 13 - 9 = 4. Hundred thousands: after borrowing, 8 - 4 = 4. Answer = 449,008.

lessons.title: Subtraction Word Problems: Finding What Is Left
lessons.notes_html:
Subtraction word problems

When a problem gives a total and one part, or asks how many are left, how many more or what the difference is, we subtract the smaller number from the bigger number. Write the bigger number on top and borrow carefully where needed.

Worked example

The government spent Rs 985,000 on two schools in total. Rs 539,450 were spent on one school. How much was spent on the other school?

Step 1: Subtract one school amount from the total: 985,000 - 539,450.

Step 2: Ones 0 - 0 = 0. Tens: borrow, 10 - 5 = 5. Hundreds: after borrowing, 9 - 4 = 5.

Step 3: Thousands: borrow, 14 - 9 = 5. Ten thousands: after borrowing, 7 - 3 = 4. Hundred thousands 9 - 5 = 4.

Answer: Rs 445,550 were spent on the other school.

Key points

  • Total minus one part gives the other part.
  • Words like left, more and difference point to subtraction.
  • Always subtract the smaller number from the bigger number.

mcqs.q: 57,986 students appeared in an examination and 43,985 passed. How many students did not pass?
mcqs.why: Did not pass means subtract: 57,986 - 43,985. Ones 6 - 5 = 1, tens 8 - 8 = 0, hundreds 9 - 9 = 0, thousands 7 - 3 = 4, ten thousands 5 - 4 = 1. Answer = 14,001 students.

mcqs.q: The government spent Rs 985,000 on two schools in total and Rs 539,450 on one school. How much was spent on the other school?
mcqs.why: Subtract one part from the total: 985,000 - 539,450. Ones 0. Tens: borrow, 10 - 5 = 5. Hundreds: 9 - 4 = 5. Thousands: borrow, 14 - 9 = 5. Ten thousands: 7 - 3 = 4. Hundred thousands 9 - 5 = 4. Answer = Rs 445,550.

mcqs.q: Aslam and Atif together invested Rs 658,700. Aslam share is Rs 385,780. What is Atif share?
mcqs.why: Subtract Aslam share from the total: 658,700 - 385,780. Ones 0. Tens: borrow, 10 - 8 = 2. Hundreds: borrow, 16 - 7 = 9. Thousands: 7 - 5 = 2 after borrowing. Ten thousands: borrow, 15 - 8 = 7. Hundred thousands: 5 - 3 = 2. Answer = Rs 272,920.

mcqs.q: A cotton company profit for two months is Rs 320,000. One month profit is Rs 139,998. What is the other month profit?
mcqs.why: Subtract: 320,000 - 139,998. Ones: borrow, 10 - 8 = 2. Tens: 9 - 9 = 0. Hundreds: 9 - 9 = 0. Thousands: 9 - 9 = 0. Ten thousands: borrow, 11 - 3 = 8. Hundred thousands: 2 - 1 = 1. Answer = Rs 180,002.

mcqs.q: On Eid days, 3,955 people visited the zoo on the first day and 3,843 on the second day. How many more people came on the first day?
mcqs.why: More means find the difference: 3,955 - 3,843. Ones 5 - 3 = 2, tens 5 - 4 = 1, hundreds 9 - 8 = 1, thousands 3 - 3 = 0. Answer = 112 more people.

mcqs.q: A poultry farm had 89,534 hens and 43,294 hens died. How many hens were left?
mcqs.why: Left means subtract: 89,534 - 43,294. Ones 4 - 4 = 0. Tens: borrow, 13 - 9 = 4. Hundreds: after borrowing, 4 - 2 = 2. Thousands 9 - 3 = 6. Ten thousands 8 - 4 = 4. Answer = 46,240 hens.

mcqs.q: A total of Rs 985,000 is shared so that one part is Rs 385,780. What is the other part?
mcqs.why: Subtract the known part from the total using numbers from this unit: 985,000 - 385,780. Ones 0. Tens: borrow, 10 - 8 = 2. Hundreds: 9 - 7 = 2 after borrowing. Thousands: borrow, 14 - 5 = 9. Ten thousands: 7 - 8 needs a borrow, 17 - 8 = 9. Hundred thousands: 8 - 3 = 5. Answer = Rs 599,220.

mcqs.q: A farm store had 57,986 bags and 43,294 bags were sold. How many bags are left?
mcqs.why: Left means subtract: 57,986 - 43,294. Ones 6 - 4 = 2, tens 8 - 9 needs a borrow so 18 - 9 = 9, hundreds 8 - 2 = 6 after borrowing, thousands 7 - 3 = 4, ten thousands 5 - 4 = 1. Answer = 14,692 bags.

mcqs.q: A profit total is Rs 658,700 and one month profit is Rs 139,998. What is the remaining profit?
mcqs.why: Subtract: 658,700 - 139,998. Ones: borrow, 10 - 8 = 2. Tens: 9 - 9 = 0. Hundreds: 6 - 9 needs a borrow, 16 - 9 = 7. Thousands: 7 - 9 needs a borrow, 17 - 9 = 8. Ten thousands: 4 - 3 = 1 after borrowing. Hundred thousands 6 - 1 = 5. Answer = Rs 518,702.

mcqs.q: A farm had 89,534 hens and 43,985 hens were sold. How many hens remain?
mcqs.why: Subtract: 89,534 - 43,985. Ones: borrow, 14 - 5 = 9. Tens: 2 - 8 needs a borrow, 12 - 8 = 4. Hundreds: 4 - 9 needs a borrow, 14 - 9 = 5. Thousands: 8 - 3 = 5 after borrowing. Ten thousands 8 - 4 = 4. Answer = 45,549 hens.

lessons.title: Multiplication: Multiplying by Two and Three Digits
lessons.notes_html:
Multiplication with partial products

To multiply by a two or three digit number, break the multiplier into ones, tens and hundreds parts. Multiply by each part to get partial products, remembering that multiplying by the tens part gives an answer ten times bigger and by the hundreds part one hundred times bigger. Then add all the partial products.

Worked example

Multiply 1,632 x 23.

Step 1: Break 23 into 3 + 20.

Step 2: Multiply by the ones: 1,632 x 3 = 4,896.

Step 3: Multiply by the tens: 1,632 x 2 = 3,264, then x 10 gives 32,640.

Step 4: Add the partial products: 4,896 + 32,640 = 37,536.

Answer: 1,632 x 23 = 37,536.

Key points

  • Break the multiplier into ones, tens and hundreds first.
  • Multiply by 100 by writing two zeros at the end.
  • Add all partial products carefully at the end.

mcqs.q: What is 1,632 x 23?
mcqs.why: Break 23 into 3 + 20. Ones part: 1,632 x 3 = 4,896. Tens part: 1,632 x 2 = 3,264, then x 10 = 32,640. Add the partial products: 4,896 + 32,640 = 37,536.

mcqs.q: What is 6,314 x 52?
What is 2,341 x 70?
What is 2,109 x 84?
What is 11,689 x 100?
mcqs.why: Multiplying by 100 makes the number one hundred times bigger: 11,689 x 1 = 11,689, then x 100 means write two zeros at the end, giving 1,168,900.

mcqs.q: What is 12,345 x 123?
What is 21,499 x 120?
What is 41,078 x 203?
mcqs.why: Break 203 into 3 + 200; the tens part is zero so there are only two parts. Ones part: 41,078 x 3 = 123,234. Hundreds part: 41,078 x 2 = 82,156, then x 100 = 8,215,600. Add: 123,234 + 8,215,600 = 8,338,834.

mcqs.q: What is 32,145 x 152?
What is 25,701 x 553?

lessons.title: Multiplication Word Problems: Groups and Totals
lessons.notes_html:
Multiplication word problems

When every group, truck, day or person has the same amount, we multiply to find the total: amount in one group x number of groups. Break the multiplier into parts, find the partial products and add them.

Worked example

One truck carries 5,324 bottles. How many bottles can be carried in 132 trucks?

Step 1: Multiply 5,324 x 132. Break 132 into 2 + 30 + 100.

Step 2: 5,324 x 2 = 10,648. 5,324 x 3 = 15,972, then x 10 gives 159,720. 5,324 x 1 = 5,324, then x 100 gives 532,400.

Step 3: Add the partial products: 10,648 + 159,720 + 532,400 = 702,768.

Answer: 702,768 bottles can be carried in 132 trucks.

Key points

  • Same amount repeated many times means multiply.
  • One amount x number of groups gives the total.
  • Write the unit, such as bottles, eggs or litres, in the answer.

mcqs.q: A school has 630 students and each student pays a monthly fee of Rs 1,200. How much fee is collected in a month?
One truck carries 5,324 bottles. How many bottles can be carried in 132 trucks?
A poultry farm produces 43,290 eggs in one day. How many eggs are produced in 400 days?
The price of one motorcycle is Rs 35,800. What is the price of 325 motorcycles?
One family spends Rs 15,980 on food in a month. How much do 580 such families spend?
A town uses 45,038 litres of water in one week. How much water is used in 890 weeks?
One truck carries 5,324 bottles. How many bottles can be carried in 100 trucks?
mcqs.why: Multiply 5,324 x 100: multiplying by 100 means writing two zeros at the end of 5,324, which gives 532,400 bottles.

mcqs.q: A poultry farm produces 43,290 eggs in one day. How many eggs are produced in 132 days?
A town uses 45,038 litres of water in one week. How much water is used in 400 weeks?
The price of one motorcycle is Rs 35,800. What is the price of 132 motorcycles?

lessons.title: Division: Sharing and Finding Quotients
lessons.notes_html:
Division step by step

Division shares a number into equal parts. The number being shared is the dividend, the number we divide by is the divisor, the answer is the quotient and anything left over is the remainder. Divide digit by digit from the left: at each step multiply, subtract and bring down the next digit.

Worked example

Divide 6,744 by 12.

Step 1: 67 / 12: 12 x 5 = 60; remainder 67 - 60 = 7.

Step 2: Bring down 4 to make 74. 74 / 12: 12 x 6 = 72; remainder 74 - 72 = 2.

Step 3: Bring down 4 to make 24. 24 / 12: 12 x 2 = 24; remainder 0.

Answer: 6,744 / 12 = 562.

Key points

  • Work from the left, one digit at a time.
  • The remainder must always be smaller than the divisor.
  • Check a division by multiplying the quotient by the divisor.

mcqs.q: What is 6,744 / 12?
mcqs.why: Divide step by step: 67 / 12 gives 5 since 12 x 5 = 60, remainder 7. Bring down 4: 74 / 12 gives 6 since 12 x 6 = 72, remainder 2. Bring down 4: 24 / 12 = 2 exactly. Quotient = 562.

mcqs.q: What is 7,293 / 13?
mcqs.why: Divide step by step: 72 / 13 gives 5 since 13 x 5 = 65, remainder 7. Bring down 9: 79 / 13 gives 6 since 13 x 6 = 78, remainder 1. Bring down 3: 13 / 13 = 1 exactly. Quotient = 561.

mcqs.q: What is 3,795 / 15?
mcqs.why: Divide step by step: 37 / 15 gives 2 since 15 x 2 = 30, remainder 7. Bring down 9: 79 / 15 gives 5 since 15 x 5 = 75, remainder 4. Bring down 5: 45 / 15 = 3 exactly. Quotient = 253.

mcqs.q: What is 9,384 / 12?
mcqs.why: Divide step by step: 93 / 12 gives 7 since 12 x 7 = 84, remainder 9. Bring down 8: 98 / 12 gives 8 since 12 x 8 = 96, remainder 2. Bring down 4: 24 / 12 = 2 exactly. Quotient = 782.

mcqs.q: What is 2,214 / 18?
mcqs.why: Divide step by step: 22 / 18 gives 1 since 18 x 1 = 18, remainder 4. Bring down 1: 41 / 18 gives 2 since 18 x 2 = 36, remainder 5. Bring down 4: 54 / 18 = 3 exactly. Quotient = 123.

mcqs.q: What is 9,944 / 22?
mcqs.why: Divide step by step: 99 / 22 gives 4 since 22 x 4 = 88, remainder 11. Bring down 4: 114 / 22 gives 5 since 22 x 5 = 110, remainder 4. Bring down 4: 44 / 22 = 2 exactly. Quotient = 452.

mcqs.q: What is 4,368 / 28?
mcqs.why: Divide step by step: 43 / 28 gives 1 since 28 x 1 = 28, remainder 15. Bring down 6: 156 / 28 gives 5 since 28 x 5 = 140, remainder 16. Bring down 8: 168 / 28 = 6 exactly. Quotient = 156.

mcqs.q: What is 6,300 / 25?
mcqs.why: Divide step by step: 63 / 25 gives 2 since 25 x 2 = 50, remainder 13. Bring down 0: 130 / 25 gives 5 since 25 x 5 = 125, remainder 5. Bring down 0: 50 / 25 = 2 exactly. Quotient = 252.

mcqs.q: When 31,035 is divided by 12, what are the quotient and remainder?
mcqs.why: Divide step by step: 31 / 12 = 2 remainder 7; 70 / 12 = 5 remainder 10; 103 / 12 = 8 remainder 7; 75 / 12 = 6 remainder 3. Check: 12 x 2,586 = 31,032 and 31,032 + 3 = 31,035. Quotient 2,586, remainder 3.

mcqs.q: When 9,267 is divided by 15, what are the quotient and remainder?
mcqs.why: Divide step by step: 92 / 15 = 6 remainder 2 since 15 x 6 = 90; 26 / 15 = 1 remainder 11; 117 / 15 = 7 remainder 12 since 15 x 7 = 105. Check: 15 x 617 = 9,255 and 9,255 + 12 = 9,267. Quotient 617, remainder 12.

lessons.title: Division Word Problems: One Share at a Time
lessons.notes_html:
Division word problems

When a total is shared equally, or we ask how many equal groups fit into a total, we divide: total / size of one share = number of shares, and total / number of shares = size of one share.

Worked example

A piece of cloth is 6,272 metres long. One suit needs 7 metres of cloth. How many suits can be made?

Step 1: Divide the total cloth by the cloth for one suit: 6,272 / 7.

Step 2: 62 / 7 = 8 remainder 6, since 7 x 8 = 56. Bring down 7: 67 / 7 = 9 remainder 4, since 7 x 9 = 63.

Step 3: Bring down 2: 42 / 7 = 6 exactly.

Answer: 896 suits can be made.

Key points

  • Equal sharing and equal groups both mean division.
  • Price of one item = total price / number of items.
  • Number of groups = total / size of one group.

mcqs.q: The monthly salary of 12 workers together is Rs 7,032 and all get the same salary. What is the salary of one worker?
mcqs.why: Divide the total by the number of workers: 7,032 / 12. Steps: 70 / 12 = 5 remainder 10; 103 / 12 = 8 remainder 7; 72 / 12 = 6 exactly. One worker gets Rs 586.

mcqs.q: A piece of cloth is 6,272 metres long and one suit needs 7 metres. How many suits can be made?
mcqs.why: Divide: 6,272 / 7. Steps: 62 / 7 = 8 remainder 6; 67 / 7 = 9 remainder 4; 42 / 7 = 6 exactly. So 896 suits can be made.

mcqs.q: Asif spent Rs 2,925 to buy 13 shirts of the same price. What is the price of each shirt?
mcqs.why: Divide: 2,925 / 13. Steps: 29 / 13 = 2 remainder 3; 32 / 13 = 2 remainder 6; 65 / 13 = 5 exactly. Each shirt costs Rs 225.

mcqs.q: The weight of 16 sacks of flour is 4,496 kg and all sacks weigh the same. What is the weight of one sack?
mcqs.why: Divide: 4,496 / 16. Steps: 44 / 16 = 2 remainder 12; 129 / 16 = 8 remainder 1; 16 / 16 = 1 exactly. One sack weighs 281 kg.

mcqs.q: The price of 25 cricket bats is Rs 3,075. What is the price of one bat?
mcqs.why: Divide: 3,075 / 25. Steps: 30 / 25 = 1 remainder 5; 57 / 25 = 2 remainder 7; 75 / 25 = 3 exactly. One bat costs Rs 123.

mcqs.q: One crate holds 36 bottles. There are 5,616 bottles in all. How many crates are required?
mcqs.why: Divide the total bottles by the bottles in one crate: 5,616 / 36. Steps: 56 / 36 = 1 remainder 20; 201 / 36 = 5 remainder 21; 216 / 36 = 6 exactly. So 156 crates are required.

mcqs.q: There are 5,616 bottles in all and one crate holds 12 bottles. How many crates are required?
mcqs.why: Divide using numbers from this unit: 5,616 / 12. Steps: 56 / 12 = 4 remainder 8; 81 / 12 = 6 remainder 9; 96 / 12 = 8 exactly. So 468 crates are required.

mcqs.q: Asif spent Rs 2,925 to buy 25 shirts of the same price. What is the price of each shirt?
mcqs.why: Divide: 2,925 / 25. Steps: 29 / 25 = 1 remainder 4; 42 / 25 = 1 remainder 17; 175 / 25 = 7 exactly. Each shirt costs Rs 117.

mcqs.q: A cloth piece of 6,272 metres is cut into pieces of 16 metres each. How many pieces are made?
mcqs.why: Divide: 6,272 / 16. Steps: 62 / 16 = 3 remainder 14; 147 / 16 = 9 remainder 3; 32 / 16 = 2 exactly. So 392 pieces are made.

mcqs.q: There are 5,616 bottles in all and one crate holds 16 bottles. How many crates are required?
mcqs.why: Divide: 5,616 / 16. Steps: 56 / 16 = 3 remainder 8; 81 / 16 = 5 remainder 1; 16 / 16 = 1 exactly. So 351 crates are required.

lessons.title: Mixed Operations: Which Operation First
lessons.notes_html:
Mixed operations

When an expression has only addition and subtraction, work from left to right. When it has only multiplication and division, also work from left to right. When operations are mixed, do multiplication and division first, then addition and subtraction.

Worked example

Solve: 12 x 114 / 19 + 10.

Step 1: Multiplication and division come before addition, so first work out 12 x 114 / 19 from left to right.

Step 2: 12 x 114 = 1,368.

Step 3: 1,368 / 19 = 72.

Step 4: Now add: 72 + 10 = 82.

Answer: 12 x 114 / 19 + 10 = 82.

Key points

  • Addition and subtraction together: go left to right.
  • Multiplication and division together: go left to right.
  • In a mixed expression, multiplication and division are done before addition and subtraction.

mcqs.q: What is 46 - 23 + 17?
mcqs.why: Only addition and subtraction are here, so work from left to right. First 46 - 23 = 23. Then 23 + 17 = 40.

mcqs.q: What is 98 - 46 + 24?
mcqs.why: Only addition and subtraction are here, so work from left to right. First 98 - 46 = 52. Then 52 + 24 = 76.

mcqs.q: What is 99 - 77 + 33?
mcqs.why: Only addition and subtraction are here, so work from left to right. First 99 - 77 = 22. Then 22 + 33 = 55.
Only addition and subtraction are here, so work from left to right. First 324 - 152 = 172. Then 172 + 182 = 354.
Only addition and subtraction are here, so work from left to right. First 682 + 329 = 1,011. Then 1,011 - 159 = 852.

mcqs.q: What is 253 / 11 x 5?
mcqs.why: Only division and multiplication are here, so work from left to right. First 253 / 11 = 23. Then 23 x 5 = 115.

mcqs.q: What is 540 / 15 x 8?
mcqs.why: Only division and multiplication are here, so work from left to right. First 540 / 15 = 36. Then 36 x 8 = 288.

mcqs.q: What is 7 x 375 / 15?
mcqs.why: Only multiplication and division are here, so work from left to right. First 7 x 375 = 2,625. Then 2,625 / 15 = 175.
Division and multiplication are done before addition. First 800 / 20 = 40. Then 40 x 2 = 80. Then 23 + 80 = 103.
Division and multiplication are done before addition. First 32 x 400 = 12,800. Then 12,800 / 16 = 800. Then 800 + 23 = 823.

lessons.title: Mixed Word Problems: Choosing the Right Operation
lessons.notes_html:
Mixed word problems

Word problems can need any of the four operations. Ask yourself what the problem wants: a total means add, left or difference means subtract, the same amount in many groups means multiply, and equal sharing means divide. Then solve in columns or with partial products, step by step.

Worked example

One car costs Rs 748,630 and another car costs Rs 630,010. What is the total cost of both?

Step 1: Total means add: 748,630 + 630,010.

Step 2: Ones 0, tens 3 + 1 = 4, hundreds 6 + 0 = 6, thousands 8 + 0 = 8, ten thousands 4 + 3 = 7.

Step 3: Hundred thousands 7 + 6 = 13, write 3 and carry 1, then write the carried 1.

Answer: The total cost of both cars is Rs 1,378,640.

Key points

  • Choose the operation from the meaning of the problem before calculating.
  • Total and altogether: add. Left and difference: subtract.
  • Equal groups: multiply. Equal sharing: divide.

mcqs.q: Shagufta had Rs 389,000 in the bank. She spent Rs 183,499 on house repair. How much money is left with her?
mcqs.why: Left means subtract: 389,000 - 183,499. Ones: borrow, 10 - 9 = 1. Tens: 9 - 9 = 0. Hundreds: 9 - 4 = 5. Thousands: borrow, 8 - 3 = 5. Ten thousands 8 - 8 = 0. Hundred thousands 3 - 1 = 2. Answer = Rs 205,501.

mcqs.q: One car costs Rs 748,630 and another car costs Rs 630,010. What is the total cost of both cars?
mcqs.why: Total means add: 748,630 + 630,010. Ones 0, tens 3 + 1 = 4, hundreds 6, thousands 8, ten thousands 4 + 3 = 7, hundred thousands 7 + 6 = 13, write 3 and carry 1 into a new column. Total = Rs 1,378,640.

mcqs.q: The cost of one TV is Rs 95,400. What is the cost of 150 TVs?
A poultry farm sold 143,860 chickens in one month and 354,180 in the next month. What is the difference in sale?
mcqs.why: Difference means subtract the smaller from the bigger: 354,180 - 143,860. Ones 0, tens 8 - 6 = 2, hundreds: borrow, 11 - 8 = 3, thousands: 3 - 3 = 0 after borrowing, ten thousands 5 - 4 = 1, hundred thousands 3 - 1 = 2. Difference = 210,320 chickens.

mcqs.q: A school spent Rs 4,375 on a picnic and only 35 students went. How much did each student pay?
mcqs.why: Each student share means divide: 4,375 / 35. Steps: 43 / 35 = 1 remainder 8; 87 / 35 = 2 remainder 17; 175 / 35 = 5 exactly. Each student paid Rs 125.

mcqs.q: Najeeb is distributing 3,290 food packs among 235 families. How many packs does each family get?
mcqs.why: Divide: 3,290 / 235. Steps: 329 / 235 = 1 remainder 94, since 235 x 1 = 235. Bring down 0: 940 / 235 = 4 exactly, since 235 x 4 = 940. Each family gets 14 packs.

mcqs.q: One farm contains 56,321 date trees. How many trees are there in 835 such farms?
One car costs Rs 748,630 and another car costs Rs 630,010. How much more does the first car cost?
mcqs.why: More means find the difference: 748,630 - 630,010. Ones 0, tens 3 - 1 = 2, hundreds 6 - 0 = 6, thousands 8 - 0 = 8, ten thousands 4 - 3 = 1, hundred thousands 7 - 6 = 1. Difference = Rs 118,620.

mcqs.q: The cost of one TV is Rs 95,400. What is the cost of 35 TVs?
A school spent Rs 4,375 on a picnic and 25 students went. How much did each student pay?
mcqs.why: Divide: 4,375 / 25. Steps: 43 / 25 = 1 remainder 18; 187 / 25 = 7 remainder 12, since 25 x 7 = 175; 125 / 25 = 5 exactly. Each student paid Rs 175.

lessons.title: Review Exercise 1: Mixed Practice
lessons.notes_html:
Review of Unit 1

This review mixes everything from Unit 1: reading and writing numbers up to hundred millions, place value, addition, subtraction, multiplication, division and mixed operations. Remember that a seven digit number is in the millions, and in mixed operations multiplication and division are done before addition and subtraction.

Worked example

Add 416,712 and 712,145.

Step 1: Ones 2 + 5 = 7. Tens 1 + 4 = 5. Hundreds 7 + 1 = 8.

Step 2: Thousands 6 + 2 = 8. Ten thousands 1 + 1 = 2.

Step 3: Hundred thousands 4 + 7 = 11, write 1 and carry 1, then write the carried 1.

Answer: 416,712 + 712,145 = 1,128,857.

Key points

  • The place value of a digit is the digit multiplied by its place.
  • Seven digit numbers represent millions.
  • Check every answer by working carefully column by column.

mcqs.q: What is the place value of 8 in 2,485,612?
mcqs.why: Count the places from the right in 2,485,612: ones 2, tens 1, hundreds 6, thousands 5, ten thousands 8. So 8 is in the ten thousands place and its value is 8 x 10,000 = 80,000.

mcqs.q: Seven digit numbers represent which group?
mcqs.why: Count the digits: a number like 4,312,687 has seven digits and is read as four million and so on, so seven digit numbers represent millions. Ten millions needs eight digits.

mcqs.q: What is 20 + 8 / 4?
mcqs.why: Division is done before addition. First 8 / 4 = 2. Then 20 + 2 = 22. Adding first would give 28 / 4 = 7, which is the common mistake.

mcqs.q: What is 2,412,316 in words?
options: Two million four hundred and twelve thousand three hundred and sixteen
Two million four hundred and twenty thousand three hundred and sixteen
Twenty four million twelve thousand three hundred and sixteen
Two million four hundred and twelve thousand three hundred and sixty
mcqs.why: Group 2,412,316 as 2 million, 412 thousand and 316. Read each group in order: two million four hundred and twelve thousand three hundred and sixteen.

mcqs.q: What is twenty million in figures?
mcqs.why: Twenty million means 20 millions: 20 x 1,000,000 = 20,000,000. It has eight digits, with 20 in the millions group and zeros in all other places.
Add in columns: ones 2 + 5 = 7, tens 1 + 4 = 5, hundreds 7 + 1 = 8, thousands 6 + 2 = 8, ten thousands 1 + 1 = 2, hundred thousands 4 + 7 = 11, write 1 and carry 1 into a new column. Sum = 1,128,857.
Subtract in columns: ones 9 - 2 = 7, tens 2 - 2 = 0, hundreds 8 - 8 = 0, thousands: borrow, 17 - 8 = 9, ten thousands: 5 - 1 = 4 after borrowing, hundred thousands 9 - 2 = 7. Answer = 749,007.

mcqs.q: What is 3,810 / 15?
mcqs.why: Divide step by step: 38 / 15 = 2 remainder 8, since 15 x 2 = 30. Bring down 1: 81 / 15 = 5 remainder 6, since 15 x 5 = 75. Bring down 0: 60 / 15 = 4 exactly. Quotient = 254.

mcqs.q: What is 600,216 in words?
options: Six hundred thousand two hundred and sixty
Sixty thousand two hundred and sixteen
Six hundred thousand two hundred and sixteen
Six million two hundred and sixteen
mcqs.why: Group 600,216 as 600 thousand and 216. Read 600 as six hundred, say thousand, then read 216 as two hundred and sixteen: six hundred thousand two hundred and sixteen.

mcqs.q: The annual saving of Raheel is Rs 89,560. He purchases a TV for Rs 35,000. How much money is left with him?
mcqs.why: Left means subtract: 89,560 - 35,000. Ones 0, tens 6 - 0 = 6, hundreds 5 - 0 = 5, thousands 9 - 5 = 4, ten thousands 8 - 3 = 5. Answer = Rs 54,560.

lessons.title: Exercise 2.1: Divisibility by 2, 3, 5 and 10
lessons.notes_html:
Divisibility rules for 2, 3, 5 and 10

A number is divisible by another number if it divides exactly with no remainder. A number is divisible by 2 if its last digit is even. A number is divisible by 3 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 3. A number is divisible by 5 if its last digit is 0 or 5. A number is divisible by 10 if its last digit is 0.

Worked example

Check the divisibility of 15,381 by 2, 3, 5 and 10.

Step 1: Test for 2: the last digit is 1, which is odd, so 15,381 is NOT divisible by 2.

Step 2: Test for 3: the sum of the digits is 1 + 5 + 3 + 8 + 1 = 18. 18 is divisible by 3, so 15,381 is divisible by 3. Check: 15,381 / 3 = 5,127.

Step 3: Test for 5: the last digit is neither 0 nor 5, so it is NOT divisible by 5.

Step 4: Test for 10: the last digit is not 0, so it is NOT divisible by 10.

Answer: 15,381 is divisible by 3 only.

Key points

  • For 2, 5 and 10, look only at the last digit.
  • For 3, add all the digits and test the sum.
  • Every number divisible by 10 is also divisible by 2 and 5.

mcqs.q: Which number is divisible by 2?
mcqs.why: Check the last digits: 1,001 ends in 1 (odd), 1,434 ends in 4 (even), 2,221 ends in 1 (odd) and 34,329 ends in 9 (odd). Only 1,434 ends in an even digit, and 1,434 / 2 = 717 exactly.

mcqs.q: What is the sum of the digits of 1,471?
mcqs.why: Add the digits one by one: 1 + 4 = 5, 5 + 7 = 12, 12 + 1 = 13. The digit sum is 13, and since 13 is not divisible by 3, 1,471 is not divisible by 3.

mcqs.q: Is 2,100 divisible by 3?
options: Yes, because the digit sum 2 + 1 + 0 + 0 = 3 is divisible by 3
No, because the digit sum is 3 and 3 is too small
mcqs.why: For 3 we add the digits: 2 + 1 + 0 + 0 = 3. 3 is divisible by 3 (3 / 3 = 1), so 2,100 is divisible by 3. The last digit is used for 2, 5 and 10, not for 3.

mcqs.q: Which number is divisible by 5?
mcqs.why: A number is divisible by 5 only when its last digit is 0 or 5. The last digits here are 2, 1, 5 and 4. Only 6,035 ends in 5, and 6,035 / 5 = 1,207 exactly.

mcqs.q: Which number is NOT divisible by 5?
mcqs.why: Check each last digit: 1,235 ends in 5, 6,035 ends in 5 and 53,550 ends in 0, so all three are divisible by 5. 5,552 ends in 2, which is neither 0 nor 5, so 5,552 is not divisible by 5.

mcqs.q: Which number is divisible by 10?
mcqs.why: Divisibility by 10 needs the last digit to be 0. The numbers 2,225, 13,575 and 12,345 all end in 5, so they fail. 1,350 ends in 0, and 1,350 / 10 = 135 exactly.

mcqs.q: Is 2,145 divisible by both 5 and 10?
options: Yes, it is divisible by both 5 and 10
No, it is divisible by 5 only
No, it is divisible by 10 only
No, it is divisible by neither 5 nor 10
mcqs.why: The last digit of 2,145 is 5, so it passes the test for 5 (2,145 / 5 = 429). The test for 10 needs a last digit of 0, and 5 is not 0, so 2,145 is divisible by 5 only, not by both.

mcqs.q: 405 is divisible by which of these?
mcqs.why: The last digit of 405 is 5, so it is odd and fails 2 and 10, but passes 5. The digit sum is 4 + 0 + 5 = 9, and 9 is divisible by 3, so it passes 3 as well. So 405 is divisible by 3 and 5 only.

mcqs.q: 2,340 is divisible by which of these?
mcqs.why: The last digit is 0, so 2,340 passes the tests for 2, 5 and 10 at once. The digit sum is 2 + 3 + 4 + 0 = 9, and 9 is divisible by 3, so it also passes the test for 3. It is divisible by 2, 3, 5 and 10.

mcqs.q: 15,381 is divisible by which of these?
mcqs.why: The last digit is 1, which is odd and is neither 0 nor 5, so 15,381 fails the tests for 2, 5 and 10. The digit sum is 1 + 5 + 3 + 8 + 1 = 18, and 18 is divisible by 3, so it passes for 3 only. Check: 15,381 / 3 = 5,127.

lessons.title: Exercise 2.2: Prime and Composite Numbers
lessons.notes_html:
Prime and composite numbers

A prime number has exactly two factors: 1 and the number itself. A composite number has more than two factors. The number 1 has only one factor, so 1 is neither prime nor composite. To test a number, first write down all its factors and then count them.

Worked example

Is 63 a prime number?

Step 1: Find the factors of 63: 63 = 1 x 63, 63 = 3 x 21 and 63 = 7 x 9, so the factors are 1, 3, 7, 9, 21, 63.

Step 2: Count the factors: 63 has 6 factors in total, which is more than two.

Answer: 63 is a composite number.

Key points

  • Exactly two factors means prime; more than two factors means composite.
  • 1 is neither prime nor composite because it has only one factor.
  • The prime numbers between 1 and 20 are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17 and 19.

mcqs.q: Which statement about 41 is correct?
options: 41 is composite because it has 4 factors
41 is prime because its only factors are 1 and 41
41 is composite because it is odd
mcqs.why: Divide 41 by the numbers from 1 upwards: only 41 = 1 x 41 divides exactly, so the factors of 41 are 1 and 41. Exactly two factors means 41 is a prime number.

mcqs.q: What are all the factors of 63?
mcqs.why: Use the pairs: 63 = 1 x 63, 63 = 3 x 21 and 63 = 7 x 9. Collecting every number from these pairs gives 1, 3, 7, 9, 21, 63, which is six factors, so 63 is composite.

mcqs.q: Is 51 a prime number?
options: Yes, because it has exactly two factors
No, because 51 = 3 x 17, so its factors are 1, 3, 17, 51
Yes, because 51 is an odd number
No, because 51 is an even number
mcqs.why: The digit sum of 51 is 5 + 1 = 6, so 51 is divisible by 3: 51 / 3 = 17. Its factors are 1, 3, 17 and 51, which is four factors, more than two, so 51 is composite, not prime.

mcqs.q: What kind of number is 1?
mcqs.why: The only factor of 1 is 1 itself, so 1 has just one factor. A prime number needs exactly two factors and a composite number needs more than two, so 1 is neither prime nor composite.

mcqs.q: Which of these numbers between 41 and 60 is prime?
mcqs.why: 42 is even so it is composite, 49 = 7 x 7 so it is composite, and 57 = 3 x 19 so it is composite. The factors of 53 are only 1 and 53, exactly two factors, so 53 is prime.

mcqs.q: How many factors does 81 have?
mcqs.why: Use the pairs: 81 = 1 x 81, 81 = 3 x 27 and 81 = 9 x 9. The factors are 1, 3, 9, 27 and 81. Counting them gives 5 factors, so 81 is a composite number.

mcqs.q: How many prime numbers are there between 1 and 20?
mcqs.why: Testing every number from 2 to 20, the ones with exactly two factors are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17 and 19. Counting this list gives 8 prime numbers between 1 and 20.

mcqs.q: Which of these numbers is composite?
mcqs.why: 71, 163 and 23 each have only two factors (1 and the number itself), so they are prime. The factors of 100 are 1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20, 25, 50, 100, which is 9 factors, more than two, so 100 is composite.

mcqs.q: Why is 119 a composite number?
options: Because 119 = 7 x 17, so its factors are 1, 7, 17, 119
mcqs.why: 119 divides exactly by 7: 119 / 7 = 17. So the factor pairs are 119 = 1 x 119 and 119 = 7 x 17, giving the factors 1, 7, 17 and 119. Four factors is more than two, so 119 is composite.

mcqs.q: Which number between 10 and 30 is composite?
mcqs.why: 11, 13 and 29 each have exactly two factors, so they are prime. For 27 the pairs are 27 = 1 x 27 and 27 = 3 x 9, giving factors 1, 3, 9 and 27, which is more than two, so 27 is composite.

lessons.title: Exercise 2.3: Multiples and Factors
lessons.notes_html:
Multiples and factors

A multiple of a number is found by multiplying it by 1, 2, 3 and so on. A factor of a number divides it exactly with no remainder. To find all the factors, divide the number by every number starting from 1 and note the exact divisions.

Worked example

Write down all the factors of 45.

Step 1: Divide 45 by every number starting from 1 and note the exact divisions.

Step 2: Exact divisions: 45 = 1 x 45, 45 = 3 x 15 and 45 = 5 x 9.

Answer: The factors of 45 are 1, 3, 5, 9, 15 and 45.

Key points

  • The first twelve multiples of 4 are 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36, 40, 44 and 48.
  • Every number is a factor and also a multiple of itself.
  • Factors come in pairs that multiply to give the number.

mcqs.q: What is the 7th multiple of 4?
mcqs.why: Multiply 4 by 1 to 7: 4 x 1 = 4, 4 x 2 = 8, 4 x 3 = 12, 4 x 4 = 16, 4 x 5 = 20, 4 x 6 = 24 and 4 x 7 = 28. The 7th multiple in the list 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28 is 28.

mcqs.q: Which of these numbers is a multiple of 7?
mcqs.why: Divide each number by 7: 24 / 7 = 3 remainder 3, 45 / 7 = 6 remainder 3, 56 / 7 = 8 exactly with no remainder, and 62 / 7 = 8 remainder 6. Only 56 divides exactly, so 56 is a multiple of 7.

mcqs.q: What are all the factors of 16?
mcqs.why: Use the pairs: 16 = 1 x 16, 16 = 2 x 8 and 16 = 4 x 4. Collecting every number from these pairs gives 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16. The lists missing 4 or 8 are incomplete.

mcqs.q: What are all the factors of 26?
mcqs.why: Use the pairs: 26 = 1 x 26 and 26 = 2 x 13. No other division is exact, so collecting both pairs gives the full factor list 1, 2, 13 and 26.

mcqs.q: What is the 9th multiple of 9?
mcqs.why: The multiples of 9 are 9 x 1 = 9, 9 x 2 = 18, 9 x 3 = 27, 9 x 4 = 36, 9 x 5 = 45, 9 x 6 = 54, 9 x 7 = 63, 9 x 8 = 72 and 9 x 9 = 81. Counting to the 9th multiple gives 81.

mcqs.q: What is the smallest multiple of 8 that is greater than 20?
mcqs.why: The multiples of 8 are 8, 16, 24, 32, 40 and so on. 16 is less than 20, so it does not count. The first multiple in the list that is greater than 20 is 24, since 8 x 3 = 24.

mcqs.q: What are all the factors of 45?
mcqs.why: Use the pairs: 45 = 1 x 45, 45 = 3 x 15 and 45 = 5 x 9. Collecting every number from all three pairs gives 1, 3, 5, 9, 15 and 45. Any shorter list has missed one of the pairs.

mcqs.q: Which of these numbers is NOT a multiple of 7?
mcqs.why: Divide each by 7: 14 / 7 = 2 exactly, 28 / 7 = 4 exactly and 35 / 7 = 5 exactly, so all three are multiples of 7. But 69 / 7 = 9 remainder 6, which is not exact, so 69 is not a multiple of 7.

mcqs.q: What is the 12th multiple of 7?
mcqs.why: The multiples of 7 end with 7 x 10 = 70, 7 x 11 = 77 and 7 x 12 = 84. Counting through the full list 7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42, 49, 56, 63, 70, 77, 84, the 12th multiple is 84.

mcqs.q: What are all the factors of 50?
mcqs.why: Use the pairs: 50 = 1 x 50, 50 = 2 x 25 and 50 = 5 x 10. Collecting every number from these pairs gives 1, 2, 5, 10, 25 and 50, which is the complete factor list.

lessons.title: Exercise 2.4: Prime Factorization
lessons.notes_html:
Prime factorization

Prime factorization means writing a number as a product of prime numbers only. In the factor tree method, keep splitting the number into two factors until every branch ends in a prime number. In the division method, keep dividing by the smallest prime number until the answer is 1.

Worked example

Factorize 36 using the factor tree method.

Step 1: Start with 36 and split it as 36 = 6 x 6.

Step 2: Split each 6: 6 = 2 x 3 and 6 = 2 x 3. Both 2 and 3 are prime, so the tree stops.

Step 3: Collect all the prime factors from the ends of the branches.

Answer: 36 = 2 x 2 x 3 x 3.

Key points

  • 1 is never written in a prime factorization because 1 is not prime.
  • Check your answer by multiplying the prime factors back together.
  • Among the factors of 20, which are 1, 2, 4, 5, 10 and 20, the prime factors are 2 and 5.

mcqs.q: Which factors of 12 are prime factors?
mcqs.why: All the factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12, from 12 = 1 x 12, 12 = 2 x 6 and 12 = 3 x 4. Among them, only 2 and 3 have exactly two factors each, so the prime factors of 12 are 2 and 3.

mcqs.q: What is the prime factorization of 54 by the factor tree method?
mcqs.why: Split 54 = 2 x 27, then split 27 = 3 x 9, then split 9 = 3 x 3. Collecting the primes gives 54 = 2 x 3 x 3 x 3. Check: 2 x 3 x 3 x 3 = 54, which is correct.

mcqs.q: What is the prime factorization of 27?
mcqs.why: Split 27 = 3 x 9, then split 9 = 3 x 3. Every end number is now prime, so 27 = 3 x 3 x 3. The answer 3 x 9 is not finished because 9 is composite and must be split further.

mcqs.q: Using the division method, what is the prime factorization of 45?
mcqs.why: Divide step by step: 45 / 3 = 15, then 15 / 3 = 5, then 5 / 5 = 1. The divisors used are 3, 3 and 5, so 45 = 3 x 3 x 5. Check: 3 x 3 x 5 = 45.

mcqs.q: Using the division method, what is the prime factorization of 72?
mcqs.why: Divide step by step: 72 / 2 = 36, 36 / 2 = 18, 18 / 2 = 9, 9 / 3 = 3 and 3 / 3 = 1. The divisors are 2, 2, 2, 3 and 3, so 72 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 3 x 3. Check: 8 x 9 = 72.

mcqs.q: What is the prime factorization of 38?
mcqs.why: Divide by the smallest prime: 38 / 2 = 19, then 19 / 19 = 1. Both 2 and 19 are prime, so the factorization stops: 38 = 2 x 19. Check: 2 x 19 = 38.

mcqs.q: What is the prime factorization of 90?
mcqs.why: Divide step by step: 90 / 2 = 45, 45 / 3 = 15, 15 / 3 = 5 and 5 / 5 = 1. The divisors are 2, 3, 3 and 5, so 90 = 2 x 3 x 3 x 5. Check: 2 x 9 x 5 = 90.

mcqs.q: The factors of 64 are 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 and 64. Which of them is a prime factor?
mcqs.why: A prime factor must itself be a prime number with exactly two factors. In the list, 4, 8, 16, 32 and 64 are all composite and 1 is not prime. Only 2 is prime, and indeed 64 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 x 2.

mcqs.q: What is the prime factorization of 32 by the factor tree method?
mcqs.why: Split 32 = 2 x 16, then 16 = 2 x 8, then 8 = 2 x 4, then 4 = 2 x 2. Counting the prime ends gives five 2s: 32 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 x 2. Check: 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 = 32.

mcqs.q: What is the prime factorization of 82?
mcqs.why: Split 82 = 2 x 41. Now check 41: its only factors are 1 and 41, so 41 is prime and the tree stops. So 82 = 2 x 41. Check: 2 x 41 = 82.

lessons.title: Exercise 2.5: Highest Common Factor (HCF)
lessons.notes_html:
Highest Common Factor

A common factor is a factor that appears in the factor lists of two or more numbers. The Highest Common Factor (HCF) is the greatest of the common factors. One method is to list all the factors and pick the greatest common one, as shown in a Venn diagram. Another method is prime factorization: multiply only the prime factors that are common to all the numbers.

Worked example

Find the HCF of 36 and 42 by the Prime Factorization Method.

Step 1: Prime factors of 36: 36 = 2 x 2 x 3 x 3.

Step 2: Prime factors of 42: 42 = 2 x 3 x 7.

Step 3: Take the common prime factors: one 2 and one 3 are common, so 2 x 3 = 6.

Answer: HCF = 6.

Key points

  • For HCF by prime factorization, take each common prime the smallest number of times it appears.
  • The HCF can never be greater than the smallest number in the question.
  • In a Venn diagram, the common factors go in the overlapping middle part, and the greatest one is the HCF.

mcqs.q: What are the common factors of 12 and 18?
mcqs.why: Factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12 and factors of 18 are 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18. The numbers appearing in both lists are 1, 2, 3 and 6, so these are the common factors, and the greatest of them is 6.

mcqs.q: What is the HCF of 36 and 42?
mcqs.why: Prime factorize: 36 = 2 x 2 x 3 x 3 and 42 = 2 x 3 x 7. The common prime factors are one 2 and one 3, so HCF = 2 x 3 = 6. The 7 is not in 36, so it cannot be part of the HCF.

mcqs.q: What is the HCF of 28 and 42?
mcqs.why: Prime factorize: 28 = 2 x 2 x 7 and 42 = 2 x 3 x 7. The common prime factors are one 2 and one 7, so HCF = 2 x 7 = 14. Check: 28 / 14 = 2 and 42 / 14 = 3, both exact.

mcqs.q: What is the HCF of 45 and 75?
mcqs.why: Prime factorize: 45 = 3 x 3 x 5 and 75 = 3 x 5 x 5. The common prime factors are one 3 and one 5, so HCF = 3 x 5 = 15. Check: 45 / 15 = 3 and 75 / 15 = 5, both exact.

mcqs.q: What is the HCF of 25 and 75?
mcqs.why: Prime factorize: 25 = 5 x 5 and 75 = 3 x 5 x 5. Both numbers share two 5s, so HCF = 5 x 5 = 25. Check: 25 / 25 = 1 and 75 / 25 = 3, both exact, and 25 itself is a factor of 75.

mcqs.q: What is the HCF of 60 and 90?
mcqs.why: Prime factorize: 60 = 2 x 2 x 3 x 5 and 90 = 2 x 3 x 3 x 5. The common prime factors are one 2, one 3 and one 5, so HCF = 2 x 3 x 5 = 30. Check: 60 / 30 = 2 and 90 / 30 = 3.

mcqs.q: Using a Venn diagram of factors, what is the HCF of 24 and 36?
mcqs.why: Factors of 24 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24 and factors of 36 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36. The overlapping middle part holds 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12, and the greatest number in the middle is 12, so HCF = 12.

mcqs.q: Using a Venn diagram of factors, what is the HCF of 63 and 54?
mcqs.why: Factors of 63 are 1, 3, 7, 9, 21, 63 and factors of 54 are 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18, 27, 54. The common factors in the middle are 1, 3 and 9, and the greatest of these is 9, so HCF = 9.

mcqs.q: What is the HCF of 14, 21 and 49?
mcqs.why: Factors of 14 are 1, 2, 7, 14; factors of 21 are 1, 3, 7, 21; factors of 49 are 1, 7, 49. The only factors in all three lists are 1 and 7, and the greatest is 7, so HCF = 7.

mcqs.q: What is the HCF of 25, 40 and 50?
mcqs.why: Prime factorize: 25 = 5 x 5, 40 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 5 and 50 = 2 x 5 x 5. The only prime factor common to all three numbers is a single 5, so HCF = 5. Check: 25 / 5 = 5, 40 / 5 = 8 and 50 / 5 = 10.

lessons.title: Exercise 2.6: HCF Word Problems
lessons.notes_html:
HCF in real-life problems

Use the HCF when things must be shared or cut equally with nothing left over, and the question asks for the greatest or maximum number or size. First find the HCF of the given numbers, then use it to answer what the question asks.

Worked example

Haider wants to distribute 36 sweets and 48 jellies equally among students. What is the maximum number of students among whom he can distribute them equally?

Step 1: For an equal distribution we need the HCF of 36 and 48.

Step 2: Factors of 36: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36.

Step 3: Factors of 48: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 48.

Step 4: Common factors: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. The greatest common factor is 12.

Answer: The maximum number of students is 12.

Key points

  • Words like maximum, greatest and largest with equal sharing point to HCF.
  • After finding the HCF, divide to find how much each share gets.
  • Always check that the HCF divides every given number exactly.

mcqs.q: Haider distributes 36 sweets and 48 jellies equally. What is the maximum number of students?
mcqs.why: Factors of 36 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36 and factors of 48 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 48. The common factors are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12, and the greatest is 12, so the maximum number of students is 12.

mcqs.q: 18 Science books, 24 Maths books and 36 English books are arranged in equal bundles using the HCF. What is the HCF of 18, 24 and 36?
mcqs.why: Factors of 18 are 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18; factors of 24 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24; factors of 36 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36. The factors in all three lists are 1, 2, 3 and 6, and the greatest is 6, so HCF = 6.

mcqs.q: Two ribbons are 44 m and 66 m long and are cut into pieces of the same length. What is the greatest length of each piece?
mcqs.why: Factors of 44 are 1, 2, 4, 11, 22, 44 and factors of 66 are 1, 2, 3, 6, 11, 22, 33, 66. The common factors are 1, 2, 11 and 22, and the greatest is 22, so each piece can be 22 m long with nothing left over.

mcqs.q: Tablecloths 48 cm and 90 cm wide are cut into strips of equal width. What is the maximum width of each strip?
mcqs.why: Factors of 48 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 48 and factors of 90 are 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 9, 10, 15, 18, 30, 45, 90. The common factors are 1, 2, 3 and 6, and the greatest is 6, so the maximum strip width is 6 cm.

mcqs.q: A teacher shares 32 red, 28 blue and 20 green balloons equally. The equal share number is the HCF of 32, 28 and 20. What is it?
mcqs.why: Factors of 32 are 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32; factors of 28 are 1, 2, 4, 7, 14, 28; factors of 20 are 1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20. The factors in all three lists are 1, 2 and 4, and the greatest is 4, so the balloons divide equally into 4 shares.

mcqs.q: Three containers hold 144, 176 and 256 litres of oil. What is the capacity of the largest tin that can measure all the oil exactly?
mcqs.why: Common factors of 144, 176 and 256: factors of 176 are 1, 2, 4, 8, 11, 16, 22, 44, 88, 176 and factors of 256 are 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256. The factors common to all three are 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16, and the greatest is 16, so the largest tin holds 16 litres.

mcqs.q: Haider shares his items among the maximum 12 students. How many sweets does each student get from the 36 sweets?
mcqs.why: The maximum number of students is the HCF of 36 and 48, which is 12. Divide the sweets equally: 36 / 12 = 3, so each student gets 3 sweets. As a check, the jellies give 48 / 12 = 4 jellies each, also exact.

mcqs.q: The 44 m ribbon is cut into pieces of the greatest length, 22 m. How many pieces are cut from it?
mcqs.why: The greatest piece length is the HCF of 44 and 66, which is 22 m. Divide the ribbon by the piece length: 44 / 22 = 2, so 2 pieces are cut from the 44 m ribbon. The 66 m ribbon gives 66 / 22 = 3 pieces.

mcqs.q: The books are arranged using HCF 6. How many Science books go in each equal share, out of 18 Science books?
mcqs.why: The HCF of 18, 24 and 36 is 6, so there are 6 equal shares. Divide the Science books: 18 / 6 = 3, so each share gets 3 Science books. As a check, Maths gives 24 / 6 = 4 and English gives 36 / 6 = 6 per share.

mcqs.q: The largest oil tin holds 16 litres. How many full tins are needed to measure the 144 litres exactly?
mcqs.why: The tin capacity is the HCF of 144, 176 and 256, which is 16 litres. Divide: 144 / 16 = 9, so 9 full tins measure the 144 litres exactly. As a check, 176 / 16 = 11 and 256 / 16 = 16 are also whole numbers.

lessons.title: Exercise 2.7: Lowest Common Multiple (LCM)
lessons.notes_html:
Lowest Common Multiple

A common multiple is a multiple that appears in the lists of two or more numbers. The Lowest Common Multiple (LCM) is the smallest of the common multiples. One method is to list the multiples of each number and pick the smallest one they share. By prime factorization, take every prime factor the greatest number of times it appears in any one number, and multiply them all.

Worked example

Find the LCM of 42 and 18 by the prime factorization method.

Step 1: Prime factors of 42: 42 = 2 x 3 x 7.

Step 2: Prime factors of 18: 18 = 2 x 3 x 3.

Step 3: Take every prime factor the greatest number of times it appears: 2 appears once, 3 appears twice in 18, and 7 appears once, so 2 x 3 x 3 x 7 = 126.

Answer: LCM = 126.

Key points

  • For LCM, take each prime factor the greatest number of times it appears; for HCF, take only the common primes.
  • The LCM is never smaller than the largest number in the question.
  • If one number is a multiple of the other, the larger number is the LCM, like 10 and 20 giving LCM 20.

mcqs.q: What is the LCM of 25 and 15 by the common multiples method?
mcqs.why: Multiples of 25 are 25, 50, 75 and multiples of 15 are 15, 30, 45, 60, 75. The first multiple appearing in both lists is 75, so LCM = 75. 50 is not a multiple of 15, so it cannot be common.

mcqs.q: What is the LCM of 12 and 14?
mcqs.why: Multiples of 12 are 12, 24, 36, 48, 60, 72, 84 and multiples of 14 are 14, 28, 42, 56, 70, 84. The smallest multiple in both lists is 84, so LCM = 84. 42 is a multiple of 14 but not of 12.

mcqs.q: What is the LCM of 6 and 9?
mcqs.why: Multiples of 6 are 6, 12, 18 and multiples of 9 are 9, 18. The smallest multiple common to both lists is 18, so LCM = 18. 36 is also a common multiple, but it is not the lowest one.

mcqs.q: What is the LCM of 7 and 5?
mcqs.why: Multiples of 7 are 7, 14, 21, 28, 35 and multiples of 5 are 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35. The smallest multiple in both lists is 35, so LCM = 35. 70 is common too, but it is twice as big.

mcqs.q: What is the LCM of 42 and 18 by prime factorization?
mcqs.why: Prime factorize: 42 = 2 x 3 x 7 and 18 = 2 x 3 x 3. Take every prime the greatest number of times: one 2, two 3s and one 7, giving 2 x 3 x 3 x 7 = 126. So LCM = 126.

mcqs.q: What is the LCM of 15 and 36 by prime factorization?
mcqs.why: Prime factorize: 15 = 3 x 5 and 36 = 2 x 2 x 3 x 3. Take every prime the greatest number of times: two 2s, two 3s and one 5, giving 2 x 2 x 3 x 3 x 5 = 180. So LCM = 180.

mcqs.q: What is the LCM of 35 and 15 by prime factorization?
mcqs.why: Prime factorize: 35 = 5 x 7 and 15 = 3 x 5. Take every prime the greatest number of times: one 3, one 5 and one 7, giving 3 x 5 x 7 = 105. So LCM = 105, and 105 / 35 = 3 and 105 / 15 = 7.

mcqs.q: What is the LCM of 11, 22 and 33?
mcqs.why: Prime factorize: 11 = 11, 22 = 2 x 11 and 33 = 3 x 11. Take every prime the greatest number of times: one 2, one 3 and one 11, giving 2 x 3 x 11 = 66. So LCM = 66, which is a multiple of all three numbers.

mcqs.q: What is the LCM of 24, 30 and 36?
mcqs.why: Prime factorize: 24 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 3, 30 = 2 x 3 x 5 and 36 = 2 x 2 x 3 x 3. Take every prime the greatest number of times: three 2s, two 3s and one 5, giving 2 x 2 x 2 x 3 x 3 x 5 = 360. So LCM = 360.

mcqs.q: What is the LCM of 30 and 18 by prime factorization?
mcqs.why: Prime factorize: 30 = 2 x 3 x 5 and 18 = 2 x 3 x 3. Take every prime the greatest number of times: one 2, two 3s and one 5, giving 2 x 3 x 3 x 5 = 90. So LCM = 90, and 90 / 30 = 3 and 90 / 18 = 5.

lessons.title: Exercise 2.8: LCM Word Problems
lessons.notes_html:
LCM in real-life problems

Use the LCM when events repeat and the question asks when they will happen together again, or for the least amount that matches two or more patterns. List the multiples of each number and find the smallest one they all share.

Worked example

Ali visits the garden every 15 days and Azhar every 20 days. Both met in the garden today. After how many days will they meet in the garden again?

Step 1: Find the LCM to get the day they come together.

Step 2: Multiples of 15: 15, 30, 45, 60.

Step 3: Multiples of 20: 20, 40, 60.

Step 4: The smallest multiple common to all is 60.

Answer: They will meet in the garden again after 60 days.

Key points

  • Words like together, same time and again point to LCM in word problems.
  • After finding the LCM, divide it by the total time to count how many times the events meet.
  • One radio station plays a song every 2 days and another every 3 days, so they play it together every 6 days, which is 5 times in 30 days.

mcqs.q: Ali saves Rs 9 every day and Maria saves Rs 12 every day. What is the least amount of money each can save so that both have saved the same amount?
mcqs.why: Multiples of 9 are 9, 18, 27, 36 and multiples of 12 are 12, 24, 36, so the LCM is 36 and the least equal amount is Rs 36. Note: the solved book wrongly calls 36 the number of days; 36 is the amount in rupees. Ali reaches it in 36 / 9 = 4 days and Maria in 36 / 12 = 3 days.

mcqs.q: One child smiles every 3 seconds and another smiles back every 6 seconds. After how many seconds will both smile at the same time?
mcqs.why: Multiples of 3 are 3, 6 and multiples of 6 are just 6 at the start. The smallest multiple common to both lists is 6, so both children smile together every 6 seconds. 12 seconds also works, but it is not the first time.

mcqs.q: Boxes 12 inches tall are piled next to boxes 10 inches tall. What is the least height, in inches, at which the two piles are the same height?
mcqs.why: Multiples of 12 are 12, 24, 36, 48, 60 and multiples of 10 are 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60. The smallest multiple in both lists is 60, so the least equal height is 60 inches, which is 60 / 12 = 5 feet.

mcqs.q: A marathon runner sips water every 9 minutes. Another sips every 8 minutes. What is the LCM of 9 and 8, the time after which they sip together?
mcqs.why: Multiples of 9 are 9, 18, 27, 36, 45, 54, 63, 72 and multiples of 8 are 8, 16, 24, 32, 40, 48, 56, 64, 72. The smallest multiple in both lists is 72, so they sip together after 72 minutes, matching the solved exercise.

mcqs.q: One radio station plays a song every 2 days and another every 3 days. How many times in 30 days will both play it on the same day?
mcqs.why: Multiples of 2 are 2, 4, 6 and multiples of 3 are 3, 6, so the LCM is 6 and the stations play together every 6 days. Divide the month: 30 / 6 = 5, so both stations play the song on the same day 5 times in 30 days.

mcqs.q: Ali runs every 12 days, Anees every 8 days and Ameen every 6 days. All ran today. After how many days will they all run together again?
mcqs.why: Multiples of 12 are 12, 24; multiples of 8 are 8, 16, 24; multiples of 6 are 6, 12, 18, 24. The smallest multiple appearing in all three lists is 24, so they will all run together again after 24 days.

mcqs.q: Ali visits the garden every 15 days and Azhar every 20 days. They met today. After how many days will they meet again?
mcqs.why: Multiples of 15 are 15, 30, 45, 60 and multiples of 20 are 20, 40, 60. The smallest multiple common to both lists is 60, so they will meet in the garden again after 60 days. 300 is the product 15 x 20, which is a common multiple but not the lowest.

mcqs.q: The two children smile together every 6 seconds. How many times will they smile together in 60 seconds?
mcqs.why: From the LCM of 3 and 6, the children smile together every 6 seconds. Divide the total time by the gap: 60 / 6 = 10, so in 60 seconds they smile at each other at the same time 10 times.

mcqs.q: The two piles of boxes first match at 60 inches. How many of the 12-inch boxes make that pile?
mcqs.why: The matching height is the LCM of 12 and 10, which is 60 inches from the multiples 12, 24, 36, 48, 60 and 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60. Divide: 60 / 12 = 5, so the pile has 5 boxes of 12 inches. The other pile has 60 / 10 = 6 boxes.

mcqs.q: In the 60 days until they meet again, how many times does Ali visit the garden if he goes every 15 days?
mcqs.why: Ali and Azhar meet again after the LCM of 15 and 20, which is 60 days. Ali visits every 15 days, so divide: 60 / 15 = 4. Ali visits 4 times in those 60 days, on days 15, 30, 45 and 60.

lessons.title: Review Exercise 2: Mixed Practice
lessons.notes_html:
Mixed review of Unit 2

This review mixes all the skills of the unit: divisibility rules, prime and composite numbers, prime factorization, HCF for equal sharing and LCM for events that meet together. Two different prime numbers have only one common factor, which is 1, and their LCM is simply their product.

Worked example

What is the HCF and LCM of 37 and 41? Explain how you got your answer.

Step 1: Factors of 37: 1, 37. It has only two factors, so 37 is prime.

Step 2: Factors of 41: 1, 41. It has only two factors, so 41 is also prime.

Step 3: Two different prime numbers have only one common factor: 1. So HCF = 1.

Step 4: The LCM of two prime numbers is their product: 37 x 41 = 1,517.

Answer: HCF = 1 and LCM = 1,517.

Key points

  • A number ending in 0 is divisible by 2, 5 and 10; still test the digit sum for 3.
  • For three numbers, the HCF must divide all three numbers exactly.
  • The LCM of 48 and 66 is 528, from 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 x 3 x 11.

mcqs.q: Which number is divisible by 2?
mcqs.why: A number is divisible by 2 when its last digit is even. The last digits are 7, 4, 7 and 3. Only 484 ends in the even digit 4, and 484 / 2 = 242 exactly, so 484 is divisible by 2.

mcqs.q: Which number is divisible by 3?
mcqs.why: Add the digits of each: 143 gives 1 + 4 + 3 = 8, 367 gives 3 + 6 + 7 = 16, 483 gives 4 + 8 + 3 = 15 and 941 gives 9 + 4 + 1 = 14. Only 15 is divisible by 3, so 483 is divisible by 3, and 483 / 3 = 161.

mcqs.q: Which number is divisible by both 2 and 10?
mcqs.why: Divisible by 10 needs a last digit of 0, and such a number is automatically even, so it is also divisible by 2. Only 4050 ends in 0. 2108 ends in 8, so it is divisible by 2 only, and 4579 and 3921 end in odd digits.

mcqs.q: What is the HCF of 39 and 52?
mcqs.why: Factors of 39 are 1, 3, 13, 39 and factors of 52 are 1, 2, 4, 13, 26, 52. The common factors are 1 and 13, and the greatest of them is 13, so the HCF of 39 and 52 is 13.

mcqs.q: What is the LCM of 48 and 66?
mcqs.why: Prime factorize: 48 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 x 3 and 66 = 2 x 3 x 11. Take every prime the greatest number of times: four 2s, one 3 and one 11, giving 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 x 3 x 11 = 528. So the LCM is 528.

mcqs.q: What is the HCF of 48, 69 and 36?
mcqs.why: Factors of 48 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 48; factors of 69 are 1, 3, 23, 69; factors of 36 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36. The factors in all three lists are 1 and 3, and the greatest is 3, so HCF = 3.

mcqs.q: What is the LCM of 48, 69 and 36?
mcqs.why: Prime factorize: 48 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 x 3, 69 = 3 x 23 and 36 = 2 x 2 x 3 x 3. Take every prime the greatest number of times: four 2s, two 3s and one 23, giving 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 x 3 x 3 x 23 = 3,312. So LCM = 3,312.

mcqs.q: What is the HCF of 37 and 41?
mcqs.why: Factors of 37 are 1 and 37, so 37 is prime. Factors of 41 are 1 and 41, so 41 is also prime. Two different prime numbers share only the factor 1, so the HCF of 37 and 41 is 1.

mcqs.q: What is the LCM of 37 and 41?
mcqs.why: Both 37 and 41 are prime, so they have no common prime factors to share. The LCM of two different prime numbers is their product: 37 x 41 = 1,517. Check: 1,517 / 37 = 41 and 1,517 / 41 = 37, both exact.

mcqs.q: Mrs. Sayem distributes 45 patties, 60 samosas and 75 juices equally. What is the greatest number of students?
