mcqs.why: Factors of 45 are 1, 3, 5, 9, 15, 45; factors of 60 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 10, 12, 15, 20, 30, 60; factors of 75 are 1, 3, 5, 15, 25, 75. The common factors are 1, 3, 5 and 15, and the greatest is 15, so the greatest number of students is 15.

lessons.title: Exercise 3.1: Like and Unlike Fractions and Their Comparison
lessons.notes_html:
Like and unlike fractions

A fraction has a numerator, the upper part, and a denominator, the lower part. In 3/5 the numerator is 3 and the denominator is 5. Fractions with the same denominator are like fractions. Fractions with different denominators are unlike fractions. To compare unlike fractions, first convert them into like fractions using the LCM of the denominators, then compare the numerators. A fraction can be simplified to its lowest form by dividing the numerator and denominator by common factors.

Worked example

Compare 5/6 and 4/9.

Step 1: The denominators are 6 and 9 and their LCM is 18.

Step 2: Convert 5/6 by multiplying the numerator and denominator by 3 to get 15/18.

Step 3: Convert 4/9 by multiplying the numerator and denominator by 2 to get 8/18.

Step 4: Compare the numerators 15 and 8. 15 is greater than 8.

Answer: 5/6 is greater than 4/9.

Key points

  • Like fractions have the same denominator, for example 2/7 and 6/7.
  • Unlike fractions have different denominators, for example 2/9 and 2/15.
  • To compare, make the denominators equal with the LCM and then compare numerators.
  • Simplify by dividing the numerator and denominator by the same common factor again and again.

mcqs.q: Are 2/7 and 6/7 like or unlike fractions?
mcqs.why: Both fractions have denominator 7. Fractions with the same denominator are like fractions, so 2/7 and 6/7 are like fractions.

mcqs.q: Are 2/9 and 2/15 like or unlike fractions?
mcqs.why: The denominators are 9 and 15, which are different. Fractions with different denominators are unlike fractions.

mcqs.q: In the fraction 3/5, what is the numerator?
mcqs.why: In 3/5 the upper part is 3 and the lower part is 5, so the numerator is 3 and the denominator is 5.

mcqs.q: Which fraction is greater, 5/6 or 4/9?
mcqs.why: LCM of 6 and 9 is 18. 5/6 = 15/18 and 4/9 = 8/18. Since 15 is greater than 8, 5/6 is greater than 4/9.

mcqs.q: Which fraction is smaller, 2/7 or 13/14?
mcqs.why: LCM of 7 and 14 is 14. 2/7 = 4/14 and 13/14 stays 13/14. Since 4 is smaller than 13, 2/7 is smaller than 13/14.

mcqs.q: Arrange in ascending order: 6/7, 9/7, 5/7.
mcqs.why: All denominators are already 7, so order by numerators from smallest to largest: 5, then 6, then 9, giving 5/7, 6/7, 9/7.

mcqs.q: Arrange in ascending order: 5/6, 2/3, 5/9.
mcqs.why: LCM of 6, 3 and 9 is 18. 5/6 = 15/18, 2/3 = 12/18 and 5/9 = 10/18. Smallest numerator first gives 5/9, 2/3, 5/6.

mcqs.q: Simplify 24/32 to its lowest form.
mcqs.why: Divide by 2: 24/32 = 12/16. Divide by 2 again: 12/16 = 6/8. Divide by 2 again: 6/8 = 3/4, which is the lowest form.

mcqs.q: Simplify 18/27 to its lowest form.
mcqs.why: Divide the numerator and denominator by 3: 18/27 = 6/9. Divide by 3 again: 6/9 = 2/3, which is the lowest form.

mcqs.q: Simplify 33/66 to its lowest form.
mcqs.why: Divide the numerator and denominator by 3: 33/66 = 11/22. Divide by 11: 11/22 = 1/2, which is the lowest form.

lessons.title: Exercise 3.2: Types of Fractions and Conversion
lessons.notes_html:
Types of fractions

A unit fraction has numerator 1, for example 1/3 and 1/4. A proper fraction has a numerator smaller than the denominator, for example 5/9. An improper fraction has a numerator greater than or equal to the denominator. A mixed fraction has a whole part and a fraction part, for example 4 3/4 and 2 1/8. To convert an improper fraction into a mixed fraction, divide the numerator by the denominator. To convert a mixed fraction into an improper fraction, multiply the whole part by the denominator and add the numerator.

Worked example

Convert the improper fraction 43/7 into a mixed fraction.

Step 1: Divide the numerator 43 by the denominator 7.

Step 2: 43 divided by 7 is 6 remainder 1.

Step 3: The quotient 6 becomes the whole part and the remainder 1 becomes the new numerator. The denominator stays 7.

Answer: 43/7 = 6 1/7.

Key points

  • Unit fraction: numerator is 1.
  • Proper fraction: numerator is smaller than the denominator.
  • Mixed fraction: a whole number together with a proper fraction, for example 1 1/3 is a mixed fraction.
  • Improper to mixed: divide. Mixed to improper: whole times denominator plus numerator, over the same denominator.

mcqs.q: What type of fraction is 1/3?
mcqs.why: The numerator of 1/3 is 1. A fraction with numerator 1 is a unit fraction, so 1/3 is a unit fraction.

mcqs.q: What type of fraction is 5/9?
mcqs.why: In 5/9 the numerator 5 is smaller than the denominator 9, so 5/9 is a proper fraction.

mcqs.q: What type of fraction is 4 3/4?
mcqs.why: 4 3/4 has a whole part 4 and a fraction part 3/4, so it is a mixed fraction. Note: the solved book wrongly calls it improper; a whole part plus a fraction part is mixed.

mcqs.q: What type of fraction is 1 1/3?
mcqs.why: 1 1/3 has a whole part 1 and a fraction part 1/3, so it is a mixed fraction. Note: the solved book wrongly calls it improper; the mixed form is the correct type.

mcqs.q: A circle is divided into 5 equal parts and 1 part is shaded. What type of fraction is this?
mcqs.why: One shaded part out of 5 equal parts is 1/5. Its numerator is 1, so 1/5 is a unit fraction.

mcqs.q: Convert 43/7 into a mixed fraction.
mcqs.why: Divide 43 by 7: 43 = 7 x 6 + 1, so the quotient is 6 and the remainder is 1. The mixed fraction is 6 1/7.

mcqs.q: Convert 14/6 into a mixed fraction in its lowest form.
mcqs.why: Divide 14 by 6: quotient 2 remainder 2, giving 2 2/6. Simplify 2/6 by dividing by 2 to get 1/3, so the answer is 2 1/3.

mcqs.q: Express 4 3/10 as an improper fraction.
mcqs.why: Multiply the whole part by the denominator: 4 x 10 = 40. Add the numerator: 40 + 3 = 43. Keep denominator 10, giving 43/10.

mcqs.q: Express 5 2/3 as an improper fraction.
mcqs.why: Multiply the whole part by the denominator: 5 x 3 = 15. Add the numerator: 15 + 2 = 17. Keep denominator 3, giving 17/3.

mcqs.q: Express 7 7/8 as an improper fraction.
mcqs.why: Multiply the whole part by the denominator: 7 x 8 = 56. Add the numerator: 56 + 7 = 63. Keep denominator 8, giving 63/8.

lessons.title: Exercise 3.3: Addition and Subtraction of Fractions
lessons.notes_html:
Adding and subtracting fractions

To add or subtract fractions, first make the denominators the same using the LCM. Convert any mixed fraction into an improper fraction first. Then add or subtract only the numerators and keep the denominator the same. Simplify the result and change it back into a mixed fraction if needed. Addition is commutative, so changing the order does not change the sum, and associative, so changing the grouping does not change the sum.

Worked example

Add 2/3 + 1 2/9.

Step 1: The denominators are 3 and 9 and their LCM is 9.

Step 2: Convert 2/3 to 6/9 and convert 1 2/9 to 11/9.

Step 3: Add the numerators: 6 + 11 = 17, giving 17/9.

Step 4: Change 17/9 into a mixed fraction: 17 divided by 9 is 1 remainder 8.

Answer: 1 8/9.

Key points

  • Never add or subtract the denominators.
  • Use the LCM to make like fractions first.
  • Change mixed fractions into improper fractions before adding or subtracting.
  • Simplify the final answer and use a mixed fraction when the numerator is bigger.

mcqs.why: LCM of 3 and 9 is 9. 2/3 = 6/9 and 1 2/9 = 11/9. Add numerators: 6 + 11 = 17, giving 17/9 = 1 8/9.
LCM of 6 and 2 is 6. 1 1/6 = 7/6 and 1/2 = 3/6. Add: 7 + 3 = 10, giving 10/6 = 5/3 = 1 2/3 after simplifying.

mcqs.q: Subtract: 5/6 - 1/2.
mcqs.why: LCM of 6 and 2 is 6. 5/6 stays 5/6 and 1/2 = 3/6. Subtract: 5 - 3 = 2, giving 2/6, which simplifies by dividing by 2 to 1/3.

mcqs.q: Subtract: 7/8 - 3/4.
mcqs.why: LCM of 8 and 4 is 8. 7/8 stays 7/8 and 3/4 = 6/8. Subtract: 7 - 6 = 1, giving 1/8.

mcqs.q: Subtract: 4/5 - 1/3.
mcqs.why: LCM of 5 and 3 is 15. 4/5 = 12/15 and 1/3 = 5/15. Subtract: 12 - 5 = 7, giving 7/15.

mcqs.q: Subtract: 9 1/2 - 3 1/5.
Find the missing value: 3/5 + 7/4 = ? + 3/5.
mcqs.why: By the commutative property the order of addition does not change the sum, so the fraction that swaps places with 3/5 is 7/4.

mcqs.q: Find the missing value: 1/3 + (1/5 + 1/4) = (1/3 + ?) + 1/4.
mcqs.why: By the associative property only the grouping changes and the fractions stay the same, so the missing fraction inside the new brackets is 1/5.

lessons.title: Exercise 3.4: Multiplication of Fractions
lessons.notes_html:
Multiplying fractions

To multiply fractions, first convert any mixed fraction into an improper fraction. Then multiply the numerators together and multiply the denominators together. A whole number is written as a fraction over 1, for example 9 is 9/1. The word of means multiply. Always simplify the product and write it as a mixed number when the numerator is bigger than the denominator.

Worked example

Find the product: 1/2 x 4/10.

Step 1: Multiply the numerators: 1 x 4 = 4.

Step 2: Multiply the denominators: 2 x 10 = 20, giving 4/20.

Step 3: Divide the numerator and denominator by 2: 4/20 = 2/10.

Step 4: Divide by 2 again: 2/10 = 1/5.

Answer: 1/5.

Key points

  • Multiply numerators together and denominators together. Do not use an LCM for multiplication.
  • Change mixed fractions into improper fractions first.
  • Write a whole number over 1 before multiplying.
  • Simplify the answer fully.

mcqs.q: Find 5/6 of 9.
mcqs.why: Write 9 as 9/1. Multiply numerators: 5 x 9 = 45. Multiply denominators: 6 x 1 = 6, giving 45/6 = 15/2 = 7 1/2 after simplifying.

mcqs.q: Find 4/8 of 6.
mcqs.why: Write 6 as 6/1. Multiply: 4 x 6 = 24 and 8 x 1 = 8, giving 24/8. Simplify by dividing by 8 to get 3.

mcqs.q: Find the product: 1/2 x 4/10.
mcqs.why: Multiply numerators: 1 x 4 = 4. Multiply denominators: 2 x 10 = 20, giving 4/20. Simplify by dividing by 4 to get 1/5.

mcqs.q: Find the product: 6/9 x 8/6.
mcqs.why: Multiply numerators: 6 x 8 = 48. Multiply denominators: 9 x 6 = 54, giving 48/54. Simplify by dividing by 6 to get 8/9.

mcqs.q: Find the product: 12/24 x 15/18.
mcqs.why: Multiply numerators: 12 x 15 = 180. Multiply denominators: 24 x 18 = 432, giving 180/432. Simplify step by step to 5/12.

mcqs.q: Find the product: 6/12 x 21/24.
mcqs.why: Multiply numerators: 6 x 21 = 126. Multiply denominators: 12 x 24 = 288, giving 126/288. Simplify step by step to 7/16.

mcqs.q: Find the product: 8/16 x 4/8 x 3/2.
mcqs.why: Multiply numerators: 8 x 4 x 3 = 96. Multiply denominators: 16 x 8 x 2 = 256, giving 96/256. Simplify by dividing by 32 to get 3/8.

mcqs.q: Find the product: 8 1/4 x 3 2/6.
Find 3/14 of 45.
mcqs.why: Write 45 as 45/1. Multiply numerators: 3 x 45 = 135. Multiply denominators: 14 x 1 = 14, giving 135/14 = 9 9/14.

mcqs.q: Find the product: 15/21 x 6/9 x 1/2.
mcqs.why: Multiply numerators: 15 x 6 x 1 = 90. Multiply denominators: 21 x 9 x 2 = 378, giving 90/378. Simplify step by step to 5/21.

lessons.title: Exercise 3.5: Division of Fractions
lessons.notes_html:
Dividing fractions

To divide fractions, keep the first fraction as it is, flip the second fraction to make its reciprocal, and change the division into multiplication. Then multiply the numerators and multiply the denominators. Convert any mixed fraction into an improper fraction first. A whole number is written over 1, and its flip swaps the numerator and denominator, for example 8 becomes 1/8 when flipped. Always simplify the final answer.

Worked example

Solve: 4/9 divided by 16/9.

Step 1: Keep the first fraction 4/9 as it is.

Step 2: Flip the second fraction: 16/9 becomes 9/16.

Step 3: Multiply: 4 x 9 = 36 and 9 x 16 = 144, giving 36/144.

Step 4: Simplify step by step: 36/144 = 18/72 = 9/36 = 3/12 = 1/4.

Answer: 1/4.

Key points

  • Keep, flip, change: keep the first fraction, flip the second, change division to multiplication.
  • Never flip the first fraction.
  • Change mixed fractions and whole numbers into fractions over 1 first.
  • Simplify the answer fully and use a mixed number when needed.

mcqs.q: Solve: 4/9 divided by 16/9.
mcqs.why: Keep 4/9 and flip 16/9 to 9/16. Multiply: 4 x 9 = 36 and 9 x 16 = 144, giving 36/144, which simplifies step by step to 1/4.

mcqs.q: Solve: 4/8 divided by 2/12.
mcqs.why: Keep 4/8 and flip 2/12 to 12/2. Multiply: 4 x 12 = 48 and 8 x 2 = 16, giving 48/16 = 3 after simplifying.

mcqs.q: Solve: 1/4 divided by 7/16.
mcqs.why: Keep 1/4 and flip 7/16 to 16/7. Multiply: 1 x 16 = 16 and 4 x 7 = 28, giving 16/28, which simplifies by dividing by 4 to 4/7.

mcqs.q: Solve: 9/10 divided by 12/15.
mcqs.why: Keep 9/10 and flip 12/15 to 15/12. Multiply: 9 x 15 = 135 and 10 x 12 = 120, giving 135/120 = 9/8 = 1 1/8 after simplifying.

mcqs.q: Solve: 9/30 divided by 6/12.
mcqs.why: Keep 9/30 and flip 6/12 to 12/6. Multiply: 9 x 12 = 108 and 30 x 6 = 180, giving 108/180, which simplifies step by step to 3/5.

mcqs.q: Solve: 12/21 divided by 6/27.
mcqs.why: Keep 12/21 and flip 6/27 to 27/6. Multiply: 12 x 27 = 324 and 21 x 6 = 126, giving 324/126 = 18/7 = 2 4/7 after simplifying.

mcqs.q: Solve: 2 1/3 divided by 2/5.
mcqs.why: Convert 2 1/3 to 7/3 and flip 2/5 to 5/2. Multiply: 7 x 5 = 35 and 3 x 2 = 6, giving 35/6 = 5 5/6.

mcqs.q: Solve: 6 divided by 2/3.
mcqs.why: Write 6 as 6/1 and flip 2/3 to 3/2. Multiply: 6 x 3 = 18 and 1 x 2 = 2, giving 18/2 = 9.

mcqs.q: Solve: 2/3 divided by 8.
mcqs.why: Keep 2/3 and flip 8, written as 8/1, to 1/8. Multiply: 2 x 1 = 2 and 3 x 8 = 24, giving 2/24 = 1/12 after simplifying.

mcqs.q: Solve: 12/5 divided by 9.
mcqs.why: Keep 12/5 and flip 9, written as 9/1, to 1/9. Multiply: 12 x 1 = 12 and 5 x 9 = 45, giving 12/45 = 4/15 after dividing by 3.

lessons.title: Exercise 3.6: Fraction Word Problems
lessons.notes_html:
Word problems with fractions

Read the problem carefully and decide the operation. Putting amounts together means addition. Finding how much more or how much is left means subtraction. Finding a fraction of an amount means multiplication. Sharing a total into equal parts of a given size means division. Use the LCM for addition and subtraction, convert mixed fractions into improper fractions, and simplify the answer. Write the unit, such as litres, cm or metres, with the final answer.

Worked example

A family used 4 1/4 litres of milk and another family used 7 1/2 litres in a day. How much milk was used by both families?

Step 1: Both amounts are put together, so add them.

Step 2: The denominators are 4 and 2 and their LCM is 4. Convert 4 1/4 to 17/4 and 7 1/2 to 30/4.

Step 3: Add the numerators: 17 + 30 = 47, giving 47/4.

Step 4: Change 47/4 into a mixed fraction: 47 divided by 4 is 11 remainder 3.

Answer: Both families used 11 3/4 litres of milk in all.

Key points

  • Together and in all usually mean add.
  • How much longer, how much more and younger usually mean subtract.
  • A fraction of an amount means multiply.
  • How many pieces or bags from a total means divide the total by the size of one part.

mcqs.q: A family used 4 1/4 litres of milk and another used 7 1/2 litres. How much milk did both families use?
mcqs.why: Add with LCM 4: 4 1/4 = 17/4 and 7 1/2 = 30/4. Add numerators: 17 + 30 = 47, giving 47/4 = 11 3/4 litres.

mcqs.q: My aunty buys a piece of ribbon 4 1/6 cm long and another piece 4 2/5 cm long. How much longer was the second piece?
mcqs.why: Subtract with LCM 30: 4 2/5 = 132/30 and 4 1/6 = 125/30. Subtract: 132 - 125 = 7, giving 7/30 cm longer.

mcqs.q: I am 8 1/2 years old and my brother is 2 1/2 years younger. How old is my brother?
mcqs.why: Subtract with denominator 2: 8 1/2 = 17/2 and 2 1/2 = 5/2. Subtract: 17 - 5 = 12, giving 12/2 = 6 years old.

mcqs.q: Nazia has 4 4/5 metres of ribbon and used 1/2 of it. How many metres did she use?
mcqs.why: Of means multiply. Convert 4 4/5 to 24/5. Multiply: 24 x 1 = 24 and 5 x 2 = 10, giving 24/10 = 12/5 = 2 2/5 metres.

mcqs.q: A tree is 18 metres tall. How many pieces of 2/3 metre can be cut from it?
mcqs.why: Divide 18 by 2/3. Flip 2/3 to 3/2 and multiply: 18 x 3 = 54 and 1 x 2 = 2, giving 54/2 = 27 pieces.

mcqs.q: A shopkeeper has 15 kg of peanuts and puts 2/5 kg in each bag. How many bags are needed?
options: 37 bags exactly with no part bag
mcqs.why: Divide 15 by 2/5. Flip 2/5 to 5/2 and multiply: 15 x 5 = 75 and 1 x 2 = 2, giving 75/2 = 37 1/2, so 38 bags are needed and the last is half filled.

mcqs.q: How much more milk did the second family (7 1/2 litres) use than the first family (4 1/4 litres)?
mcqs.why: Subtract with LCM 4: 7 1/2 = 30/4 and 4 1/4 = 17/4. Subtract: 30 - 17 = 13, giving 13/4 = 3 1/4 litres more.

mcqs.q: What is the total length of ribbon pieces 4 1/6 cm and 4 2/5 cm together?
Nazia had 4 4/5 metres of ribbon and used 2 2/5 metres. How much ribbon is left?
mcqs.why: Subtract with denominator 5: 4 4/5 - 2 2/5. Subtract wholes 4 - 2 = 2 and fractions 4/5 - 2/5 = 2/5, giving 2 2/5 metres left.

mcqs.q: My age is 8 1/2 years and my brother is 6 years old. What is the sum of our ages?
mcqs.why: Add: 8 1/2 + 6 = 8 1/2 + 6/1. With denominator 2 this is 17/2 + 12/2 = 29/2 = 14 1/2 years.

lessons.title: Review Exercise 3: Mixed Practice
lessons.notes_html:
Mixed practice

This review mixes all the skills of the unit: converting between improper fractions and mixed fractions, arranging fractions in ascending and descending order, reducing fractions to the lowest terms, and adding, subtracting, multiplying and dividing fractions. For ordering, addition and subtraction use the LCM. For multiplication multiply across. For division keep, flip and change to multiplication.

Worked example

Simplify: 3/5 + 2/4.

Step 1: The denominators are 5 and 4 and their LCM is 20.

Step 2: Convert 3/5 to 12/20 and 2/4 to 10/20.

Step 3: Add the numerators: 12 + 10 = 22, giving 22/20.

Step 4: Divide the numerator and denominator by 2: 22/20 = 11/10.

Answer: 1 1/10.

Key points

  • Improper to mixed: divide the numerator by the denominator.
  • Mixed to improper: whole times denominator plus numerator.
  • Ascending means smallest first and descending means largest first.
  • Always give the final answer in the lowest terms.

mcqs.q: Convert 66/8 into a mixed fraction in its lowest form.
mcqs.why: Divide 66 by 8: quotient 8 remainder 2, giving 8 2/8. Simplify 2/8 by dividing by 2 to get 1/4, so the answer is 8 1/4.

mcqs.q: Express 8 4/5 as an improper fraction.
mcqs.why: Multiply the whole part by the denominator: 8 x 5 = 40. Add the numerator: 40 + 4 = 44. Keep denominator 5, giving 44/5.

mcqs.q: Arrange in ascending order: 2/3, 1/4, 5/6.
mcqs.why: LCM of 3, 4 and 6 is 12. 2/3 = 8/12, 1/4 = 3/12 and 5/6 = 10/12. Smallest first gives 1/4, 2/3, 5/6.

mcqs.q: Arrange in descending order: 2/3, 3/5, 5/6.
Reduce 30/42 to the lowest terms.
mcqs.why: Divide by 2: 30/42 = 15/21. Divide by 3: 15/21 = 5/7, which is the lowest form.

mcqs.q: Simplify: 3/5 + 2/4.
Simplify: 3/4 - 4/8.
mcqs.why: LCM of 4 and 8 is 8. 3/4 = 6/8 and 4/8 stays 4/8. Subtract: 6 - 4 = 2, giving 2/8 = 1/4 after simplifying.

mcqs.q: Multiply in lowest terms: 2 2/5 x 2 1/2.
mcqs.why: Convert: 2 2/5 = 12/5 and 2 1/2 = 5/2. Multiply: 12 x 5 = 60 and 5 x 2 = 10, giving 60/10 = 6.

mcqs.q: Divide in lowest terms: 3/4 divided by 5/8.
mcqs.why: Keep 3/4 and flip 5/8 to 8/5. Multiply: 3 x 8 = 24 and 4 x 5 = 20, giving 24/20 = 6/5 = 1 1/5 after simplifying.

mcqs.q: There are 32 balloons and 1/4 are red. How many balloons are red?
mcqs.why: Find 1/4 of 32. Multiply: 1 x 32 = 32 and 4 x 1 = 4, giving 32/4 = 8, so 8 balloons are red.

lessons.title: Exercise 4.1: Decimal Figures and Place Value
lessons.notes_html:
Decimal figures and place value

A decimal fraction shows parts of a whole using a decimal point. A strip divided into 10 equal parts gives tenths, a grid of 100 squares gives hundredths and 1000 parts give thousandths. The digits after the point are the decimal places. The first place after the point is tenths, the second is hundredths and the third is thousandths.

Worked example

Write the place value and value of each digit in 18.97.

Step 1: Start from the left. The digit 1 is in the tens place, so its value is 10.

Step 2: The digit 8 is in the ones place, so its value is 8.

Step 3: The digit 9 is the first digit after the point, in the tenths place, so its value is 0.9.

Step 4: The digit 7 is in the hundredths place, so its value is 0.07.

Answer: 18.97 means 10 and 8 and 0.9 and 0.07.

Key points

  • Count the digits after the decimal point to find the number of decimal places.
  • One decimal place means denominator 10, two means 100 and three means 1000.
  • Shading 34 squares of a 100-square grid shows 0.34.

mcqs.q: A strip is divided into 10 equal parts and 3 parts are shaded. What decimal does the figure show?
mcqs.why: 3 shaded parts out of 10 equal parts is the fraction 3/10. Denominator 10 means one decimal place, so write 3 after the point with 0 before it: 0.3.

mcqs.q: How many decimal places are there in 57.322?
mcqs.why: Count the digits after the decimal point in 57.322. The digits are 3, 2 and 2, which is 3 digits, so the number has three decimal places.

mcqs.q: How many decimal places are there in 0.87?
mcqs.why: The digits after the decimal point in 0.87 are 8 and 7. Counting them gives 2 digits, so 0.87 has two decimal places.

mcqs.q: In 725.04, what is the value of the digit 4?
mcqs.why: In 725.04 the digit 4 is the second digit after the point, so it is in the hundredths place. Its value is 4 hundredths, which is 4/100 = 0.04.

mcqs.q: In 5.092, in which place is the digit 2?
mcqs.why: After the point in 5.092, 0 is in the tenths place, 9 is in the hundredths place and 2 is in the third place, the thousandths place, with value 0.002.

mcqs.q: In 0.534, what is the value of the digit 5?
mcqs.why: The digit 5 in 0.534 is the first digit after the decimal point, so it is in the tenths place. Five tenths is 5/10, which equals 0.5.

mcqs.q: In a grid of 100 squares, 23 squares are shaded. What decimal does this show?
mcqs.why: 23 shaded squares out of 100 is 23/100. Denominator 100 means two decimal places, so place the point two places from the right in 23: 0.23.

mcqs.q: In 18.97, what is the value of the digit 7?
mcqs.why: In 18.97 the digit 7 is the second digit after the point, in the hundredths place. Seven hundredths is written as 7/100, which equals 0.07.

mcqs.q: One full strip is shaded and 6 parts of another strip of 10 parts are shaded. What decimal is shown?
mcqs.why: The full strip is 1 whole and the 6 parts are 6/10 = 0.6. Adding them gives 1 + 0.6 = 1.6, so the figure shows 1.6.

mcqs.q: How many decimal places are there in 735.9?
mcqs.why: In 735.9 there is only one digit after the decimal point, the digit 9. So the number has one decimal place.

lessons.title: Exercise 4.2: Conversion of Fractions and Decimals
lessons.notes_html:
Changing fractions and decimals

To change a fraction into a decimal, first make the denominator 10, 100 or 1000, then write the numerator and place the decimal point. The number of zeros in the denominator tells how many places to count from the right. To change a decimal into a fraction, write the digits over 10, 100 or 1000 and then make it simplest form.

Worked example

Convert 3/4 into a decimal.

Step 1: Make the denominator 100. Multiply the numerator and denominator by 25.

Step 2: 3 times 25 is 75, so the new fraction is 75/100.

Step 3: Denominator 100 has 2 zeros, so place the point 2 places from the right in 75.

Answer: 3/4 = 0.75.

Key points

  • Multiply the top and bottom by the same number; the value does not change.
  • For 25 multiply by 4, for 4 multiply by 25, for 8 multiply by 125.
  • Always reduce a fraction answer to its simplest form.

mcqs.q: Convert 5/10 into a decimal.
mcqs.why: The denominator 10 has one zero, so place the decimal point one place from the right in the numerator 5. Put a 0 before the point: 5/10 = 0.5.

mcqs.q: Convert 23/100 into a decimal.
mcqs.why: The denominator 100 has two zeros, so place the decimal point two places from the right in 23. This gives 23/100 = 0.23.

mcqs.q: Convert 29/1000 into a decimal.
mcqs.why: The denominator 1000 has three zeros, so the point goes three places from the right. Write 29 as 029 and place the point: 29/1000 = 0.029.

mcqs.q: Convert 7/25 into a decimal.
mcqs.why: Multiply numerator and denominator by 4 to make the denominator 100: 7 times 4 is 28, giving 28/100. Place the point two places from the right: 0.28.

mcqs.q: Convert 3/4 into a decimal.
mcqs.why: Multiply numerator and denominator by 25 to make the denominator 100: 3 times 25 is 75, giving 75/100. Place the point two places from the right: 0.75.

mcqs.q: Convert 0.45 into a fraction in its simplest form.
mcqs.why: 0.45 has two decimal places, so write it as 45/100. Divide the numerator and denominator by 5: 45 divided by 5 is 9 and 100 divided by 5 is 20, giving 9/20.

mcqs.q: Convert 0.3 into a fraction in its simplest form.
mcqs.why: 0.3 has one decimal place, so the denominator is 10. Write the digit 3 over 10 to get 3/10, which is already in its simplest form.

mcqs.q: Convert 231/100 into a decimal.
mcqs.why: The denominator 100 has two zeros, so place the decimal point two places from the right in 231. Counting back two places gives 231/100 = 2.31.

mcqs.q: Convert 3/8 into a decimal.
mcqs.why: Multiply numerator and denominator by 125 to make the denominator 1000: 3 times 125 is 375, giving 375/1000. Place the point three places from the right: 0.375.

mcqs.q: Convert 1.35 into a fraction in its simplest form.
mcqs.why: 1.35 has two decimal places, so write it as 135/100. Divide top and bottom by 5 to get 27/20, which as a mixed number is 1 7/20.

lessons.title: Exercise 4.3: Addition and Subtraction of Decimals
lessons.notes_html:
Adding and subtracting decimals

Write the numbers one below the other with the decimal points in one straight line, so ones are under ones, tenths under tenths and hundredths under hundredths. Then add or subtract column by column from the right, carrying or borrowing just like whole numbers, and put the point in the answer in the same line.

Worked example

Add 25.32 and 15.75.

Step 1: Line up the points. Hundredths column: 2 + 5 = 7.

Step 2: Tenths column: 3 + 7 = 10, write 0 and carry 1.

Step 3: Ones column: 5 + 5 + 1 carried = 11, write 1 and carry 1.

Step 4: Tens column: 2 + 1 + 1 carried = 4. Put the point in line.

Answer: 25.32 + 15.75 = 41.07.

Key points

  • Misaligned points are the most common mistake; always line the points up first.
  • Add a zero at the end if needed, for example write 97.5 as 97.50.
  • Work from the rightmost column and carry or borrow carefully.

mcqs.why: Line up the decimal points. Hundredths: 5 + 2 = 7. Tenths: 3 + 4 = 7. Keep the point in the same column in the answer: 0.35 + 0.42 = 0.77.
Hundredths: 7 + 9 = 16, write 6 and carry 1. Tenths: 2 + 4 + 1 carried = 7. Ones: 1 + 3 = 4. With points aligned the answer is 4.76.

mcqs.q: Subtract: 0.84 - 0.61
mcqs.why: Line up the points and subtract column by column. Hundredths: 4 - 1 = 3. Tenths: 8 - 6 = 2. So 0.84 - 0.61 = 0.23.
Tenths: 5 + 2 + 9 = 16, write 6 and carry 1. Ones: 3 + 4 + 7 + 1 carried = 15, write 5 and carry 1. Tens: 1 + 1 + 1 carried = 3. Answer: 35.6.

mcqs.q: Subtract: 10.59 - 3.27
mcqs.why: Hundredths: 9 - 7 = 2. Tenths: 5 - 2 = 3. Ones: 0 - 3 needs the tens, giving 10 - 3 = 7 after borrowing. With points aligned: 10.59 - 3.27 = 7.32.
Hundredths: 2 + 5 = 7. Tenths: 3 + 7 = 10, write 0 carry 1. Ones: 5 + 5 + 1 = 11, write 1 carry 1. Tens: 2 + 1 + 1 = 4. Answer: 41.07.

mcqs.q: Subtract: 0.9 - 0.3
mcqs.why: Both numbers have one decimal place. Work in tenths: 9 tenths minus 3 tenths equals 6 tenths. Six tenths is written as 0.6.

Thousandths: 8 + 3 = 11, write 1 carry 1. Hundredths: 7 + 3 + 1 = 11, write 1 carry 1. Tenths: 3 + 6 + 1 = 10, write 0 carry 1. Ones: 8 + 2 + 1 = 11, write 1 carry 1. Tens: 6 + 1 + 1 = 8. Answer: 81.011.

mcqs.q: Subtract: 54.79 - 39.84
mcqs.why: Hundredths: 9 - 4 = 5. Tenths: borrow, 17 - 8 = 9. Ones: borrow, 13 - 9 = 4. Tens: 4 - 3 = 1. With points aligned: 54.79 - 39.84 = 14.95.
Thousandths: 3 + 3 = 6. Hundredths: 4 + 8 = 12, write 2 carry 1. Tenths: 2 + 4 + 1 = 7. Ones: 2 + 1 = 3. Tens: 4 + 8 = 12. Answer: 123.726.

lessons.title: Exercise 4.4: Multiplication of Decimals
lessons.notes_html:
Multiplying decimals

To multiply by 10, 100 or 1000, move the decimal point to the right by 1, 2 or 3 places. To multiply a decimal by a whole number, first ignore the point and multiply as whole numbers, then count the decimal places in the decimal number and put the point that many places from the right in the answer.

Worked example

Multiply 0.85 by 25.

Step 1: Ignore the point and take 85. Multiply by the ones: 85 times 5 = 425.

Step 2: Multiply by the tens: 85 times 20 = 1700.

Step 3: Add the parts: 425 + 1700 = 2125.

Step 4: 0.85 has 2 decimal places, so put the point 2 places from the right in 2125.

Answer: 0.85 x 25 = 21.25.

Key points

  • Multiplying by 10, 100 or 1000 only moves the point; the digits stay the same.
  • The answer has the same number of decimal places as the decimal number you multiplied.
  • Add zeros at the front if the answer needs more places.

mcqs.q: Multiply 6.3 by 10.
mcqs.why: Multiplying by 10 moves the decimal point one place to the right. In 6.3 the point moves past the 3, giving 6.3 x 10 = 63.

mcqs.q: Multiply 0.25 by 10.
mcqs.why: Multiplying by 10 moves the decimal point one place to the right. In 0.25 the point moves to after the 2, giving 2.5, which the book writes as 2.50.

mcqs.q: Multiply 1.265 by 1000.
mcqs.why: Multiplying by 1000 moves the decimal point three places to the right. In 1.265 the point moves past 2, 6 and 5, giving 1.265 x 1000 = 1265.

mcqs.q: Multiply 6.3 by 3.
mcqs.why: Ignore the point: 63 x 3 = 189, since 60 x 3 = 180 and 3 x 3 = 9. The number 6.3 has one decimal place, so put the point one place from the right: 18.9.

mcqs.q: Multiply 0.85 by 25.
mcqs.why: Ignore the point: 85 x 5 = 425 and 85 x 20 = 1700, total 2125. The number 0.85 has two decimal places, so put the point two places from the right: 21.25.

mcqs.q: Multiply 7.9 by 13.
mcqs.why: Ignore the point: 79 x 3 = 237 and 79 x 10 = 790, total 1027. The number 7.9 has one decimal place, so put the point one place from the right: 102.7.

mcqs.q: Multiply 0.327 by 100.
mcqs.why: Multiplying by 100 moves the decimal point two places to the right. In 0.327 the point moves past 3 and 2, giving 32.7, written in the book as 32.700.

mcqs.q: Multiply 5.42 by 24.
mcqs.why: Ignore the point: 542 x 4 = 2168 and 542 x 20 = 10840, total 13008. The number 5.42 has two decimal places, so put the point two places from the right: 130.08.

mcqs.q: Multiply 3.52 by 45.
mcqs.why: Ignore the point: 352 x 5 = 1760 and 352 x 40 = 14080, total 15840. The number 3.52 has two decimal places, so the point goes two places from the right: 158.40 = 158.4.

mcqs.q: Multiply 1.834 by 11.
mcqs.why: Ignore the point: 1834 x 1 = 1834 and 1834 x 10 = 18340, total 20174. The number 1.834 has three decimal places, so put the point three places from the right: 20.174.

lessons.title: Exercise 4.5: Division of Decimals
lessons.notes_html:
Dividing decimals

Divide by long division, digit by digit. Divide the whole-number part first. When you pass the decimal point in the number being divided, put a point in the quotient in the same place, then keep bringing digits down until the remainder is 0.

Worked example

Divide 17.1 by 6.

Step 1: 17 divided by 6 is 2, since 6 times 2 = 12, remainder 5.

Step 2: Put the decimal point in the quotient and bring down 1 to make 51.

Step 3: 51 divided by 6 is 8, since 6 times 8 = 48, remainder 3.

Step 4: Bring down a 0 to make 30. 30 divided by 6 is 5, remainder 0.

Answer: 17.1 divided by 6 = 2.85.

Key points

  • The decimal point in the quotient sits exactly above the point in the number being divided.
  • If the first digit is smaller than the divisor, write 0 and then the point.
  • You can add a zero after the last decimal digit to finish the division.

mcqs.q: Divide 17.1 by 6.
mcqs.why: 17 divided by 6 is 2 (6 x 2 = 12), remainder 5. Place the point, bring down 1: 51 divided by 6 is 8 (48), remainder 3. Bring down 0: 30 divided by 6 is 5. Answer: 2.85.

mcqs.q: Divide 1.8 by 5.
mcqs.why: 1 is smaller than 5, so write 0 and place the point. Bring down 8: 18 divided by 5 is 3 (15), remainder 3. Bring down 0: 30 divided by 5 is 6. Answer: 0.36.

mcqs.q: Divide 9.36 by 4.
mcqs.why: 9 divided by 4 is 2 (8), remainder 1. Place the point, bring down 3: 13 divided by 4 is 3 (12), remainder 1. Bring down 6: 16 divided by 4 is 4. Answer: 2.34.

mcqs.q: Divide 4.68 by 9.
mcqs.why: 4 is smaller than 9, so write 0 and place the point. Bring down 6: 46 divided by 9 is 5 (45), remainder 1. Bring down 8: 18 divided by 9 is 2. Answer: 0.52.

mcqs.q: Divide 17.85 by 7.
mcqs.why: 17 divided by 7 is 2 (14), remainder 3. Place the point, bring down 8: 38 divided by 7 is 5 (35), remainder 3. Bring down 5: 35 divided by 7 is 5. Answer: 2.55.

mcqs.q: Divide 6.28 by 4.
mcqs.why: 6 divided by 4 is 1 (4), remainder 2. Place the point, bring down 2: 22 divided by 4 is 5 (20), remainder 2. Bring down 8: 28 divided by 4 is 7. Answer: 1.57.

mcqs.q: Divide 34.23 by 3.
mcqs.why: 3 divided by 3 is 1 and 4 divided by 3 is 1, remainder 1. Place the point, bring down 2: 12 divided by 3 is 4. Bring down 3: 3 divided by 3 is 1. Answer: 11.41.

mcqs.q: Divide 67.25 by 5.
mcqs.why: 6 divided by 5 is 1, remainder 1, then 17 divided by 5 is 3 (15), remainder 2. Place the point, bring down 2: 22 divided by 5 is 4 (20), remainder 2. Bring down 5: 25 divided by 5 is 5. Answer: 13.45.

mcqs.q: Divide 40.05 by 5.
mcqs.why: 40 divided by 5 is 8 exactly. Place the point, bring down 0: 0 divided by 5 is 0. Bring down 5: 5 divided by 5 is 1. Answer: 8.01.

mcqs.q: Divide 9.66 by 3.
mcqs.why: 9 divided by 3 is 3 exactly. Place the point, bring down 6: 6 divided by 3 is 2. Bring down the last 6: 6 divided by 3 is 2. Answer: 3.22.

lessons.title: Exercise 4.6: Decimal Word Problems
lessons.notes_html:
Word problems with decimals

Read the story and decide the operation. Words like total and altogether usually mean add. Words like left and how much more usually mean subtract. Equal groups of the same weight or price mean multiply, and sharing or cutting into equal parts means divide. Always write the unit, such as Rs, kg or m, in the answer.

Worked example

Ahmed purchased a shirt for Rs 325.80 and jeans for Rs 525.25. Find the amount spent.

Step 1: He spent on both items, so add the two prices with points in line.

Step 2: Hundredths: 0 + 5 = 5. Tenths: 8 + 2 = 10, write 0 and carry 1.

Step 3: Ones: 5 + 5 + 1 carried = 11, write 1 and carry 1. Tens: 2 + 2 + 1 carried = 5. Hundreds: 3 + 5 = 8.

Answer: Ahmed spent Rs 851.05 in all.

Key points

  • For two subtractions, do them one at a time, like the pocket money question.
  • For many equal items, multiply the decimal by the number of items.
  • For equal pieces or equal shares, divide the decimal by the number of parts.

mcqs.q: Ahmed bought a shirt for Rs 325.80 and jeans for Rs 525.25. How much did he spend in all?
mcqs.why: Add with points aligned: 32580 hundredths + 52525 hundredths = 85105 hundredths. Placing the point two places from the right gives Rs 851.05.

mcqs.q: Javeria weighs 10.24 kg and her sister weighs 11.28 kg. What is their total weight?
mcqs.why: Add column by column: hundredths 4 + 8 = 12, write 2 carry 1. Tenths 2 + 2 + 1 = 5. Ones 0 + 1 = 1. Tens 1 + 1 = 2. Total weight is 21.52 kg.

mcqs.q: Ansa paid Rs 97.5 in total for a pencil case and a colour box. The pencil case costs Rs 30.25. What does the colour box cost?
mcqs.why: Subtract: write 97.5 as 97.50. Hundredths: borrow, 10 - 5 = 5. Tenths: 4 - 2 = 2. Ones: 7 - 0 = 7. Tens: 9 - 3 = 6. The colour box costs Rs 67.25.

mcqs.q: Haroon and Shafique spent Rs 95.82 in all. Haroon spent Rs 89.75. How much did Shafique spend?
mcqs.why: Subtract in hundredths: 9582 - 8975 = 607 hundredths. With borrowing column by column and the point two places from the right, Shafique spent Rs 6.07.

mcqs.q: Ali has Rs 50.29. He gives Rs 15.45 to his sister and spends Rs 13.84 on coffee. How much is left?
mcqs.why: First subtraction: 50.29 - 15.45 = 34.84. Second subtraction: 34.84 - 13.84 = 21.00, since hundredths 4 - 4 = 0, tenths 8 - 8 = 0, ones 4 - 3 = 1 and tens 3 - 1 = 2. So Rs 21.00 is left.

mcqs.q: Aslam brought 65 hens. Each hen weighs 2.72 kg. What is the weight of all the hens?
mcqs.why: Multiply: ignore the point, 272 x 5 = 1360 and 272 x 60 = 16320, total 17680. The number 2.72 has two decimal places, so place the point two places from the right: 176.8 kg.

mcqs.q: One set of books weighs 3.75 kg. What is the weight of 32 such sets?
mcqs.why: Multiply: ignore the point, 375 x 2 = 750 and 375 x 30 = 11250, total 12000. The number 3.75 has two decimal places, so the answer is 120.00, that is 120 kg.

mcqs.q: Yusra cuts a ribbon 13.75 m long into 5 equal pieces. How long is each piece?
mcqs.why: Divide: 13 divided by 5 is 2 (10), remainder 3. Place the point, bring down 7: 37 divided by 5 is 7 (35), remainder 2. Bring down 5: 25 divided by 5 is 5. Each piece is 2.75 m.

mcqs.q: The total weight of 5 sacks of flour is 58.75 kg. What is the weight of one sack?
mcqs.why: Divide: 5 divided by 5 is 1 and 8 divided by 5 is 1, remainder 3. Place the point, bring down 7: 37 divided by 5 is 7 (35), remainder 2. Bring down 5: 25 divided by 5 is 5. One sack weighs 11.75 kg.

mcqs.q: The total weight of Javeria and her sister is 21.52 kg. Javeria weighs 10.24 kg. How much does her sister weigh?
mcqs.why: Subtract using the numbers from the total weight question: 21.52 - 10.24. Hundredths: borrow, 12 - 4 = 8. Tenths: 4 - 2 = 2. Ones: 1 - 0 = 1. Tens: 2 - 1 = 1. Her sister weighs 11.28 kg.

lessons.title: Review Exercise 4: Mixed Practice
lessons.notes_html:
Mixed practice

This review mixes everything in the unit: place value, changing fractions to decimals and decimals to fractions, addition and subtraction with points in line, multiplication by moving the point or counting decimal places, and division by long division. Choose the right method for each question.

Worked example

Anas ran 110.25 m and Asma ran 97.75 m. What total distance did both run altogether?

Step 1: Total means add, with the decimal points in one line.

Step 2: Hundredths: 5 + 5 = 10, write 0 and carry 1. Tenths: 2 + 7 + 1 carried = 10, write 0 and carry 1.

Step 3: Ones: 0 + 7 + 1 carried = 8. Tens: 1 + 9 = 10, write 0 and carry 1. Hundreds: 1 + 0 + 1 carried = 2.

Answer: Both ran 208 m altogether.

Key points

  • In 37.87 the digit 7 appears twice: ones value 7 and hundredths value 0.07.
  • Check every answer by asking whether its size makes sense.
  • For how much more, subtract the smaller distance from the bigger one.

mcqs.q: In 2.325, what is the value of the digit 5?
mcqs.why: In 2.325 the digit 5 is the third digit after the decimal point, in the thousandths place. Its value is 5 thousandths, which is 5/1000 = 0.005.

mcqs.q: Convert 321/100 into a decimal.
mcqs.why: The denominator 100 has two zeros, so place the decimal point two places from the right in the numerator 321. Counting back two places gives 3.21.

mcqs.q: Convert 19/4 into a decimal.
mcqs.why: Multiply numerator and denominator by 25 to make the denominator 100: 19 times 25 is 475, giving 475/100. Place the point two places from the right: 4.75.

mcqs.q: Convert 0.35 into a fraction in its simplest form.
mcqs.why: 0.35 has two decimal places, so write it as 35/100. Divide the numerator and denominator by 5: 35 divided by 5 is 7 and 100 divided by 5 is 20, giving 7/20.
Add with points aligned: hundredths 7 + 2 = 9, tenths 5 + 4 = 9 and ones 1 + 3 = 4. Keeping the point in the same column gives 4.99.
Subtract with points aligned: hundredths need borrowing, 17 - 8 = 9. Tenths after borrowing: 2 - 1 = 1. So 0.37 - 0.18 = 0.19.

mcqs.q: Multiply 0.325 by 100.
mcqs.why: Multiplying by 100 moves the decimal point two places to the right. In 0.325 the point moves past 3 and 2, giving 32.5, written in the book as 32.500.

mcqs.q: Divide 9.42 by 6.
mcqs.why: 9 divided by 6 is 1 (6), remainder 3. Place the point, bring down 4: 34 divided by 6 is 5 (30), remainder 4. Bring down 2: 42 divided by 6 is 7. Answer: 1.57.

mcqs.q: Anas ran 110.25 m and Asma ran 97.75 m. What total distance did both run altogether?
mcqs.why: Add in hundredths: 11025 + 9775 = 20800 hundredths. Column by column the carries give 208.00, so both ran 208 m altogether.

mcqs.q: Abdullah drinks 0.45 litre of juice every day. How many litres will he drink in 30 days?
mcqs.why: Multiply: ignore the point, 45 x 30 = 1350. The number 0.45 has two decimal places, so place the point two places from the right in 1350: 13.5 litres.

lessons.title: Exercise 5.1: Converting Units of Length
lessons.notes_html:
Converting Units of Length

Length is measured in kilometres, metres, centimetres and millimetres. To change a bigger unit into a smaller unit, we multiply. Remember: 1 km = 1000 m, 1 m = 100 cm and 1 cm = 10 mm. Also, 1 m = 1000 mm, because 100 cm multiplied by 10 mm gives 1000 mm.

Worked example

Change 35 m into centimetres and millimetres (Exercise 5.1, Question 4 iii).

Step 1: First convert into centimetres: 35 x 100 = 3500 cm, because 1 m = 100 cm.

Step 2: Then convert into millimetres: 35 x 1000 = 35000 mm, because 1 m = 1000 mm.

Answer: 3500 cm and 35000 mm.

Key points

  • 1 km = 1000 m, so multiply kilometres by 1000 to get metres.
  • 1 m = 100 cm, so multiply metres by 100 to get centimetres.
  • 1 cm = 10 mm, so multiply centimetres by 10 to get millimetres.
  • Always write the unit with the answer.

mcqs.q: How many metres are there in 5 km?
mcqs.why: 1 km = 1000 m, so multiply: 5 x 1000 = 5000. The answer is 5000 metres.

mcqs.q: Convert 32 m into centimetres.
mcqs.why: 1 m = 100 cm, so multiply: 32 x 100 = 3200. The answer is 3200 centimetres.

mcqs.q: Convert 15 cm into millimetres.
mcqs.why: 1 cm = 10 mm, so multiply: 15 x 10 = 150. The answer is 150 millimetres.

mcqs.q: How many metres are there in 9 km?
mcqs.why: 1 km = 1000 m, so multiply: 9 x 1000 = 9000. The answer is 9000 metres.

mcqs.q: Convert 45 m into centimetres.
mcqs.why: 1 m = 100 cm, so multiply: 45 x 100 = 4500. The answer is 4500 centimetres.

mcqs.q: Convert 49 cm into millimetres.
mcqs.why: 1 cm = 10 mm, so multiply: 49 x 10 = 490. The answer is 490 millimetres.

mcqs.q: Change 4 m into centimetres and millimetres.
mcqs.why: Centimetres: 4 x 100 = 400 cm. Millimetres: 4 x 1000 = 4000 mm, because 1 m = 1000 mm.

mcqs.q: How many metres are there in 20 km?
mcqs.why: 1 km = 1000 m, so multiply: 20 x 1000 = 20000. The answer is 20000 metres.

mcqs.q: Convert 54 m into centimetres.
mcqs.why: 1 m = 100 cm, so multiply: 54 x 100 = 5400. The answer is 5400 centimetres.

mcqs.q: Convert 30 cm into millimetres.
mcqs.why: 1 cm = 10 mm, so multiply: 30 x 10 = 300. The answer is 300 millimetres.

lessons.title: Exercise 5.2: Addition and Subtraction of Length
lessons.notes_html:
Addition and Subtraction of Length

When lengths have two units, add or subtract the same units together: metres with metres, centimetres with centimetres. If the smaller unit total reaches the bigger unit, regroup: 1000 m = 1 km and 100 cm = 1 m and 10 mm = 1 cm. For subtraction, if the top smaller unit is too small, borrow 1 from the bigger unit.

Worked example

Add 25 km 520 m and 12 km 840 m (Exercise 5.2, Question 1 ii).

Step 1: Add the m parts: 520 + 840 = 1360 m.

Step 2: Regroup: 1360 m = 1 km and 360 m, because 1 km = 1000 m; carry 1 to the km side.

Step 3: Add the km parts: 25 + 12 + 1 carried = 38 km.

Answer: 38 km 360 m.

Key points

  • Add or subtract metres with metres and centimetres with centimetres.
  • Regroup 1000 m as 1 km and 100 cm as 1 m when the smaller unit is full.
  • For subtraction, borrow 1 km as 1000 m or 1 m as 100 cm when needed.

mcqs.q: Add 4200 m and 9600 m.
mcqs.why: Both are in metres, so add in columns: 4200 + 9600 = 13800. The answer is 13800 m.

mcqs.q: Add 25 km 520 m and 12 km 840 m.
mcqs.why: Metres: 520 + 840 = 1360 m = 1 km 360 m. Kilometres: 25 + 12 + 1 carried = 38 km. Answer: 38 km 360 m.

mcqs.q: Add 69 m 17 cm and 99 m 32 cm.
mcqs.why: Centimetres: 17 + 32 = 49 cm. Metres: 69 + 99 = 168 m. The answer is 168 m 49 cm.

mcqs.q: Add 42 cm 3 mm and 68 cm 5 mm.
mcqs.why: Millimetres: 3 + 5 = 8 mm. Centimetres: 42 + 68 = 110 cm. The answer is 110 cm 8 mm.

mcqs.q: Subtract 5050 m from 7000 m.
mcqs.why: Subtract in columns with borrowing: 7000 - 5050 = 1950. The answer is 1950 m.

mcqs.q: Subtract 2 m 76 cm from 6 m 35 cm.
mcqs.why: Borrow 1 m = 100 cm: cm part becomes 135 and m part becomes 5. Centimetres: 135 - 76 = 59 cm. Metres: 5 - 2 = 3 m. Answer: 3 m 59 cm.

mcqs.q: Subtract 36 km 500 m from 87 km 250 m.
mcqs.why: Borrow 1 km = 1000 m: m part becomes 1250 and km part becomes 86. Metres: 1250 - 500 = 750 m. Kilometres: 86 - 36 = 50 km. Answer: 50 km 750 m.

mcqs.q: Subtract 18 km 352 m from 70 km 100 m.
mcqs.why: Borrow 1 km = 1000 m: m part becomes 1100 and km part becomes 69. Metres: 1100 - 352 = 748 m. Kilometres: 69 - 18 = 51 km. Answer: 51 km 748 m.

mcqs.q: Subtract 27 cm 8 mm from 74 cm 7 mm.
mcqs.why: Borrow 1 cm = 10 mm: mm part becomes 17 and cm part becomes 73. Millimetres: 17 - 8 = 9 mm. Centimetres: 73 - 27 = 46 cm. Answer: 46 cm 9 mm.

mcqs.q: Add 90 km 820 m, 75 km 500 m and 110 km 175 m.
mcqs.why: Metres: 820 + 500 + 175 = 1495 m = 1 km 495 m. Kilometres: 90 + 75 + 110 + 1 carried = 276 km. Answer: 276 km 495 m.

lessons.title: Exercise 5.3: Length Word Problems
lessons.notes_html:
Length Word Problems

Read the story carefully and decide whether to add or subtract. Words like total and altogether usually mean add. Words like left, difference and how much more usually mean subtract. Choose a sensible unit: mm and cm for small things, m for rooms and grounds, and km for distances between cities.

Worked example

Ali covered 789 m from his house to Jamia Masjid and then 368 m from Jamia Masjid to School. What is the total distance covered? (Exercise 5.3, Question 3)

Step 1: Ali went from home to the mosque and then to school, so add the two distances.

Step 2: Add in columns: ones 9 + 8 = 17, write 7 and carry 1; tens 8 + 6 + 1 carried = 15, write 5 and carry 1; hundreds 7 + 3 + 1 carried = 11.

Answer: Ali covered 1157 m in all.

Key points

  • Total distance means add the parts together.
  • Distance left or difference means subtract the smaller from the bigger.
  • The thickness of an eraser is measured in cm, a football ground in m, and the Karachi to Hyderabad road distance in km.

mcqs.q: What is the best measure for the thickness of an eraser?
mcqs.why: An eraser is a small object. Millimetres are too tiny for its thickness here and metres and kilometres are far too big, so 2 cm is the best measure.

mcqs.q: What is the best measure for the length of a football ground?
mcqs.why: A football ground is large but not city-size. Millimetres and centimetres are too small and kilometres are too big, so 30 m is the best measure.

mcqs.q: What is the best measure for the distance between Karachi and Hyderabad by road?
mcqs.why: The distance between two cities is very large, so it is measured in kilometres. The best measure is 165 km.

mcqs.q: An iron rod is 2 m 86 cm long. How much is left if 1 m 38 cm is cut off?
mcqs.why: Centimetres: 86 - 38 = 48 cm. Metres: 2 - 1 = 1 m. The length left is 1 m 48 cm.

mcqs.q: Ali covered 789 m to Jamia Masjid and then 368 m to school. What is the total distance?
mcqs.why: Add the two distances: 789 + 368. Ones: 9 + 8 = 17, carry 1. Tens: 8 + 6 + 1 = 15, carry 1. Hundreds: 7 + 3 + 1 = 11. Total is 1157 m.

mcqs.q: A car is 1 m 62 cm wide and a garage is 2 m 41 cm wide. How much space is left when the car is in the garage?
mcqs.why: Borrow 1 m = 100 cm: cm part becomes 141 and m part becomes 1. Centimetres: 141 - 62 = 79 cm. Metres: 1 - 1 = 0 m. Space left is 79 cm.

mcqs.q: The red part of a pencil is 65 mm and the blue part is 52 mm. What is the full length?
mcqs.why: Add the parts: 65 + 52 = 117 mm. Convert: 10 mm = 1 cm, so 117 mm = 11 cm and 7 mm left over.

mcqs.q: Tariq ran 9 km 200 m and Sajjad ran 8 km 850 m. How far ahead was Tariq?
mcqs.why: Borrow 1 km = 1000 m: m part becomes 1200 and km part becomes 8. Metres: 1200 - 850 = 350 m. Kilometres: 8 - 8 = 0 km. Tariq was 350 m ahead.

mcqs.q: In a 10 km race, a horse fell 245 m from the winning point. What distance had it run?
mcqs.why: Convert first: 10 km = 10 x 1000 = 10000 m. Subtract: 10000 - 245 = 9755 m, which is 9 km 755 m.

mcqs.q: Nasir is 142 cm tall. His friend is 8 cm taller. How tall is his friend?
mcqs.why: The friend is taller, so add: 142 + 8. Ones: 2 + 8 = 10, write 0 and carry 1. Tens: 4 + 0 + 1 carried = 5. Hundreds: 1. The friend is 150 cm tall.

lessons.title: Exercise 5.4: Mass — Addition and Subtraction
lessons.notes_html:
Mass: Addition and Subtraction

Mass is measured in kilograms and grams. Remember: 1 kg = 1000 g. To convert kilograms into grams, multiply by 1000. Add or subtract grams with grams and kilograms with kilograms. Regroup 1000 g as 1 kg, and borrow 1 kg as 1000 g when subtracting.

Worked example

Add 4 kg 485 g, 2 kg 390 g and 4 kg 425 g (Exercise 5.4, Question 1 ii).

Step 1: Add the g parts: 485 + 390 + 425 = 1300 g.

Step 2: Regroup: 1300 g = 1 kg and 300 g, because 1 kg = 1000 g; carry 1 to the kg side.

Step 3: Add the kg parts: 4 + 2 + 4 + 1 carried = 11 kg.

Answer: 11 kg 300 g.

Key points

  • 1 kg = 1000 g, so 18 kg = 18000 g and 4 kg 80 g = 4080 g.
  • Light things like a silver ring and one soap are measured in grams.
  • Heavy things like bags of flour, sugar, potatoes and salt are measured in kilograms.

mcqs.q: Convert 18 kg into grams.
mcqs.why: 1 kg = 1000 g, so multiply: 18 x 1000 = 18000. The answer is 18000 grams.

mcqs.q: Convert 4 kg 80 g into grams.
mcqs.why: Convert the kg part: 4 x 1000 = 4000 g. Add the extra grams: 4000 + 80 = 4080 g.
Add in columns: ones 5 + 6 + 0 = 11, carry 1. Tens 0 + 3 + 0 + 1 = 4. Hundreds 7 + 5 + 0 = 12, carry 1. Thousands 3 + 8 + 4 + 1 = 16. Total is 16241 g.

mcqs.q: Add 4 kg 485 g, 2 kg 390 g and 4 kg 425 g.
mcqs.why: Grams: 485 + 390 + 425 = 1300 g = 1 kg 300 g. Kilograms: 4 + 2 + 4 + 1 carried = 11 kg. Answer: 11 kg 300 g.

mcqs.q: Add 8 kg 75 g and 9 kg 46 g.
mcqs.why: Grams: 75 + 46 = 121 g. Kilograms: 8 + 9 = 17 kg. The answer is 17 kg 121 g.

mcqs.q: Add 16 kg 860 g, 23 kg 545 g and 49 kg 360 g.
mcqs.why: Grams: 860 + 545 + 360 = 1765 g = 1 kg 765 g. Kilograms: 16 + 23 + 49 + 1 carried = 89 kg. Answer: 89 kg 765 g.

mcqs.q: Subtract 1 kg 250 g from 5 kg.
mcqs.why: Borrow 1 kg = 1000 g: g part becomes 1000 and kg part becomes 4. Grams: 1000 - 250 = 750 g. Kilograms: 4 - 1 = 3 kg. Answer: 3 kg 750 g.

mcqs.q: Subtract 4505 g from 9007 g.
mcqs.why: Subtract in columns with borrowing: 9007 - 4505 = 4502. The answer is 4502 g.

mcqs.q: Subtract 36 kg 740 g from 59 kg 960 g.
mcqs.why: Grams: 960 - 740 = 220 g. Kilograms: 59 - 36 = 23 kg. The answer is 23 kg 220 g.

mcqs.q: Subtract 14 kg 72 g from 20 kg 40 g.
mcqs.why: Borrow 1 kg = 1000 g: g part becomes 1040 and kg part becomes 19. Grams: 1040 - 72 = 968 g. Kilograms: 19 - 14 = 5 kg. Answer: 5 kg 968 g.

lessons.title: Exercise 5.5: Mass Word Problems
lessons.notes_html:
Mass Word Problems

In mass word problems, choose the sensible unit first: very light things are measured in grams and heavier things in kilograms. For total mass, add the masses. For how much lighter or how much is left, subtract, borrowing 1 kg as 1000 g when the grams part is too small.

Worked example

Hussain weighs 28 kg 750 g and his father weighs 63 kg 500 g. How much lighter is Hussain than his father? (Exercise 5.5, Question 3)

Step 1: Borrow 1 kg: 1 kg = 1000 g; now the g part is 1500 and the kg part is 62.

Step 2: Subtract the g parts: 1500 - 750 = 750 g.

Step 3: Subtract the kg parts: 62 - 28 = 34 kg.

Answer: 34 kg 750 g.

Key points

  • A paper clip is about 1 g and a 13 years old boy is about 40 kg.
  • A box of tea is about 400 g and a watermelon is about 5 kg.
  • Total weight means add; lighter than and left over mean subtract.

mcqs.q: What is the best measure for the mass of a paper clip?
mcqs.why: A paper clip is very light, so it is measured in grams. Among the choices, 1 g is the sensible mass for a paper clip.

mcqs.q: What is the best measure for the mass of a 13 years old boy?
mcqs.why: A boy is heavy, so grams are far too small. 4 kg is too light for a 13 years old boy, so 40 kg is the best measure.

mcqs.q: What is the best measure for the mass of a box of tea?
mcqs.why: A box of tea is light but much heavier than a few grams, and 4 kg is too heavy for one box, so 400 g is the best measure.

mcqs.q: What is the best measure for the weight of a watermelon?
mcqs.why: A watermelon is heavy, so it is measured in kilograms. 50 kg is far too heavy and the gram choices are too light, so 5 kg is best.

mcqs.q: Which unit is best for the mass of a silver ring?
mcqs.why: A silver ring is very light, so its mass is measured in grams. Kilograms are for heavy things, and litre and metre do not measure mass.

mcqs.q: Which unit is best for the mass of one soap?
mcqs.why: One soap is light, so its mass is measured in grams. Bags of flour and sugar are measured in kilograms instead.

mcqs.q: A bale of rubber weighs 75 kg 700 g and another weighs 86 kg 400 g. Find the total weight.
mcqs.why: Grams: 700 + 400 = 1100 g = 1 kg 100 g. Kilograms: 75 + 86 + 1 carried = 162 kg. Total weight is 162 kg 100 g.

mcqs.q: Hussain weighs 28 kg 750 g and his father weighs 63 kg 500 g. How much lighter is Hussain?
mcqs.why: Borrow 1 kg = 1000 g: g part becomes 1500 and kg part becomes 62. Grams: 1500 - 750 = 750 g. Kilograms: 62 - 28 = 34 kg. Answer: 34 kg 750 g.

mcqs.q: Fozia bought 21 kg 350 g of sweet from one shop and 1 kg 200 g from another. What is the total weight?
mcqs.why: Grams: 350 + 200 = 550 g. Kilograms: 21 + 1 = 22 kg. The total weight of sweet is 22 kg 550 g.

mcqs.q: A grain merchant had 3000 kg of peas and sold 1856 kg 750 g. What weight of peas was left?
mcqs.why: Borrow 1 kg = 1000 g: g part becomes 1000 and kg part becomes 2999. Grams: 1000 - 750 = 250 g. Kilograms: 2999 - 1856 = 1143 kg. Left: 1143 kg 250 g.

lessons.title: Exercise 5.6: Volume — Addition and Subtraction
lessons.notes_html:
Volume: Addition and Subtraction

Volume or capacity is measured in litres and millilitres. Remember: 1 litre = 1000 ml. To convert litres into millilitres, multiply by 1000. Add or subtract millilitres with millilitres and litres with litres. Regroup 1000 ml as 1 litre, and borrow 1 litre as 1000 ml when subtracting.

Worked example

Add 14 l 782 ml, 17 l 300 ml and 26 l 450 ml (Exercise 5.6, Question 1 v).

Step 1: Add the ml parts: 782 + 300 + 450 = 1532 ml.

Step 2: Regroup: 1532 ml = 1 l and 532 ml, because 1 l = 1000 ml; carry 1 to the l side.

Step 3: Add the l parts: 14 + 17 + 26 + 1 carried = 58 l.

Answer: 58 l 532 ml.

Key points

  • 1 litre = 1000 ml, so 15 l = 15000 ml and 40 l = 40000 ml.
  • A cold drink bottle holds about 250 ml and a milk pack holds about 1 litre.
  • A drink can holds about 360 ml.

mcqs.q: Convert 15 litres into millilitres.
mcqs.why: 1 litre = 1000 ml, so multiply: 15 x 1000 = 15000. The answer is 15000 millilitres.

mcqs.q: Add 7 l 420 ml and 10 l 500 ml.
mcqs.why: Millilitres: 420 + 500 = 920 ml. Litres: 7 + 10 = 17 l. The answer is 17 l 920 ml.

mcqs.q: Add 2100 ml, 4960 ml and 3755 ml.
mcqs.why: Add in columns: ones 0 + 0 + 5 = 5. Tens 0 + 6 + 5 = 11, carry 1. Hundreds 1 + 9 + 7 + 1 = 18, carry 1. Thousands 2 + 4 + 3 + 1 = 10. Total is 10815 ml.

mcqs.q: Add 705 ml, 820 ml and 695 ml.
mcqs.why: Add in columns: ones 5 + 0 + 5 = 10, carry 1. Tens 0 + 2 + 9 + 1 = 12, carry 1. Hundreds 7 + 8 + 6 + 1 = 22. Total is 2220 ml, that is 2 l 220 ml.

mcqs.q: Add 14 l 782 ml, 17 l 300 ml and 26 l 450 ml.
mcqs.why: Millilitres: 782 + 300 + 450 = 1532 ml = 1 l 532 ml. Litres: 14 + 17 + 26 + 1 carried = 58 l. Answer: 58 l 532 ml.

mcqs.q: Subtract 719 l from 825 l.
mcqs.why: Subtract in columns with borrowing: 825 - 719 = 106. The answer is 106 litres.

mcqs.q: Subtract 16 l 415 ml from 60 l 600 ml.
mcqs.why: Millilitres: 600 - 415 = 185 ml. Litres: 60 - 16 = 44 l. The answer is 44 l 185 ml.

mcqs.q: Subtract 8 l 205 ml from 11 l 150 ml.
mcqs.why: Borrow 1 l = 1000 ml: ml part becomes 1150 and l part becomes 10. Millilitres: 1150 - 205 = 945 ml. Litres: 10 - 8 = 2 l. Answer: 2 l 945 ml.

mcqs.q: Subtract 640 ml from 905 ml.
mcqs.why: Subtract in columns with borrowing: 905 - 640 = 265. The answer is 265 ml.

mcqs.q: What is the appropriate measure for a cold drink bottle?
mcqs.why: A cold drink bottle holds much more than 25 ml but much less than litres. The appropriate measure given in the activity is 250 ml.

lessons.title: Exercise 5.7: Volume Word Problems
lessons.notes_html:
Volume Word Problems

In volume word problems, choose the sensible unit first: small bottles are measured in millilitres and big containers in litres. For total quantity, add. For how much is left or how much more is needed, subtract, borrowing 1 litre as 1000 ml when the millilitres part is too small.

Worked example

A container contains 98 l 300 ml of oil. If 51 l 700 ml more is added, how much oil will there be altogether? (Exercise 5.7, Question 4)

Step 1: Add the ml parts: 300 + 700 = 1000 ml.

Step 2: Regroup: 1000 ml = 1 l and 0 ml, because 1 l = 1000 ml; carry 1 to the l side.

Step 3: Add the l parts: 98 + 51 + 1 carried = 150 l.

Answer: 150 l.

Key points

  • An oil tin holds about 4 l and a juice carton holds about 1 l.
  • A milk jug holds about 4 l and a small medicine bottle holds about 5 ml.
  • Left over and needed more mean subtract; altogether means add.

mcqs.q: What is the best measure for an oil tin?
mcqs.why: An oil tin holds a few litres of oil. 40 l and 400 l are far too big and 4 ml is only a few drops, so 4 l is the best measure.

mcqs.q: What is the best measure for a juice carton?
mcqs.why: A juice carton holds about one litre. Millilitre choices are only a few drops and 10 l is far too big, so 1 l is the best measure.

mcqs.q: What is the best measure for a milk jug?
mcqs.why: A milk jug holds a few litres of milk. The millilitre choices are far too small and 400 l is far too big, so 4 l is the best measure.

mcqs.q: What is the best measure for a small medicine bottle?
mcqs.why: A small medicine bottle holds only a few millilitres. Litre choices are far too big, so 5 ml is the best measure.

mcqs.q: How much water is left if 19 ml are taken from a cup holding 28 ml?
mcqs.why: Subtract because water is taken out: 28 - 19. Borrow: ones become 18 - 9 = 9, tens become 1 - 1 = 0. Water left is 9 ml.

mcqs.q: A bath tub needs 850 l to fill and now holds 552 l. How many more litres are needed?
mcqs.why: Subtract: 850 - 552. Ones: borrow, 10 - 2 = 8. Tens: 14 - 5 = 9 after borrowing. Hundreds: 7 - 5 = 2. Needed: 298 more litres.

mcqs.q: A container has 98 l 300 ml of oil and 51 l 700 ml more is added. How much oil is there altogether?
mcqs.why: Millilitres: 300 + 700 = 1000 ml = 1 l 0 ml. Litres: 98 + 51 + 1 carried = 150 l. Altogether there is 150 l of oil.

mcqs.q: A milk van carried 272 l of milk and 35 l 875 ml was spilt. How much milk was left?
mcqs.why: Borrow 1 l = 1000 ml: ml part becomes 1000 and l part becomes 271. Millilitres: 1000 - 875 = 125 ml. Litres: 271 - 35 = 236 l. Left: 236 l 125 ml.

mcqs.q: One bottle has 1 l 10 ml of syrup and another has 2 l 75 ml. Find the total quantity.
mcqs.why: Millilitres: 10 + 75 = 85 ml. Litres: 1 + 2 = 3 l. The total quantity of syrup is 3 l 85 ml.

mcqs.q: A bus tank has 80 l 750 ml of diesel. How much diesel must be added to make it 100 l?
mcqs.why: Borrow 1 l = 1000 ml: ml part becomes 1000 and l part becomes 99. Millilitres: 1000 - 750 = 250 ml. Litres: 99 - 80 = 19 l. Add 19 l 250 ml.

lessons.title: Review Exercise 5: Mixed Practice
lessons.notes_html:
Review: Mixed Practice

This review mixes length, mass and volume. Remember all the conversion facts: 1 cm = 10 mm, 1 km = 1000 m, 1 m = 100 cm, 1 kg = 1000 g and 1 litre = 1000 ml. To change metres into kilometres, divide by 1000. Add and subtract same units together, regrouping or borrowing as needed.

Worked example

Add 48 m 65 cm and 38 m 76 cm (Review Exercise 5, Question 5 ii).

Step 1: Add the cm parts: 65 + 76 = 141 cm.

Step 2: Regroup: 141 cm = 1 m and 41 cm, because 1 m = 100 cm; carry 1 to the m side.

Step 3: Add the m parts: 48 + 38 + 1 carried = 87 m.

Answer: 87 m 41 cm.

Key points

  • 6000 m = 6 km and 3500 m = 3 km 500 m, that is 3.5 km.
  • Long distances like home to school, city to city, motorways and village to village are measured in kilometres.
  • Always regroup 1000 of the small unit as 1 of the bigger unit.

mcqs.q: 1 centimetre is equal to how many millimetres?
mcqs.why: The conversion fact is 1 cm = 10 mm. So 1 centimetre is equal to 10 millimetres.

mcqs.q: 1 kilometre is equal to how many metres?
mcqs.why: The conversion fact is 1 km = 1000 m. So 1 kilometre is equal to 1000 metres.

mcqs.q: 1 litre is equal to how many millilitres?
mcqs.why: The conversion fact is 1 litre = 1000 ml. So 1 litre is equal to 1000 millilitres.

mcqs.q: Convert 6000 m into kilometres.
mcqs.why: To change metres into kilometres, divide by 1000 because 1 km = 1000 m. Working: 6000 divided by 1000 = 6. Answer: 6 km.

mcqs.q: Convert 3500 m into kilometres.
mcqs.why: Divide by 1000 because 1 km = 1000 m. Working: 3500 divided by 1000 = 3 remainder 500, so 3500 m = 3 km 500 m, that is 3.5 km.

mcqs.q: Convert 15 km into metres.
mcqs.why: 1 km = 1000 m, so multiply: 15 x 1000 = 15000. The answer is 15000 metres.

mcqs.q: Add 30 km 43 m and 18 km 84 m.
mcqs.why: Metres: 43 + 84 = 127 m. Kilometres: 30 + 18 = 48 km. The answer is 48 km 127 m.

mcqs.q: Add 13 l 800 ml and 12 l 700 ml.
mcqs.why: Millilitres: 800 + 700 = 1500 ml = 1 l 500 ml. Litres: 13 + 12 + 1 carried = 26 l. Answer: 26 l 500 ml.

mcqs.q: Add 44 kg 380 g and 38 kg 960 g.
mcqs.why: Grams: 380 + 960 = 1340 g = 1 kg 340 g. Kilograms: 44 + 38 + 1 carried = 83 kg. Answer: 83 kg 340 g.

mcqs.q: Subtract 45 kg 325 g from 86 kg 638 g.
mcqs.why: Grams: 638 - 325 = 313 g. Kilograms: 86 - 45 = 41 kg. The answer is 41 kg 313 g.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.1: Measuring Sides
lessons.notes_html:
Measuring sides with a ruler

To measure a side, place the zero of the ruler at one end of the side and read the mark at the other end. The length is written with the letter m, for example m AB means the measure of side AB. A pair of dividers can check the same length: put the divider points on both ends and compare with the ruler.

Worked example

Measure the sides of triangle ABC.

Step 1: Place the zero of the ruler at one end of AC and read up to the other end: m AC = 3 cm.

Step 2: Measure AB in the same way: m AB = 5.6 cm.

Step 3: Measure CB in the same way: m CB = 3.5 cm.

Answer: m AC = 3 cm, m AB = 5.6 cm and m CB = 3.5 cm.

Key points

  • Always start measuring from the zero mark of the ruler.
  • In quadrilateral PQRS, m PQ = 5.4 cm, m QR = 5.4 cm, m RS = 2.6 cm and m SP = 3.3 cm.
  • The opposite sides of a rectangle are equal: in rectangle WXYZ, m WX = m YZ = 2.7 cm and m XY = m ZW = 3.5 cm.
  • Segments measured in the book: PQ = 8.5 cm, ST = 7.9 cm, FG = 9.1 cm, YZ = 10 cm and MN = 10.6 cm.

mcqs.q: In triangle ABC, what is the measure of side AC?
mcqs.why: Place the zero of the ruler at one end of AC and read the other end. The reading is 3 cm, so m AC = 3 cm.

mcqs.q: In triangle ABC, what is the measure of side AB?
mcqs.why: Place the zero of the ruler at A and read up to B. The reading is 5.6 cm, so m AB = 5.6 cm.

mcqs.q: In triangle ABC, what is the measure of side CB?
mcqs.why: Place the zero of the ruler at C and read up to B. The reading is 3.5 cm, so m CB = 3.5 cm.

mcqs.q: In quadrilateral PQRS, what is m PQ?
mcqs.why: Measure side PQ with the ruler from zero at P to Q. The reading is 5.4 cm, so m PQ = 5.4 cm.

mcqs.q: In quadrilateral PQRS, what is m RS?
mcqs.why: Measure side RS with the ruler from zero at R to S. The reading is 2.6 cm, so m RS = 2.6 cm.

mcqs.q: In quadrilateral PQRS, what is m SP?
mcqs.why: Measure side SP with the ruler from zero at S to P. The reading is 3.3 cm, so m SP = 3.3 cm.

mcqs.q: In rectangle WXYZ, what is m XY?
mcqs.why: The opposite sides of a rectangle are equal. XY is opposite ZW and both measure 3.5 cm, so m XY = 3.5 cm.

mcqs.q: What is the length of segment ST when the points are joined and measured?
mcqs.why: Join S and T, then measure with the ruler from zero. The reading is 7.9 cm, and the dividers check gives the same length, so m ST = 7.9 cm.

mcqs.q: What is the first step in measuring a side with a ruler?
options: Place the zero of the ruler at one end of the side
Place the middle of the ruler at one end
Hold the ruler above the side without touching it
mcqs.why: The book method starts by placing the zero of the ruler at one end of the side, then reading the mark at the other end.

mcqs.q: How are dividers used to verify the length of a segment?
options: They draw a circle around the segment
Their points are put on both ends and the opening is checked on the ruler
They measure the angles of the segment
They draw a line parallel to the segment
mcqs.why: Put the divider points exactly on both ends of the segment, then check that opening on the ruler. If it matches the measured length, the length is verified.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.2: Drawing Segments of Given Lengths and Measuring
lessons.notes_html:
Drawing a segment of a given length

With a ruler only: mark a point, place the zero of the ruler there, mark a second point at the required length and join them. With ruler and dividers: open the dividers to the required length on the ruler, transfer that distance to the paper, mark two points and join them. A curved line cannot be measured directly with a ruler, so we use a thread or walk the dividers in small steps along the curve.

Worked example

Draw a line segment AB of 7.4 cm, and measure the curved line ABC.

Step 1: With a ruler, mark a point, place zero there, mark a second point at 7.4 cm and join them: AB = 7.4 cm.

Step 2: With dividers, open them to 7.4 cm on the ruler, transfer the distance, mark two points and join them.

Step 3: For the curved line ABC, lay the thread carefully along the curve, mark its ends, straighten the thread and measure it with the ruler: 9.6 cm.

Answer: Segment AB of 7.4 cm is drawn, and the curved line ABC measures 9.6 cm.

Key points

  • Segments drawn in the book: AB = 7.4 cm, BC = 6.6 cm, CD = 5.7 cm, DE = 3.8 cm, EF = 4.9 cm and PQ = 6.0 cm.
  • Curved line PQRS measured by walking dividers is 10.5 cm.
  • Curved lines measured with thread: CD = 4.2 cm, EF = 4.7 cm and PK = 4.3 cm.

mcqs.q: Using a ruler, a segment AB is drawn from zero to the 7.4 cm mark. What is m AB?
mcqs.why: The second point is marked at 7.4 cm from the zero point and the points are joined, so the segment measures 0 to 7.4, which is 7.4 cm.

mcqs.q: What length of segment BC is drawn in Exercise 6.2?
mcqs.why: The dividers and ruler are set to the given length for BC. The mark is made at 6.6 cm, so segment BC measures 6.6 cm.

mcqs.q: What length of segment CD is drawn in Exercise 6.2?
mcqs.why: The second point for CD is marked at 5.7 cm from zero and joined to the first point, so segment CD measures 5.7 cm.

mcqs.q: What length of segment DE is drawn in Exercise 6.2?
mcqs.why: The second point for DE is marked at 3.8 cm from zero and joined to the first point, so segment DE measures 3.8 cm.

mcqs.q: What length of segment EF is drawn in Exercise 6.2?
mcqs.why: The second point for EF is marked at 4.9 cm from zero and joined to the first point, so segment EF measures 4.9 cm.

mcqs.q: What length of segment PQ is drawn in Exercise 6.2?
mcqs.why: The second point for PQ is marked at 6.0 cm from zero and joined to the first point, so segment PQ measures 6.0 cm.

mcqs.q: The curved line ABC is measured with thread and ruler. What is its length?
mcqs.why: Lay the thread along the whole curve ABC, mark its ends, straighten it and measure with the ruler. The straightened thread reads 9.6 cm.

mcqs.q: The curved line PQRS is measured by walking dividers along it. What is its length?
mcqs.why: Walk small divider steps along the whole curve PQRS, count the steps and multiply by the divider opening measured on the ruler. The total comes to 10.5 cm.

mcqs.q: What is the length of the curved line CD in Exercise 6.2 Question 2?
mcqs.why: Lay the thread along curved line CD, mark the ends, straighten the thread and measure it with the ruler. The reading is 4.2 cm.

mcqs.q: How is a curved line measured with a thread and a ruler?
options: Guess the length by looking at it
Lay the thread along the curve, straighten it and measure it with the ruler
Measure the straight distance between its ends only
Count the points on the curve
mcqs.why: A ruler cannot bend along a curve, so the thread is laid along the curve first. When the thread is straightened, the ruler measures its full length.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.3: Directions and Horizontal/Vertical Lines
lessons.notes_html:
Horizontal and vertical lines

A horizontal line is a lying line. It shows the West and East directions, so West to East represents a horizontal line. A vertical line is a standing line. It shows the North and South directions, so North to South represents a vertical line.

Worked example

Fill in the blanks: Horizontal line shows ____ directions. North to South direction represents ____ line.

Step 1: A horizontal line runs from West to East, so it shows West and East directions.

Step 2: North to South is the standing direction, so it represents a vertical line.

Answer: Horizontal line shows West and East directions; North to South represents a vertical line.

Key points

  • Horizontal line: West and East directions.
  • Vertical line: North and South directions.
  • West to East represents a horizontal line.
  • North to South represents a vertical line.

mcqs.q: A horizontal line shows which directions?
mcqs.why: A horizontal line is the lying line that runs from West to East, so it shows the West and East directions.

mcqs.q: A vertical line shows which directions?
mcqs.why: A vertical line is the standing line that runs from North to South, so it shows the North and South directions.

mcqs.q: North to South direction represents which line?
mcqs.why: North and South are the directions of the standing line, so North to South direction represents a vertical line.

mcqs.q: West to East direction represents which line?
mcqs.why: West and East are the directions of the lying line, so West to East direction represents a horizontal line.

mcqs.q: East to West direction represents which line?
mcqs.why: East to West is the same lying direction as West to East, only reversed, so it still represents a horizontal line.

mcqs.q: South to North direction represents which line?
mcqs.why: South to North is the same standing direction as North to South, only reversed, so it still represents a vertical line.

mcqs.q: Which line is a lying line like the West to East direction?
mcqs.why: The lying line is the horizontal line, and the book links it with the West and East directions.

mcqs.q: Which line is a standing line like the North to South direction?
mcqs.why: The standing line is the vertical line, and the book links it with the North and South directions.

mcqs.q: Which pair of directions belongs to a horizontal line?
mcqs.why: The horizontal line shows West and East. North and South belong to the vertical line, not the horizontal line.

mcqs.q: Which pair of directions belongs to a vertical line?
mcqs.why: The vertical line shows North and South. West and East belong to the horizontal line, not the vertical line.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.4: Parallel and Non-Parallel Lines
lessons.notes_html:
Parallel and non-parallel lines

Parallel lines go in the same direction, they never meet, and the distance between them stays the same everywhere. Lines that would meet or cut each other are non-parallel lines. The opposite sides of a rectangle, a square, a trapezium and a rhombus are parallel, while the sides of a triangle are not parallel.

Worked example

Are line AB and line CD parallel? Both lines are horizontal.

Step 1: Look at the direction of both lines: both are horizontal, going in the same direction.

Step 2: Parallel lines never meet and the distance between them stays the same everywhere.

Answer: Line AB and line CD are parallel lines.

Key points

  • Both slanting the same way, both horizontal or both vertical means parallel.
  • Different directions, for example horizontal with vertical, means non-parallel.
  • XY is horizontal, so only the horizontal line WV is parallel to it.
  • LM is horizontal; DE is slanting, so only DE is crossed as non-parallel to LM.

mcqs.q: What is true about parallel lines?
options: They never meet and the distance between them stays the same
mcqs.why: By definition in the book, parallel lines never meet and the distance between them stays the same everywhere.

mcqs.q: Line AB and line CD are both horizontal. They are:
mcqs.why: Both lines go in the same horizontal direction and never meet, with the same distance between them, so they are parallel lines.

mcqs.q: Line EF is horizontal and line GH is slanting. They are:
mcqs.why: Their directions are different, so they would meet if extended. Lines that would meet are non-parallel lines.

mcqs.q: Line MN and line OP are both slanting the same way. They are:
mcqs.why: Both lines slant in exactly the same direction and never meet, so line MN and line OP are parallel lines.

mcqs.q: Line WU and line VX are both vertical. They are:
mcqs.why: Both lines stand in the same vertical direction and the distance between them stays the same, so they are parallel lines.

mcqs.q: Line QS is horizontal and line RT is vertical. They are:
mcqs.why: A horizontal line and a vertical line have different directions and would cut each other, so they are non-parallel lines.

mcqs.q: Which shape has parallel opposite sides in the book activity?
mcqs.why: The opposite sides of a rectangle never meet, so the rectangle is crossed in the activity as a shape with parallel lines.

mcqs.q: Which shape is ticked as non-parallel in the book activity?
mcqs.why: The sides of a triangle cut each other and are not parallel, so the triangle is ticked as non-parallel in the activity.

mcqs.q: XY is a horizontal line. AB and CD are slanting and WV is horizontal. Which line is parallel to XY?
mcqs.why: Only a line in the same direction as XY can be parallel to it. WV is horizontal like XY, while AB and CD are slanting and would cut XY.

mcqs.q: LM is horizontal. ZA and MN are horizontal and DE is slanting. Which line is crossed as non-parallel to LM?
mcqs.why: ZA and MN are horizontal like LM, so they are parallel to it. DE is slanting and would cut LM, so only DE is crossed.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.5: Drawing Lines with Set Squares
lessons.notes_html:
Drawing lines with set squares

Two set squares are used together. To draw a vertical line on a horizontal line, place the right-angle corner of a set square on the horizontal line with one side along it, and draw along the other side. To draw a parallel line, place the longest side of one set square on the given line, hold the second set square firmly against it, slide the first set square to the new place and draw along its longest side.

Worked example

Draw a vertical line PQ on a given horizontal line XY using set squares.

Step 1: Place the right-angle corner of a set square on XY so that one side lies along XY.

Step 2: Draw a line upward along the other, vertical, side and name it PQ.

Step 3: Check: PQ and XY make a right angle of 90 degrees between them.

Answer: The vertical line PQ has been drawn on XY.

Key points

  • For a parallel line through a given point E, slide the set square until its longest side reaches point E, then draw the line and name it AB; AB is parallel to CD.
  • The second set square is held firm so the first one slides without turning.
  • A vertical line and a horizontal line meet at a right angle of 90 degrees.

mcqs.q: To draw a vertical line PQ on horizontal line XY, where is the set square placed first?
options: Its longest side is placed on point P only
Its right-angle corner is placed on XY with one side along XY
It is placed anywhere near XY
It is placed on the protractor
mcqs.why: The book method places the right-angle corner of the set square on XY so that one side lies along XY, then the other side gives the vertical direction.

mcqs.q: After drawing PQ on XY with a set square, what angle do PQ and XY make?
mcqs.why: PQ is vertical and XY is horizontal, and the set square corner used is the right-angle corner. A right angle measures exactly 90 degrees.

mcqs.q: To draw a line parallel to PQ with set squares, what is placed on PQ first?
options: The longest side of one set square
mcqs.why: The book method places the longest side of one set square exactly on the given line PQ before sliding it to draw the parallel line.

mcqs.q: Why is the second set square used when drawing a parallel line?
options: It is held firm so the first set square can slide along it without turning
It measures the length of the line
mcqs.why: The second set square is placed against the first and held firm. Sliding the first set square along it keeps the direction the same, so the new line stays parallel.

mcqs.q: To draw AB through point E parallel to CD, when do you stop sliding the set square?
options: When it reaches the end of the page
When its longest side reaches point E
mcqs.why: The set square on CD is slid along the second set square until its longest side reaches the given point E. The line drawn then passes through E and is parallel to CD.

mcqs.q: The line drawn through E in Exercise 6.5 Question 3 is named:
mcqs.why: In Question 3 the required line through point E, parallel to CD, is named AB after it is drawn along the set square edge.

mcqs.q: The line drawn parallel to PQ in Exercise 6.5 Question 2 is named:
mcqs.why: In Question 2 the new line drawn parallel to the given line PQ is named YZ in the book solution.

mcqs.q: Which side of the set square is used to draw the parallel line after sliding?
mcqs.why: After sliding the first set square to the required place, the new line is drawn along its longest side, the same side that was placed on the given line.

mcqs.q: In Question 1, the line drawn upward along the vertical side of the set square is named:
mcqs.why: XY is the given horizontal line. The new vertical line drawn upward along the other side of the set square is named PQ.

mcqs.q: What must be held firm during the sliding step for parallel lines?
mcqs.why: The second set square is held firm against the first one. If it moves, the sliding direction changes and the drawn line will not stay parallel.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.6: Vertex and Arms of Angles
lessons.notes_html:
Vertex and arms of an angle

An angle is formed by two arms meeting at a common point called the vertex. In the name of an angle, the middle letter is the vertex. For angle ABC, the vertex is B and the arms are BA and BC. To write an angle in symbols, write the angle sign, then a point on one arm, the vertex in the middle, and a point on the other arm.

Worked example

Write the vertex and arms of angle PQR.
