Step 1: In the name of an angle, the middle letter is the vertex: it is Q.

Step 2: The two arms starting from the vertex are QP and QR.

Answer: The vertex is Q and the arms are QP and QR.

Key points

  • Angle ABC: vertex B, arms BA and BC.
  • Angle XWY: vertex W, arms WX and WY.
  • Vertex O with points A and B on the arms is written as angle AOB.
  • Vertex E with points A and F is angle AEF; vertex K with points J and L is angle JKL.

mcqs.q: What is the vertex of angle ABC?
mcqs.why: In the name of an angle, the middle letter is the vertex. In angle ABC the middle letter is B, so the vertex is B.

mcqs.q: What are the arms of angle ABC?
options: AB and BC only from A
mcqs.why: The arms start from the vertex B and go to the other two points, so the two arms of angle ABC are BA and BC.

mcqs.q: What is the vertex of angle PQR?
mcqs.why: In the name of an angle, the middle letter is the vertex. In angle PQR the middle letter is Q, so the vertex is Q.

mcqs.q: What are the arms of angle PQR?
mcqs.why: The arms start from the vertex Q and go to P and R, so the two arms of angle PQR are QP and QR.

mcqs.q: What is the vertex of angle XWY?
mcqs.why: In the name of an angle, the middle letter is the vertex. In angle XWY the middle letter is W, so the vertex is W.

mcqs.q: What are the arms of angle XWY?
mcqs.why: The arms start from the vertex W and go to X and Y, so the two arms of angle XWY are WX and WY.

mcqs.q: The vertex is O and the points on its arms are A and B. The angle in symbols is:
mcqs.why: Write a point on one arm first, the vertex O in the middle, and a point on the other arm last. This gives the symbol angle AOB.

mcqs.q: The vertex is E and the points on its arms are A and F. The angle in symbols is:
mcqs.why: The vertex E must stay in the middle of the three letters, with A and F on the two sides. This gives the symbol angle AEF.

mcqs.q: The vertex is K and the points on its arms are J and L. The angle in symbols is:
mcqs.why: The vertex K must stay in the middle of the three letters, with J and L on the two sides. This gives the symbol angle JKL.

mcqs.q: In the name of any angle, which letter is the vertex?
mcqs.why: The book rule is that the middle letter in the three-letter name of an angle is always the vertex, the common point of the two arms.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.7: Identifying Right Angles
lessons.notes_html:
Identifying a right angle

A right angle measures 90 degrees. To test an angle, place the right-angle corner of a set square on the angle. If the angle matches the corner of the set square exactly, it is a right angle. If it is smaller than the corner, or bigger than the corner, it is not a right angle.

Worked example

Is angle MNO a right angle?

Step 1: Place the right-angle corner of a set square on angle MNO.

Step 2: The angle matches the corner of the set square exactly.

Answer: Yes, angle MNO is a right angle of 90 degrees, so tick it.

Key points

  • Angles MNO, PKL and ONM match the set square corner exactly, so they are right angles.
  • Angle ACD is smaller than the corner and angle EFG is bigger than the corner, so they are not right angles.
  • A horizontal line and a vertical line meeting at a point, like PQ and QR at Q, form a right angle.

mcqs.q: How many degrees are there in a right angle?
mcqs.why: A right angle is the angle that matches the corner of a set square exactly, and its measure is 90 degrees.

mcqs.q: How do we check whether an angle is a right angle?
options: By placing the right-angle corner of a set square on it
mcqs.why: The book method is to place the right-angle corner of a set square on the angle. An exact match means it is a right angle of 90 degrees.

mcqs.q: Angle MNO matches the set square corner exactly. It is:
mcqs.why: An angle that matches the corner of the set square exactly is a right angle, so angle MNO is a right angle of 90 degrees.

mcqs.q: Angle ACD is smaller than the set square corner. It is:
mcqs.why: Angle ACD does not match the corner of the set square because it is smaller than 90 degrees, so it is not a right angle.

mcqs.q: Angle EFG is bigger than the set square corner. It is:
mcqs.why: Angle EFG does not match the corner of the set square because it is bigger than 90 degrees, so it is not a right angle.

mcqs.q: Which of these angles is a right angle in Exercise 6.7?
mcqs.why: Angle PKL matches the corner of the set square exactly, so it is a right angle. ACD is smaller and EFG is bigger than the corner.

mcqs.q: Which of these angles is a right angle in Exercise 6.7?
mcqs.why: Angle ONM matches the corner of the set square exactly, so it is a right angle of 90 degrees. The others are smaller or bigger than the corner.

mcqs.q: Horizontal line PQ and vertical line QR meet at Q. Does the figure show a right angle?
options: Only on measuring with a thread
mcqs.why: A horizontal line and a vertical line meet at a right angle. The set square corner matches at Q, so the figure shows a right angle.

mcqs.q: Straight line AP has ray OB drawn from point O, and no angle matches the set square corner. Does it show a right angle?
mcqs.why: Checking with the corner of a set square shows no matching angle in this figure, so it does not show a right angle.

mcqs.q: Horizontal line AD has vertical line CK drawn at C. Does the figure show a right angle?
options: Only if CK is longer than AD
mcqs.why: CK is vertical and AD is horizontal, so they meet at C at a right angle of 90 degrees, confirmed by the set square corner.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.8: Types of Angles
lessons.notes_html:
Types of angles

An acute angle is smaller than 90 degrees. A right angle is exactly 90 degrees. An obtuse angle is greater than 90 degrees and smaller than 180 degrees. An angle of exactly 180 degrees is a straight angle. To name the type, compare the angle with 90 degrees.

Worked example

Tell the type of angle BAC, angle BAD and angle BAF in the book figure.

Step 1: Angle BAC matches the set square corner, so it is exactly 90 degrees.

Step 2: Angle BAD is smaller than angle BAC, so it is smaller than 90 degrees.

Step 3: Angle BAF is greater than 90 degrees and smaller than 180 degrees.

Answer: Angle BAC is a right angle, angle BAD is an acute angle and angle BAF is an obtuse angle.

Key points

  • Angle DAB is acute and angle CAB is right, the same angles as BAD and BAC named in reverse order.
  • Angle FAB is obtuse, the same angle as BAF.
  • To draw a named angle, choose the vertex, draw one arm, make the required type of opening and draw the second arm; the middle letter is the vertex.

mcqs.q: An acute angle is:
mcqs.why: The book defines an acute angle as less than 90 degrees, that is, smaller than a right angle.

mcqs.q: A right angle is:
mcqs.why: A right angle matches the corner of a set square exactly, and its measure is exactly 90 degrees.

mcqs.q: An obtuse angle is:
options: Greater than 90 degrees and smaller than 180 degrees
mcqs.why: The book defines an obtuse angle as more than 90 degrees and less than 180 degrees, written here in words to compare the sizes.

mcqs.q: In the book figure, angle BAC is:
mcqs.why: Angle BAC measures exactly 90 degrees in the figure, and an angle of exactly 90 degrees is a right angle.

mcqs.q: In the book figure, angle BAD is:
mcqs.why: Angle BAD is smaller than the right angle BAC in the same figure, so it is smaller than 90 degrees and is an acute angle.

mcqs.q: In the book figure, angle BAF is:
mcqs.why: Angle BAF is greater than 90 degrees and smaller than 180 degrees in the figure, so it is an obtuse angle.

mcqs.q: In the book figure, angle CAB is:
mcqs.why: Angle CAB is the same angle as BAC named in reverse order. It measures exactly 90 degrees, so it is a right angle.

mcqs.q: In the book figure, angle DAB is:
mcqs.why: Angle DAB is the same angle as BAD named in reverse order. It is smaller than 90 degrees, so it is an acute angle.

mcqs.q: In the book figure, angle FAB is:
mcqs.why: Angle FAB is the same angle as BAF named in reverse order. It is greater than 90 degrees and smaller than 180 degrees, so it is obtuse.

mcqs.q: An angle of exactly 180 degrees is called:
mcqs.why: A straight angle lies on a straight line and measures exactly 180 degrees, which is double the right angle of 90 degrees: 90 plus 90 equals 180.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.9: Measuring Angles with a Protractor
lessons.notes_html:
Measuring an angle with a protractor

Place the centre of the protractor on the vertex of the angle and its base line exactly on one arm. Then read the degrees at the other arm where it cuts the protractor. That reading is the measure of the angle.

Worked example

Measure angle FEG with a protractor.

Step 1: Place the centre of the protractor on vertex E and its base line exactly on one arm.

Step 2: Read the degrees at the other arm where it cuts the protractor.

Answer: Angle FEG measures 30 degrees.

Key points

  • Measures found in the book: RST = 40 degrees, ABC = 28 degrees, JLK = 43 degrees and DEF = 43 degrees.
  • The larger angles measured are PQR = 110 degrees and STU = 110 degrees.
  • The name XYZ appears for two different figures in the book list, measuring 40 degrees in one figure and 142 degrees in the other figure.

mcqs.q: What is the measure of angle FEG?
mcqs.why: Place the protractor centre on vertex E with the base line on one arm. The other arm cuts the protractor at 30, so angle FEG measures 30 degrees.

mcqs.q: What is the measure of angle RST?
mcqs.why: Place the protractor centre on vertex S with the base line on one arm. The other arm cuts the protractor at 40, so angle RST measures 40 degrees.

mcqs.q: What is the measure of angle ABC in Exercise 6.9?
mcqs.why: Place the protractor centre on vertex B with the base line on one arm. The other arm cuts the protractor at 28, so angle ABC measures 28 degrees.

mcqs.q: What is the measure of angle JLK?
mcqs.why: Place the protractor centre on vertex L with the base line on one arm. The other arm cuts the protractor at 43, so angle JLK measures 43 degrees.

mcqs.q: What is the measure of angle DEF in Exercise 6.9?
mcqs.why: Place the protractor centre on vertex E with the base line on one arm. The other arm cuts the protractor at 43, so angle DEF measures 43 degrees.

mcqs.q: What is the measure of angle PQR in Exercise 6.9?
mcqs.why: Place the protractor centre on vertex Q with the base line on one arm. The other arm cuts the protractor at 110, so angle PQR measures 110 degrees.

mcqs.q: What is the measure of angle STU?
mcqs.why: Place the protractor centre on vertex T with the base line on one arm. The other arm cuts the protractor at 110, so angle STU measures 110 degrees.

mcqs.q: What is the measure of the larger angle XYZ in the Exercise 6.9 list?
mcqs.why: For the larger XYZ figure, the protractor centre sits on vertex Y and the other arm cuts the scale at 142, so this angle XYZ measures 142 degrees.

mcqs.q: What is the first step in measuring an angle with a protractor?
options: Read any number on the protractor
Place the centre of the protractor on the vertex and its base line on one arm
Draw a circle around the angle
Measure both arms with a ruler
mcqs.why: The book method starts by placing the centre of the protractor exactly on the vertex and its base line exactly on one arm of the angle.

mcqs.q: Where is the measure of the angle read on the protractor?
options: At the zero of the ruler
Where the other arm cuts the protractor scale
At the end of the first arm
mcqs.why: After the centre is placed on the vertex and the base line on one arm, the degrees are read where the other arm cuts the protractor scale.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.10: Measuring, Naming the Type and Drawing Angles
lessons.notes_html:
Measure, name the type, and draw

First measure the angle with a protractor, then compare its measure with 90 degrees: smaller than 90 degrees is acute, exactly 90 degrees is right, and greater than 90 degrees and smaller than 180 degrees is obtuse. To draw an angle of a given measure, draw a straight line, place the protractor centre on the chosen vertex point with its base line on the line, mark the required degrees, remove the protractor and join the mark to the vertex.

Worked example

Measure angle XYZ and tell its type.

Step 1: Place the centre of the protractor on the vertex and read the degrees: 70 degrees.

Step 2: Compare 70 degrees with 90 degrees: 70 is smaller than 90.

Answer: Angle XYZ measures 70 degrees and it is an acute angle.

Key points

  • Angle PQR = 43 degrees, acute; angle TLM = 90 degrees, right.
  • Angle COT = 155 degrees, obtuse; the name ABC appears for two figures, one of 43 degrees (acute) and one of 155 degrees (obtuse).
  • Angles drawn with the protractor in the book: 10, 40, 20, 60, 30, 80, 90, 120, 145 and 45 degrees.

mcqs.q: Angle PQR measures 43 degrees. What is its type?
mcqs.why: Compare the measure with 90 degrees: 43 is smaller than 90, and 90 minus 43 is 47. An angle smaller than 90 degrees is an acute angle.

mcqs.q: Angle XYZ measures 70 degrees. What is its type?
mcqs.why: Compare the measure with 90 degrees: 70 is smaller than 90, and 90 minus 70 is 20. An angle smaller than 90 degrees is an acute angle.

mcqs.q: Angle TLM measures 90 degrees. What is its type?
mcqs.why: Compare the measure with 90 degrees: 90 is exactly equal to 90, with a difference of 0. An angle of exactly 90 degrees is a right angle.

mcqs.q: Angle COT measures 155 degrees. What is its type?
mcqs.why: Compare the measure: 155 is greater than 90 by 155 minus 90 equals 65, and 155 is smaller than 180. So it is an obtuse angle.

mcqs.q: The larger angle ABC in Exercise 6.10 measures 155 degrees. What is its type?
mcqs.why: Compare the measure: 155 is greater than 90 by 155 minus 90 equals 65, and smaller than 180, so this angle ABC is an obtuse angle.

mcqs.q: The smaller angle ABC in Exercise 6.10 measures 43 degrees. What is its type?
mcqs.why: Compare the measure with 90 degrees: 43 is smaller than 90, and 90 minus 43 is 47. An angle smaller than 90 degrees is an acute angle.

mcqs.q: An angle of 90 degrees drawn with a protractor in Question 2 is which type?
mcqs.why: The drawn angle measures exactly 90 degrees. Comparing, 90 equals 90 exactly, so the drawn angle is a right angle.

mcqs.q: An angle of 120 degrees drawn with a protractor in Question 2 is which type?
mcqs.why: Compare 120 with the limits: 120 minus 90 equals 30, so 120 is greater than 90, and 120 is smaller than 180. So it is an obtuse angle.

mcqs.q: An angle of 45 degrees drawn with a protractor in Question 2 is which type?
mcqs.why: Compare 45 with 90: 45 is smaller than 90, and 90 minus 45 is 45. An angle smaller than 90 degrees is an acute angle.

mcqs.q: An angle of 145 degrees drawn with a protractor in Question 2 is which type?
mcqs.why: Compare 145 with the limits: 145 minus 90 equals 55, so 145 is greater than 90, and 145 is smaller than 180. So it is an obtuse angle.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.11: Drawing Equal, Double and Sum Angles
lessons.notes_html:
Equal, double and sum angles

To draw an angle equal to a given angle, first measure the given angle with a protractor, then draw exactly the same measure on a new line. To draw an angle of double the measure, measure the given angle, multiply its measure by 2, and draw the doubled measure. To draw an angle equal to the sum of two angles, measure both angles, add the two measures, and draw an angle of that total.

Worked example

Draw an angle twice the measure of angle FEG, which measures 30 degrees in Exercise 6.9.

Step 1: Measure the given angle: angle FEG = 30 degrees.

Step 2: Double its measure: 30 times 2 = 60 degrees.

Step 3: Draw an angle of 60 degrees with the protractor on a new line.

Answer: The new angle measures 60 degrees, double of 30 degrees.

Key points

  • Equal angles are drawn for ABC, PQR, DEF and XYZ by copying the measured value exactly.
  • Double means multiply by 2; sum means add the two measures.
  • Always measure first with the protractor, then calculate, then draw.

mcqs.q: What is the first step to draw an angle equal to a given angle ABC?
options: Draw any angle and hope it matches
Measure the given angle ABC with the protractor
mcqs.why: The book method first measures the given angle ABC with the protractor and notes its measure, then draws exactly the same measure on a new line.

mcqs.q: Angle FEG measures 30 degrees. What is double its measure?
mcqs.why: Double means multiply by 2. Working: 30 times 2 equals 60, so the angle to draw measures 60 degrees.

mcqs.q: Angle RST measures 40 degrees. What is double its measure?
mcqs.why: Double means multiply by 2. Working: 40 times 2 equals 80, so the angle to draw measures 80 degrees.

mcqs.q: Angle PQR measures 43 degrees. What is double its measure?
mcqs.why: Double means multiply by 2. Working: 43 times 2 equals 86, so the angle to draw measures 86 degrees.

mcqs.q: Angle XYZ measures 70 degrees. What is double its measure?
mcqs.why: Double means multiply by 2. Working: 70 times 2 equals 140, so the angle to draw measures 140 degrees.

mcqs.q: What is the sum of angle FEG 30 degrees and angle RST 40 degrees?
mcqs.why: Sum means add the two measures. Working: 30 plus 40 equals 70, so the angle equal to their sum measures 70 degrees.

mcqs.q: What is the sum of angle ABC 28 degrees and angle JLK 43 degrees?
mcqs.why: Sum means add the two measures. Working: 28 plus 43 equals 71, so the angle equal to their sum measures 71 degrees.

mcqs.q: What is the sum of angle PQR 110 degrees and angle FEG 30 degrees?
mcqs.why: Sum means add the two measures. Working: 110 plus 30 equals 140, so the angle equal to their sum measures 140 degrees.

mcqs.q: What is the sum of angle XYZ 70 degrees and angle PQR 43 degrees?
mcqs.why: Sum means add the two measures. Working: 70 plus 43 equals 113, so the angle equal to their sum measures 113 degrees.

mcqs.q: To draw an angle equal to a given angle on a new line, you should draw:
options: Exactly the same measure with the protractor
mcqs.why: An equal angle has the same measure as the given angle. After measuring the given angle, draw exactly that same measure with the protractor on the new line.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.12: Drawing Circles with Given Radii
lessons.notes_html:
Drawing a circle with a compass

The radius is the distance from the centre of the circle to its edge, and it is also the opening of the compass. To draw a circle of a given radius, open the compass to that measure on the ruler, put the compass needle on the centre point, and turn the pencil all the way round. The diameter is twice the radius.

Worked example

Draw a circle whose radius is 3.2 cm.

Step 1: Open the compass to 3.2 cm on the ruler.

Step 2: Put the compass needle on the centre point and turn the pencil all the way round.

Answer: A circle of radius 3.2 cm has been drawn. Its diameter is 3.2 times 2 = 6.4 cm.

Key points

  • Circles drawn in the book have radii 3.2 cm, 4.1 cm, 4.4 cm, 5.5 cm, 6 cm and 4.8 cm.
  • Keep the compass opening fixed while turning, or the circle will not close properly.
  • Diameter equals radius times 2, as in the Review circle: radius 25 mm gives diameter 50 mm.

mcqs.q: What is the first step to draw a circle of radius 3.2 cm?
options: Open the compass to 3.2 cm on the ruler
Put the needle anywhere and guess
Measure the diameter first with a thread
mcqs.why: The book method first opens the compass to the given radius, 3.2 cm, measured on the ruler, before the needle is placed on the centre point.

mcqs.q: To draw a circle of radius 4.1 cm, the compass must be opened to:
mcqs.why: The compass opening is equal to the radius itself. For a radius of 4.1 cm the opening is 4.1 cm; 8.2 cm would be the diameter, not the opening.

mcqs.q: A circle has radius 3.2 cm. What is its diameter?
mcqs.why: Diameter is twice the radius. Working: 3.2 times 2 equals 6.4, so the diameter of this circle is 6.4 cm.

mcqs.q: A circle has radius 4.4 cm. What is its diameter?
mcqs.why: Diameter is twice the radius. Working: 4.4 times 2 equals 8.8, so the diameter of this circle is 8.8 cm.

mcqs.q: A circle has radius 5.5 cm. What is its diameter?
mcqs.why: Diameter is twice the radius. Working: 5.5 times 2 equals 11, so the diameter of this circle is 11 cm.

mcqs.q: A circle has radius 6 cm. What is its diameter?
mcqs.why: Diameter is twice the radius. Working: 6 times 2 equals 12, so the diameter of this circle is 12 cm.

mcqs.q: A circle has radius 4.8 cm. What is its diameter?
mcqs.why: Diameter is twice the radius. Working: 4.8 times 2 equals 9.6, so the diameter of this circle is 9.6 cm.

mcqs.q: Where is the compass needle placed when drawing a circle?
options: On the edge of the circle
On the vertex of an angle
mcqs.why: The book method puts the compass needle on the centre point and turns the pencil all the way round to complete the circle.

mcqs.q: How is the circle completed after placing the needle on the centre?
options: By joining two points with a ruler
By turning the pencil all the way round
By laying a thread around it
mcqs.why: With the needle fixed on the centre and the opening set to the radius, the pencil is turned all the way round until the circle is complete.

mcqs.q: A student opens the compass to 4.1 cm and draws a circle. What is the radius of the circle?
mcqs.why: The compass opening from the centre needle to the pencil is the radius itself, so an opening of 4.1 cm gives a circle of radius 4.1 cm, not double it.

lessons.title: Exercise 6.13: Drawing Squares and Rectangles
lessons.notes_html:
Drawing squares and rectangles

A square has all four sides equal and all four angles as right angles of 90 degrees. Draw one side of the given length, use a set square to make right angles at both ends, draw the side lengths upward, and join the top ends. A rectangle has opposite sides equal: draw the length side, make right angles at both ends, draw the width sides, and join the top ends with a line equal to the length.

Worked example

Draw a square with sides of 6.5 cm.

Step 1: First draw one side 6.5 cm long.

Step 2: With a set square, make right angles at both ends and draw sides of 6.5 cm upward.

Step 3: Join the top ends. All four sides are 6.5 cm and all four angles are right angles.

Answer: A square with sides of 6.5 cm has been drawn.

Key points

  • Squares drawn in the book have sides 6.5 cm, 4.9 cm, 5.8 cm, 6.3 cm, 7.3 cm, 4.1 cm, 8.7 cm and 8.5 cm.
  • Rectangles drawn in the book: 8 cm and 7 cm; 9.5 cm and 4.7 cm; 12.3 cm and 5.2 cm; 9.6 cm and 3.7 cm; 6.1 cm and 2.9 cm; 2.9 cm and 7.6 cm.
  • Every corner of both a square and a rectangle is a right angle of 90 degrees.

mcqs.q: In a square, the four sides and four angles are:
options: All sides different and angles acute
All sides equal and all angles right angles
Opposite sides equal and angles obtuse
All sides equal and angles obtuse
mcqs.why: The book construction makes all four sides the same length and all four angles right angles of 90 degrees, which is a square.

mcqs.q: A square is drawn with one side 6.5 cm. What is the length of each other side?
mcqs.why: All four sides of a square are equal. The given side is 6.5 cm, so every other side is also 6.5 cm, with no addition needed.

mcqs.q: What is the second step in drawing a square of side 4.9 cm?
options: Draw a circle of radius 4.9 cm
Join the two points with a curved line
Measure the angles with a protractor first
Make right angles at both ends and draw sides of 4.9 cm upward
mcqs.why: After drawing the first side of 4.9 cm, the book method uses a set square to make right angles at both ends and draws sides of 4.9 cm upward.

mcqs.q: A square has sides of 8.7 cm. What is the length of its top side?
mcqs.why: All four sides of a square are equal to the given side. The given side is 8.7 cm, so the top side joining the ends is also 8.7 cm.

mcqs.q: A rectangle has sides 8 cm and 7 cm. The side opposite the 8 cm side measures:
mcqs.why: In a rectangle the opposite sides are equal. The side opposite the 8 cm length is the other length, so it also measures 8 cm.

mcqs.q: A rectangle has sides 9.5 cm and 4.7 cm. The two width sides measure:
mcqs.why: The width sides are the shorter pair drawn at the right angles. Both width sides are equal to the given width, which is 4.7 cm each.

mcqs.q: A rectangle has sides 12.3 cm and 5.2 cm. The top side joining the ends measures:
mcqs.why: The top side joins the tops of the two width sides and is equal to the length side drawn first. The length is 12.3 cm, so the top side is 12.3 cm.

mcqs.q: Which pair of sides is used for the rectangle in Exercise 6.13 Question 2 part (v)?
mcqs.why: Part (v) of Question 2 gives the length and width as 6.1 cm and 2.9 cm. The other pairs belong to parts (i), (iv) and (iii).

mcqs.q: Each corner angle of a square and of a rectangle measures:
mcqs.why: Both shapes are built with right angles made by the set square at every corner, and a right angle measures exactly 90 degrees.

mcqs.q: How is a square different from a rectangle in these constructions?
options: A square has no right angles
A rectangle has all sides equal
A square has all four sides equal, while a rectangle has opposite sides equal with two different lengths
A square is drawn with a compass only
mcqs.why: In the book, every square is drawn with one single side length used four times, while every rectangle is drawn with two different lengths whose opposite sides are equal.

lessons.title: Review Exercise 6: Mixed Practice
lessons.notes_html:
Review of instruments and ideas

The geometry instruments are the ruler for measuring and drawing straight lines, the set square for right angles and parallel lines, the protractor for measuring and drawing angles, the compasses for drawing circles and the dividers for comparing lengths. A thin line is drawn with an H-grade pencil. Remember that 1 cm = 10 mm, the diameter of a circle is twice its radius, and the circumference can be measured with thread and ruler.

Worked example

Draw a circle with radius 25 mm and name its diameter and circumference.

Step 1: Open the compass to 25 mm, which is 2.5 cm, on the ruler and draw the circle.

Step 2: The diameter is twice the radius: 25 times 2 = 50 mm.

Step 3: Lay thread all the way round the circle, straighten it and measure with the ruler: about 157 mm.

Answer: Radius 25 mm, diameter 50 mm and circumference about 157 mm.

Key points

  • Corners of a book, blackboard, door, table, window and notebook are classroom examples of right angles.
  • A big square divided into four small squares contains 5 squares in all.
  • Triangle ADC with DB drawn inside contains 3 triangles in all.
  • Counting angles: from three rays at B there are 3 angles; in the semicircle figure there are 10 angles in all, including the straight angle ABC of 180 degrees.

mcqs.q: Which instrument is used to measure and draw angles in degrees?
mcqs.why: The protractor is the instrument with the degree scale. In the review list it is the instrument used for measuring and drawing angles.

mcqs.q: Which grade of pencil is used to draw a thin line segment?
mcqs.why: A thin line needs a hard pencil with a thin point. The review answer is an H-grade pencil for a thin line segment.

mcqs.q: The review circle has radius 25 mm. How many centimetres is this radius?
mcqs.why: Use 1 cm equals 10 mm. Working: 25 divided by 10 equals 2.5, so a radius of 25 mm is the same as 2.5 cm.

mcqs.q: The review circle has radius 25 mm. What is its diameter?
mcqs.why: Diameter is twice the radius. Working: 25 times 2 equals 50, so the diameter of the review circle is 50 mm.

mcqs.q: The circumference of the review circle is measured with thread and ruler. About how long is it?
mcqs.why: Lay the thread all the way round the circumference, straighten it and measure with the ruler. The measured length obtained is about 157 mm.

mcqs.q: Rays BA, BD and BC come from point B. How many angles are formed?
mcqs.why: Count the pairs of rays: ABD, CBD and the whole angle ABC. That gives 3 angles in all: ABD acute, CBD acute and ABC right.

mcqs.q: In the semicircle figure with centre B and rays BF, BE and BD between BA and BC, how many angles are there in all?
mcqs.why: Count all pairs from the 5 rays BA, BF, BE, BD and BC: 4 acute plus 3 right plus 2 obtuse plus the straight angle ABC of 180 degrees equals 10 angles. Note: the solved book lists only 9 because it misses the straight angle ABC, which is an error in the book.

mcqs.q: A big square is divided into four small squares. How many squares are there in all?
mcqs.why: Count the small squares first: there are 4. The big outer figure is also a square: 4 plus 1 equals 5 squares in all.

mcqs.q: Triangle ADC has DB drawn from D to side AC. How many triangles are in the figure?
mcqs.why: Count the small triangles ADB and CDB, which makes 2, and then the whole big triangle ADC, which makes 3 triangles in all.

mcqs.q: Which classroom object shows a right angle at its corner?
mcqs.why: The corner of a book is listed in the review as a right angle of 90 degrees, like the corners of the blackboard, door, table, window and notebook.

lessons.title: Exercise 7.1: Reading Bar Graphs
lessons.notes_html:
What is a bar graph?

A bar graph shows information with bars. The height of each bar tells the number for that item. To read a bar graph, look at the top of a bar and read the number on the side scale. In the cricket activity, the bars show runs: Ali 50 runs, Anwar 40 runs and Rashid 30 runs, so Ali scored the most and Rashid scored the least.

In the bar graph of Saima marks, the bars are: Sindhi 70, Social Studies 50, English 60, Urdu 40, Science 80 and Maths 50. Her highest marks are in Science and her lowest marks are in Urdu. Social Studies and Maths have equal marks. Her correct total is 70 + 50 + 60 + 40 + 80 + 50 = 350 marks. She scored more than 60 marks in two subjects, Sindhi with 70 and Science with 80.

The two survey graphs in Exercise 7.1

The bar graph of favourite colours of Class IV shows: blue 15, yellow 5, pink 30, red 15, black 10 and green 20 students. There are 6 colours. Pink is liked most and yellow is liked least.

The bar graph of favourite games of Class IV shows: Football 25, Swimming 30, Hockey 20 and Cricket 35 students. There are 4 games. Cricket is liked most and Hockey is liked least.

Worked example

How many students in all are included in the favourite colours survey?

Step 1: Read every bar: blue 15, yellow 5, pink 30, red 15, black 10 and green 20.

Step 2: Add them all: 15 + 5 + 30 + 15 + 10 + 20 = 95.

Answer: 95 students are included in the survey.

Key points

  • The tallest bar shows the biggest number and the shortest bar shows the smallest number.
  • Count the bars to find how many items are in the graph.
  • Add all the bar values to find the total.
  • Subtract two bar values to find how many more one item has than another.

mcqs.q: In the bar graph of favourite colours of Class IV, the bars are blue 15, yellow 5, pink 30, red 15, black 10 and green 20 students. How many students like yellow colour?
mcqs.why: The bar for yellow colour reaches 5 on the scale, so 5 students like yellow colour.

mcqs.q: In the bar graph of favourite colours, pink reaches 30 students, green reaches 20 and blue and red each reach 15. Which colour is liked most?
mcqs.why: Pink has the tallest bar at 30 students, and 30 is more than 20 and more than 15, so pink is liked most.

mcqs.q: In the bar graph of favourite colours, the values are blue 15, yellow 5, pink 30, red 15, black 10 and green 20. How many students are included in the survey in all?
mcqs.why: Add all the bars: 15 + 5 + 30 + 15 + 10 + 20 = 95, so 95 students are included in the survey.

mcqs.q: In the bar graph of favourite games of Class IV, the bars are Football 25, Swimming 30, Hockey 20 and Cricket 35 students. Which game is liked most?
mcqs.why: Cricket has the tallest bar at 35 students, and 35 is more than 30, 25 and 20, so Cricket is liked most.

mcqs.q: In the bar graph of favourite games, the values are Football 25, Swimming 30, Hockey 20 and Cricket 35. How many students are involved in games in total?
mcqs.why: Add all four games: 25 + 30 + 20 + 35 = 110, so 110 students are involved in games in total.

mcqs.q: In the bar graph of favourite games, Cricket reaches 35 students and Hockey reaches 20 students. How many more students like Cricket than Hockey?
mcqs.why: Subtract the two bars: Cricket 35 minus Hockey 20 gives 35 - 20 = 15, so 15 more students like Cricket.

mcqs.q: In the bar graph of Saima marks, the bars are Sindhi 70, Social Studies 50, English 60, Urdu 40, Science 80 and Maths 50. What is her correct total marks?
mcqs.why: Add all six marks: 70 + 50 + 60 + 40 + 80 + 50 = 350. Note: the solved book prints 340, which is wrong; the correct total is 350.

mcqs.q: In the bar graph of Saima marks, Sindhi is 70, English is 60 and Science is 80, and all other subjects are 50 or less. In which subjects did she secure more than 60 marks?
mcqs.why: More than 60 means 70 and 80 qualify: Sindhi 70 and Science 80, while English 60 does not qualify. Note: the solved book says only Science, which misses Sindhi 70.

mcqs.q: In the bar graph of Saima marks, the bars are Sindhi 70, Social Studies 50, English 60, Urdu 40, Science 80 and Maths 50. In which subject did she secure the highest marks?
mcqs.why: Science has the tallest bar at 80 marks, and 80 is more than 70, 60, 50 and 40, so Science is the highest.

mcqs.q: In the bar graph of runs in a cricket match, Ali scored 50, Anwar scored 40 and Rashid scored 30. How many runs did the three players score in all?
mcqs.why: Add the three bars: Ali 50 + Anwar 40 + Rashid 30 = 120, so the three players scored 120 runs in all.

lessons.title: Exercise 7.2: Reading Line Graphs
lessons.notes_html:
What is a line graph?

A line graph shows information with points joined by lines. To read it, find a point, move across to the side scale and read its value. In the activity, the line graph of the temperature of Jacobabad shows: 5 a.m. 35 degrees, 7 a.m. 37 degrees, 9 a.m. 38 degrees, 11 a.m. 39 degrees, 1 p.m. 41 degrees and 3 p.m. 39 degrees Celsius. The lowest temperature was 35 degrees at 5 a.m. and the highest was 41 degrees at 1 p.m.

The graphs in Exercise 7.2

In the line graph of five teams completing a task, Team D took the shortest time of 10 minutes, Team E took the longest time of 40 minutes and Team C took 15 minutes. According to the book answer key, Teams A and B took the same length of time.

In the line graph of a farmer tractor ploughing for one week, the values in acres are: Monday 5, Tuesday 10, Wednesday 10, Thursday 15, Friday 5, Saturday 10 and Sunday 10. Thursday was the maximum and Monday and Friday were the minimum.

In the line graph of Samina quarterly test marks, the values are: Maths 80, English 70, Science 60, Islamiyat 80 and Sindhi 70. Maths and Islamiyat are the highest and Science is the lowest.

Worked example

How many acres were ploughed during the whole week by the tractor?

Step 1: Read every day point: Monday 5, Tuesday 10, Wednesday 10, Thursday 15, Friday 5, Saturday 10 and Sunday 10 acres.

Step 2: Add them all: 5 + 10 + 10 + 15 + 5 + 10 + 10 = 65.

Answer: 65 acres were ploughed during the whole week.

Key points

  • The highest point shows the biggest value and the lowest point shows the smallest value.
  • Points at the same height have the same value.
  • Add all the point values to find a total for the whole graph.
  • Read each point carefully from the side scale before answering.

mcqs.q: In the line graph of five teams completing a task, Team D is at 10 minutes, Team C is at 15 minutes and Team E is at 40 minutes. Which team completed the work in the shortest time?
mcqs.why: Team D has the lowest point at 10 minutes, and 10 is less than 15 and less than 40, so Team D was shortest.

mcqs.q: In the line graph of five teams completing a task, the highest point is 40 minutes and the lowest point is 10 minutes. Which team took the longest time?
mcqs.why: The highest point belongs to Team E at 40 minutes, and 40 is the biggest value on the graph, so Team E took the longest.

mcqs.q: In the line graph of five teams completing a task, Team D took 10 minutes and Team E took 40 minutes. How long did Team C take, if its point is at 15 minutes?
mcqs.why: The point for Team C sits at 15 on the minutes scale, so Team C took 15 minutes to complete the task.

mcqs.q: In the line graph of five teams completing a task, the book answer key says two teams have points at the same height. Which teams took the same length of time?
mcqs.why: According to the book answer key for this graph, Teams A and B took the same length of time, so their points are at the same height.

mcqs.q: In the line graph of a farmer tractor ploughing, the values are Monday 5, Tuesday 10, Wednesday 10, Thursday 15, Friday 5, Saturday 10 and Sunday 10 acres. On which day were the maximum acres ploughed?
mcqs.why: Thursday has the highest point at 15 acres, and 15 is more than 10 and more than 5, so Thursday was the maximum.

mcqs.q: In the line graph of a farmer tractor ploughing, the values for the week are 5, 10, 10, 15, 5, 10 and 10 acres. How many acres were ploughed during the whole week?
mcqs.why: Add all seven days: 5 + 10 + 10 + 15 + 5 + 10 + 10 = 65, so 65 acres were ploughed during the whole week.

mcqs.q: In the line graph of a farmer tractor ploughing, Tuesday, Wednesday, Saturday and Sunday are each 10 acres, Thursday is 15 acres and Monday and Friday are each 5 acres. Which days had the same output of 10 acres?
mcqs.why: Four days sit at 10 acres: Tuesday 10, Wednesday 10, Saturday 10 and Sunday 10, so those four days had the same output.

mcqs.q: In the line graph of Samina quarterly test marks, the values are Maths 80, English 70, Science 60, Islamiyat 80 and Sindhi 70. How many marks did she get in English?
mcqs.why: The point for English sits at 70 on the marks scale, so Samina got 70 marks in English in the quarterly test.

mcqs.q: In the line graph of Samina quarterly test marks, Maths is 80, English is 70, Science is 60, Islamiyat is 80 and Sindhi is 70. In which subject did she get the lowest marks?
mcqs.why: Science has the lowest point at 60 marks, and 60 is less than 70 and less than 80, so Science is the lowest.

mcqs.q: In the line graph of Samina quarterly test marks, the values are Maths 80, English 70, Science 60, Islamiyat 80 and Sindhi 70. What were her total marks?
mcqs.why: Add all five subjects: 80 + 70 + 60 + 80 + 70 = 360, so Samina total marks are 360 in the quarterly tests.

lessons.title: Review Exercise 7: Mixed Practice
lessons.notes_html:
Bar graphs and line graphs together

This review mixes bar graphs and a line graph. Read every bar or point from the scale first, write the values down, and then add, subtract or compare as the question asks.

The bar graph of the cost of mango squash shows: 1 litre Rs 40, 2 litres Rs 80, 3 litres Rs 100, 4 litres Rs 120, 5 litres Rs 160 and 6 litres Rs 180. Read each cost from its own bar; do not assume every litre costs the same in this graph.

The bar graph of Rashid family expenditure on food shows: January Rs 5500, February Rs 3000, March Rs 2000, April Rs 4000, May Rs 2500 and June Rs 1000. January is the highest month and June is the lowest month.

The line graph of the production of an oil plant over 5 days shows, in million litres: Day 1 is 2, Day 2 is 4, Day 3 is 6, Day 4 is 7 and Day 5 is 10. The production was measured 5 times and it was highest on Day 5.

Worked example

What is the total expenditure of Rashid family on food from January to June?

Step 1: Read every bar: January 5500, February 3000, March 2000, April 4000, May 2500 and June 1000 rupees.

Step 2: Add them all: 5500 + 3000 + 2000 + 4000 + 2500 + 1000 = 18000.

Answer: The total expenditure from January to June is Rs 18,000.

Key points

  • Write down all the graph values before adding or subtracting.
  • For change from a note, subtract the cost from the money you give.
  • For production between two days on a line graph, subtract the earlier day value from the later day value.
  • The tallest bar or highest point is the maximum and the shortest bar or lowest point is the minimum.

mcqs.q: In the bar graph of the cost of mango squash, 1 litre is Rs 40, 2 litres is Rs 80 and 4 litres is Rs 120. What is the cost of 2 litres of mango squash?
mcqs.why: The bar for 2 litres reaches Rs 80 on the cost scale, so the cost of 2 litres of mango squash is Rs 80.

mcqs.q: In the bar graph of the cost of mango squash, 2 litres cost Rs 80. How much change will we have from Rs 100 when we buy 2 litres?
mcqs.why: Subtract the cost from the note: Rs 100 minus Rs 80 for 2 litres gives 100 - 80 = 20, so the change is Rs 20.

mcqs.q: In the bar graph of the cost of mango squash, the bars are 1 litre Rs 40, 2 litres Rs 80, 3 litres Rs 100, 4 litres Rs 120, 5 litres Rs 160 and 6 litres Rs 180. How many litres can we buy from Rs 180?
mcqs.why: Rs 180 matches the bar for 6 litres exactly, since the 6 litres bar is Rs 180, so we can buy 6 litres.

mcqs.q: In the bar graph of the cost of mango squash, 6 litres cost Rs 180. We have six notes of Rs 20 each. How much money do we have in all?
mcqs.why: Multiply the notes: 6 notes times Rs 20 each gives 6 x 20 = 120, so we have Rs 120, which is less than Rs 180 for 6 litres.

mcqs.q: In the bar graph of Rashid family expenditure on food, the values are January Rs 5500, February Rs 3000, March Rs 2000, April Rs 4000, May Rs 2500 and June Rs 1000. In which month was the expenditure the lowest?
mcqs.why: June has the shortest bar at Rs 1000, and 1000 is less than 2000, 2500, 3000, 4000 and 5500, so June is lowest.

mcqs.q: In the bar graph of Rashid family expenditure on food, the values are 5500, 3000, 2000, 4000, 2500 and 1000 rupees for January to June. What is the total expenditure from January to June?
mcqs.why: Add all six months: 5500 + 3000 + 2000 + 4000 + 2500 + 1000 = 18000, so the total expenditure is Rs 18,000.

mcqs.q: In the bar graph of Rashid family expenditure on food, April is Rs 4000 and May is Rs 2500. What is the difference in expenditure for April and May?
mcqs.why: Subtract May from April: Rs 4000 minus Rs 2500 gives 4000 - 2500 = 1500, so the difference is Rs 1500.

mcqs.q: In the line graph of the production of an oil plant, Day 1 is 2, Day 2 is 4, Day 3 is 6, Day 4 is 7 and Day 5 is 10 million litres. What was the production on the 1st day?
mcqs.why: The point for Day 1 sits at 2 on the production scale, so the production on the 1st day was 2 million litres.

mcqs.q: In the line graph of the production of an oil plant, Day 2 is 4 million litres and Day 3 is 6 million litres. How much production was made between the 2nd and 3rd day?
mcqs.why: Subtract Day 2 from Day 3: 6 million litres minus 4 million litres gives 6 - 4 = 2, so 2 million litres were made between them.

mcqs.q: In the line graph of the production of an oil plant, the values are Day 1 is 2, Day 2 is 4, Day 3 is 6, Day 4 is 7 and Day 5 is 10 million litres. On which day was the production the highest?
mcqs.why: Day 5 has the highest point at 10 million litres, and 10 is more than 7, 6, 4 and 2, so Day 5 was the highest.

lessons.title: Glossary: Definitions of Terms
lessons.notes_html:
Number words

Addition — The process of putting two or more numbers together to find their total is called addition.

Associative Property of Addition — While adding three numbers, changing their grouping does not change the sum. For example, (2 + 3) + 4 = 2 + (3 + 4).

Associative Property of Multiplication — While multiplying three numbers, changing their grouping does not change the product.

Commutative Property of Addition — While adding two numbers, changing their order does not change the sum.

Commutative Property of Multiplication — While multiplying two numbers, changing their order does not change the product.

Common Multiples — The multiples which are multiples of each of two or more numbers are called their common multiples.

Composite Number — A number which has more than two factors is called a composite number; for example 4, 6 and 8.

Division — The process of sharing a number into equal parts is called division; it is the opposite process of multiplication.

Divisibility — If one number is divided exactly by another number with no remainder, the first number is divisible by the second.

Dividend — In division, the number which is being divided is called the dividend.

Divisor — In division, the number by which we divide is called the divisor.

Even Numbers — Numbers which are exactly divisible by two, whose ones digit is 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8, are called even numbers.

Factors — The numbers which divide a given number exactly, with no remainder, are called its factors.

Factorization — Writing a number as a product of its factors is called factorization.

GCD — The greatest common factor of two or more numbers, which divides them all exactly, is called GCD or HCF.

HCF — The largest factor common to two or more numbers is called their HCF (Highest Common Factor).

L.C.M — The smallest multiple common to two or more numbers is called their L.C.M (Least Common Multiple).

Multiplication — The short way of repeated addition of the same number is multiplication; it gives the product.

Million — A million is a big number: there are ten hundred-thousands (ten lakh) in one million and it is written as 1,000,000.

Place Value — The value of a digit according to its position is called its place value; for example the digit in the hundreds place.

Prime Factorisation — Writing a number as a product of prime factors only is called prime factorisation.

Quotient — The answer obtained on dividing is called the quotient.

Remainder — The amount left over after division is called the remainder.

Subtraction — The process of taking one number away from another to find the difference is called subtraction.

Symbol — Any sign used in mathematics is called a symbol; for example the signs of addition, subtraction, multiplication and division.

Fraction and decimal words

Fraction — A part or some parts of a whole thing are written as a fraction; it is written with a numerator and a denominator.

Numerator — In a fraction, the number above the line is the numerator; it tells how many parts are taken.

Denominator — In a fraction, the number below the line is the denominator; it tells into how many equal parts the whole is divided.

Decimal Fraction — A fraction whose denominator is 10, 100 or 1000 and which is written with a decimal point is called a decimal fraction.

Equivalent Fractions — Fractions which show the same amount, even though their numbers are different, are called equivalent fractions.

Improper Fraction — A fraction whose numerator is greater than or equal to its denominator is called an improper fraction.

Proper Fraction — A fraction whose numerator is smaller than its denominator is called a proper fraction.

Like Fractions — Fractions which have the same denominator are called like fractions.

Unlike Fractions — Fractions which have different denominators are called unlike fractions.

Unit Fraction — A fraction whose numerator is one (1) is called a unit fraction.

Mixed Number — A number made of a whole number together with a fraction is called a mixed number.

Measurement words

Capacity — The amount that a container can hold is called its capacity; it is measured in litres and millilitres.

Centimetre — A small unit for measuring length; there are 100 centimetres in one metre.

Gram — A small unit for measuring mass; there are 1000 grams in one kilogram.

Kilogram — A bigger unit for measuring mass; there are 1000 grams in one kilogram.

Mass — The amount of matter in an object is called its mass; it is measured in grams and kilograms.

Litre — A unit for measuring capacity; there are 1000 millilitres in one litre.

Millilitre — A small unit for measuring capacity; there are 1000 millilitres in one litre.

Millimetre — A very small unit for measuring length; there are 10 millimetres in one centimetre.

Hours — A unit for measuring time; there are 60 minutes in one hour.

Minute — A unit for measuring time; there are 60 seconds in one minute.

Second — A small unit for measuring time; there are 60 seconds in one minute.

Week — A unit of time; there are 7 days in one week.

Month — A unit of time; according to the book, one month has 30 days and one year has 12 months.

Year — A big unit of time; according to the book, one year has 365 days and one year has 12 months.

Lunar Calendar — A calendar based on the cycle of the moon is called a lunar calendar; the Islamic calendar is lunar.

Solar Calendar — A calendar based on the cycle of the sun is called a solar calendar; its one year has 365 days.

Paisa — A small unit of money; there are 100 paisas in one rupee.

Rupee — The unit of money used in Pakistan; there are 100 paisas in one rupee.

Geometry words

Point — A point shows an exact position; it has neither length nor width.

Line — A straight path which goes on endlessly in both directions is called a line; it has no endpoint.

Line Segment — The part of a line which has two fixed endpoints is called a line segment; its length can be measured.

Ray — The part of a line which has one fixed endpoint and goes on endlessly in one direction is called a ray.

Angle — Two rays starting from a common endpoint (vertex) form an angle.

Vertex — The common endpoint of the two arms of an angle is the vertex; the corner point of a figure is also called a vertex.

Acute Angle — An angle which is smaller than a right angle (90 degrees) is called an acute angle.

Right Angle — An angle which is exactly 90 degrees is called a right angle.

Obtuse Angle — An angle which is greater than a right angle (90 degrees) but smaller than a straight angle (180 degrees) is called an obtuse angle.

Protractor — The half-round instrument used for measuring and drawing angles is called a protractor.

Triangle — A closed figure which has three sides and three angles is called a triangle.

Acute Angled Triangle — A triangle whose all three angles are acute (smaller than 90 degrees) is called an acute angled triangle.

Obtuse Angled Triangle — A triangle which has one obtuse angle (more than 90 degrees) is called an obtuse angled triangle.

Right Triangle — A triangle which has one right angle (90 degrees) is called a right triangle.

Scalene Triangle — A triangle whose all three sides are of different lengths is called a scalene triangle.

Quadrilateral — A closed figure which has four sides is called a quadrilateral; square and rectangle are quadrilaterals.

Rectangle — A quadrilateral whose opposite sides are equal and all four angles are right angles is called a rectangle.

Square — A quadrilateral whose all four sides are equal and all four angles are right angles is called a square.

Circle — A closed curved figure whose all points are at an equal distance from a middle point (centre) is called a circle.

Arc — Any part of the circumference of a circle is called an arc.

Radius — The distance from the centre of a circle to its circumference is the radius; it is half of the diameter.

Diameter — The longest chord passing through the centre of a circle is called the diameter; it is twice the radius.

Edge — In a solid shape, the line segment where two faces meet is called an edge.

Ruler — The instrument used for measuring lengths and drawing straight lines is called a ruler (scale).

Graph words

Graph — A diagram which shows information with bars, lines or pictures is called a graph.

Key points

  • In a fraction, the numerator is above the line and the denominator is below the line.
  • A proper fraction has a smaller numerator, an improper fraction has a numerator greater than or equal to its denominator, and a unit fraction has numerator one.
  • An acute angle is smaller than 90 degrees, a right angle is exactly 90 degrees, and an obtuse angle is greater than 90 degrees but smaller than 180 degrees.
  • The diameter of a circle is twice the radius, and the radius is half of the diameter.
  • There are 100 centimetres in one metre, 1000 grams in one kilogram, and 1000 millilitres in one litre.
  • Changing the order in addition or multiplication does not change the sum or the product; changing the grouping also does not change the result.

mcqs.q: What is the number below the line in a fraction called?
mcqs.why: The book says that in a fraction, the number below the line is the denominator, and it tells into how many equal parts the whole is divided.

mcqs.q: What is the number above the line in a fraction called?
mcqs.why: The book says that in a fraction, the number above the line is the numerator, and it tells how many parts are taken.

mcqs.q: A fraction whose numerator is smaller than its denominator is called a what?
mcqs.why: The book defines a proper fraction as a fraction whose numerator is smaller than its denominator.

mcqs.q: What is an acute angle?
options: An angle which is smaller than a right angle (90 degrees)
An angle which is exactly 90 degrees
An angle which is greater than 180 degrees
A closed figure with four sides
mcqs.why: The book says an angle which is smaller than a right angle (90 degrees) is called an acute angle.

mcqs.q: The amount that a container can hold is called its what?
mcqs.why: The book says the amount that a container can hold is called its capacity, and it is measured in litres and millilitres.

mcqs.q: What is the diameter of a circle?
options: Any part of the circumference of a circle
The distance from the centre to the circumference
The longest chord passing through the centre of a circle
A straight path with no endpoint
mcqs.why: The book says the longest chord passing through the centre of a circle is called the diameter, and it is twice the radius.

mcqs.q: In division, the number by which we divide is called the what?
mcqs.why: The book says that in division, the number by which we divide is called the divisor, while the number being divided is the dividend.

mcqs.q: A diagram which shows information with bars, lines or pictures is called a what?
mcqs.why: The book defines a graph as a diagram which shows information with bars, lines or pictures.

mcqs.q: What is a composite number?
options: A number with exactly two factors
A number which has more than two factors
A number exactly divisible by two
A number made of a whole number and a fraction
mcqs.why: The book says a number which has more than two factors is called a composite number, for example 4, 6 and 8.

mcqs.q: Fractions which have the same denominator are called what?
mcqs.why: The book says fractions which have the same denominator are called like fractions, while different denominators make unlike fractions.
